entries.moduleTitle: Role of a Pega Business Architect
entries.version: Academy Role v2 / Stakeholder interactions v3; Workspace supplement Pega Platform '26
entries.title: Pega Business Architect (BA)
entries.text: The liaison who bridges the client organization and the Pega delivery team, understanding business needs and Pega capabilities to produce software that exceeds what either side could build alone.

entries.moduleTitle: Role of a Pega Business Architect
entries.version: Academy Role v2 / Stakeholder interactions v3; Workspace supplement Pega Platform '26
entries.title: Member of BOTH teams
entries.text: On a Pega project, the BA belongs to both the Business team (process and organizational needs) and the IT team (software development and Pega capabilities), bridging the two groups.

entries.moduleTitle: Role of a Pega Business Architect
entries.version: Academy Role v2 / Stakeholder interactions v3; Workspace supplement Pega Platform '26
entries.title: Client vs. Customer (terminology)
entries.text: Two distinct stakeholder roles in Pega implementations: CLIENT ('organization') — the BUSINESS transforming its workflows with Pega · CUSTOMER — that business's END CUSTOMER (the person using the final application)

entries.moduleTitle: Role of a Pega Business Architect

entries.moduleTitle: Role of a Pega Business Architect
entries.version: Academy Role v2 / Stakeholder interactions v3; Workspace supplement Pega Platform '26
entries.title: Analysis
entries.text: Gather a complete picture of problems before configuring a solution: Understand critical stages · Identify bottlenecks and workarounds · Diagnose root causes · Find functionality common across processes

entries.moduleTitle: Role of a Pega Business Architect
entries.version: Academy Role v2 / Stakeholder interactions v3; Workspace supplement Pega Platform '26
entries.title: Process Design
entries.text: Optimize the workflow using Pega GenAI Blueprint: Remove unnecessary steps · Re-sequence stages · Automate repetitive activities · Intelligently allocate work · Improve collaboration with team members and customers · Consolidate data for users

entries.moduleTitle: Role of a Pega Business Architect
entries.version: Academy Role v2 / Stakeholder interactions v3; Workspace supplement Pega Platform '26
entries.title: Alignment
entries.text: Collaborate with Business and IT to design, build, and test the solution using Blueprint and App Studio, ensuring both sides understand requirements and the proposed workflow improvements.

entries.moduleTitle: Role of a Pega Business Architect
entries.version: Academy Role v2 / Stakeholder interactions v3; Workspace supplement Pega Platform '26
entries.title: Education
entries.text: Continuously teach Business stakeholders the value of Pega's out-of-the-box features, helping them focus on outcomes rather than current methods and become advocates for the new process.

entries.moduleTitle: Role of a Pega Business Architect
entries.version: Academy Role v2 / Stakeholder interactions v3; Workspace supplement Pega Platform '26

entries.version: Academy Role v2 / Stakeholder interactions v3; Workspace supplement Pega Platform '26
entries.title: Facilitating requirement-gathering meetings
entries.text: Organize and facilitate focused meetings with stakeholders and SMEs to gather and document business processes and requirements, guiding stakeholder understanding by translating how OOTB Pega features meet business requirements.

entries.moduleTitle: Role of a Pega Business Architect
entries.version: Academy Role v2 / Stakeholder interactions v3; Workspace supplement Pega Platform '26
entries.title: Documenting requirements as user stories
entries.text: Document business requirements as user stories using Blueprint, App Studio's Agile workbench, and other Scrum tools. Pega developers (System Architects) use those user stories to configure the application to make the best use of Pega's strengths.

entries.moduleTitle: Role of a Pega Business Architect
entries.version: Academy Role v2 / Stakeholder interactions v3; Workspace supplement Pega Platform '26
entries.title: Demonstrating OOTB functionality
entries.text: Use Blueprint to quickly redesign a workflow based on OOTB features and case-management best practices (building stakeholder alignment), and use App Studio to demonstrate how additional Pega features address requirements.

entries.moduleTitle: Role of a Pega Business Architect
entries.version: Academy Role v2 / Stakeholder interactions v3; Workspace supplement Pega Platform '26
entries.title: Promoting Pega best practices
entries.text: Across the project landscape — organizational structure, user-story and backlog creation, governance, and testing — the BA follows and instructs on Pega's proven best practices throughout design and delivery.

entries.title: Product Owner (PO)
entries.text: A client Business-team representative primarily responsible for managing project SCOPE and PRIORITIZING requirements throughout development. The BA runs user-story review meetings with the PO to finalize acceptance criteria and prioritize the backlog so desired features land in the timeline.

entries.moduleTitle: Role of a Pega Business Architect
entries.version: Academy Role v2 / Stakeholder interactions v3; Workspace supplement Pega Platform '26
entries.title: Project Delivery Lead (PDL)
entries.text: The project manager who leads the Pega delivery team, maintains governance, and liaises with client leadership on timeline, budget, and scope — the BA works with the PDL on governance decisions.

entries.moduleTitle: Role of a Pega Business Architect
entries.version: Academy Role v2 / Stakeholder interactions v3; Workspace supplement Pega Platform '26
entries.title: Scrum Master
entries.text: Promotes and supports Scrum; organizes the team, facilitates ceremonies (Sprint Planning, Sizing, Backlog Refinement, Retrospective), and is accountable for team success and removing blockers.

entries.moduleTitle: Role of a Pega Business Architect
entries.version: Academy Role v2 / Stakeholder interactions v3; Workspace supplement Pega Platform '26
entries.title: System Architects (SA / SSA / LSA)
entries.text: System Architects configure the application. In the reviewed stakeholder-delivery model, LSAs take responsibility for Blueprint import and technical delivery; the BA helps business stakeholders understand the implementation.

entries.moduleTitle: Role of a Pega Business Architect
entries.version: Academy Role v2 / Stakeholder interactions v3; Workspace supplement Pega Platform '26
entries.title: Quality Analysts (QAs)
entries.text: Ensure functionality meets documented requirements. QAs build test scripts from user stories, participate in sizing, and flag defects. The BA helps decide if a flagged item is a defect or a new requirement.

entries.moduleTitle: Role of a Pega Business Architect
entries.version: Academy Role v2 / Stakeholder interactions v3; Workspace supplement Pega Platform '26
entries.title: Subject Matter Experts (SMEs)
entries.text: Client representatives with first-hand knowledge of the business process steps. BAs collaborate with SMEs in an operational walkthrough to observe the as-is process and capture all work, in and out of the system.

entries.moduleTitle: Role of a Pega Business Architect
entries.version: Academy Role v2 / Stakeholder interactions v3; Workspace supplement Pega Platform '26
entries.title: Business Analysts
entries.text: Client representatives primarily responsible for documenting the current 'as-is' process, data requirements, and business requirements. The BA reviews this documentation to identify redundancies and bottlenecks, recommend automations, determine resource needs, and define data/interface details.

entries.moduleTitle: Role of a Pega Business Architect
entries.version: Academy Role v2 / Stakeholder interactions v3; Workspace supplement Pega Platform '26
entries.title: UX Designers
entries.text: Ensure the design meets end-user needs, complies with accessibility standards, and delivers a consistent experience across all delivery Channels. The BA collaborates to align the UI with UX requirements, maximize OOTB features, and meet business objectives.

entries.title: Solutions Consultant
entries.text: Works with the client during the initial sales phase, often designing the Blueprint with stakeholders, then transitions the Blueprint to the delivery BAs and System Architects before the project starts.

entries.title: Workspace
entries.text: Each Workspace belongs to one developer operator and one application. An operator has a default Workspace and can create multiple Workspaces within the same application. Changes remain private until shared to a Branch, reducing the risk of conflicts.

entries.version: Academy Role v2 / Stakeholder interactions v3; Workspace supplement Pega Platform '26
entries.title: Branch
entries.text: A Branch contains Rulesets with changes under development. A Branch per feature is a common strategy, not a mandatory platform rule. Teams review changes and resolve conflicts before making them broadly available.

entries.title: Blueprint import → Branch (except Access Roles)

entries.title: Analytical & problem-solving skills

entries.title: Process design knowledge

entries.title: Systems design, Pega technology & Blueprint knowledge
entries.text: Understand Pega's architecture, out-of-the-box features, and Blueprint so business requirements and end-user needs can be mapped to the right Pega capabilities and solutions.

entries.title: Active listening, communication & facilitation
entries.text: Create a common language and shared understanding of both the business need and Pega's capabilities across the project team and stakeholders.

entries.moduleTitle: Role of a Pega Business Architect
entries.version: Academy Role v2 / Stakeholder interactions v3; Workspace supplement Pega Platform '26
entries.title: Knowledge of business change
entries.text: Help the Business team embrace the new Pega solution and become advocates for it within their organization.

entries.title: Low-code defined
entries.text: Low-code application development · Studios · App Studio · Dev Studio · Integrating with external applications

entries.title: Low-code development
entries.text: Low-code tools turn visual configuration into executable behavior. Business contributors and developers share a model; developers can still extend advanced behavior. The source’s historical slogan is not a guarantee that every requirement is automatically implemented.

entries.title: Value of low-code
entries.text: Low-code bridges business stakeholders and skilled developers with a common visual language, enabling teams to deliver faster, collaborate better, and focus on business logic rather than code.

entries.title: Omnichannel reach
entries.text: The same Pega application can serve as a web page, mobile app, or chatbot; data can arrive via email or a robot. Organizations unify all channels without maintaining disparate code lines.

entries.title: Low-code AND professional developers
entries.text: Visual, end-to-end tools make everyone more productive. Citizen developers create application code; experienced developers extend robust applications more rapidly, hide implementation, and build patterns once to reuse many times across the ecosystem.

entries.title: App Studio
entries.text: A low-code authoring space providing CORE features: Case design, data management, and user experience (UI). Users: citizen developers plus technical staff — application developers, front-end developers, data engineers, business analysts, and System Architects. The place to get applications operating quickly.

entries.title: Dev Studio
entries.text: A low-code authoring space with ADVANCED features. Technical users: full-stack developers, System Architects, and database/security administrators. Used for complex Rule configuration, security/access control, reuse management, and performance.

entries.title: Prediction Studio
entries.text: An ANALYTICS space for data scientists and business decision-makers, providing features to build machine-learning models for adaptive, predictive, and text analytics. Access requires pxPredictionStudio among the Portals on the user's access group.

entries.title: Admin Studio
entries.text: A software ADMINISTRATION space managed by IT for system administration — runtime information and configuration options for monitoring and debugging system resources.

entries.title: Three areas of every studio
entries.text: Every studio has three regions: A Header (menus and the upper-left studio-switcher) · A Navigation pane (explorers like Case Type and Data) · An Authoring space where you configure behavior

entries.title: Support for agile development
entries.text: App Studio supports agile best practices and REAL-TIME UI design while processing work. A team testing an online-shopping UI can add fields and change controls (e.g., drop-downs) live — ideal for stakeholder reviews where feedback is implemented in real time.

entries.title: Application profile
entries.text: Captures and presents user stories, bugs, and feedback items to support agile best practices and collaboration across technical and business members. Provides traceability from objectives to development tasks to implementation.

entries.title: Rules
entries.text: Instructions that govern application behavior (like the rules of chess govern the pieces). As you build visually, Pega auto-generates Rules in the background using the SAME names you choose — which is why business-friendly names matter.

entries.title: Layers & Rulesets
entries.text: Layers support application reuse and have built-on dependencies, except the base Pega Platform layer. Rulesets group identifiable Rules for reuse; the two concepts are related rather than synonyms.

entries.title: Application Layers Widget & OOTB architectures
entries.text: The App Studio overview's Application Layers Widget visualizes your Rulesets and identifies the application type. Two OOTB architectures: Constellation architecture (Constellation Ruleset, new View-based UI) and Traditional UI architecture (Theme Cosmos Ruleset, Section-based UI).

entries.title: Dev Studio: Co-development, Reuse, and Naming
Domain vs. Implementation experts
entries.text: Two groups defined by Pega for co-development: DOMAIN experts (Business Analysts, Citizen Developers, front-end developers) — provide process/user insight; primarily work in App Studio · IMPLEMENTATION experts handle complex configuration in Dev Studio when needed, and use App Studio for supported application work.

entries.title: Co-development
entries.text: Business and IT work together: a Business Analyst designs Views in App Studio while a System Architect adds advanced logic in Dev Studio, combining domain insight with implementation expertise.

entries.title: Promote reuse by extending Rule scope
entries.text: In Dev Studio, developers access all layers and extend a rule's scope from one Case Type to an application, division, or whole organization, creating a reusable library that cuts future development time.

entries.title: Advanced SLA options in Dev Studio
entries.text: Beyond App Studio's basic goal/deadline, Dev Studio exposes: Initialization behavior (custom initial urgency, delayed timer start) · Variable interval length (programmatic durations per Case) · Account-for-business-days (exclude holidays/weekends) · Additional escalation actions (reassign a task or resolve a Case)

entries.title: Integration connectors
entries.text: Pega supports many integration standards and protocols so you focus on business requirements. A standard API connector exchanges data in real time when both systems support a common protocol.

entries.title: Robotic Process Automation (RPA)
entries.text: Used when no other integration is feasible — typically legacy systems with no usable API. A robot interacts with the system's UI to perform the same steps a person would, but far faster.

entries.title: Attended RPA
entries.text: Automation that works ALONGSIDE a human in the process, in real time. Example: a CSR triggers a robot mid-call to update an address by driving the legacy system's UI while the customer waits.

entries.title: Unattended RPA
entries.text: The request is placed in a QUEUE for later background processing. Advantages: optimizes system resources, reduces peak loads, and lets the CSR keep serving the customer instead of waiting for the update to finish.

entries.title: Pega Robot Manager
entries.text: A control-tower application that lets you monitor and schedule RPA robots and provides performance analytics for all robots.

entries.title: Pega Center-out architecture
entries.text: Pega's Center-out business architecture · Accessibility in Center-out Development

entries.title: Top-down approach
entries.text: Designs applications around the PRESENTATION layer's delivery Channels (web, mobile, digital messaging, voice-AI). Its most significant disadvantage: the same business logic must be implemented MULTIPLE TIMES to deliver a consistent experience across the different Channels.

entries.title: Bottom-up approach
entries.text: Designs applications around the DATA access layer first. The risk: each system maintains its own data view, creating integration complexity and inconsistency across channels.

entries.title: Center-out business architecture
entries.text: Puts BUSINESS LOGIC at the center of application design. Customer-facing channels and back-end data sources connect to this central layer, so logic is defined once and shared across all touchpoints.

entries.title: Presentation layer (connects UP)
entries.text: The business logic is connected up into the presentation layer so delivery Channels dynamically RESPOND to changes in the central business logic — no recoding per channel.

entries.title: Application & business logic layer (the hub)
entries.text: The central hub containing all the business logic needed to achieve the desired strategic outcome for the organization.

entries.title: Data access layer (connects DOWN)
entries.text: Connections down to data are insulated from the business logic, so changes in systems of record — for example, moving from on-premise to Cloud storage — do NOT require changes in the application's business logic.

entries.title: 1. Manage intelligence centrally
entries.text: Center-out principle 1 — start with the business logic: Business outcomes guided by real-time customer information · Rules consistently enforced across all channels · Everyone uses the SAME intelligence (single source of truth)

entries.title: 2. Focus on outcomes, align your process
entries.text: Use Case Management to organize and automate work through Case Lifecycles that deliver specific business outcomes.

entries.title: 3. Connect experiences up to your Channels
entries.text: Provide a consistent user experience by keeping front-end and back-end logic coordinated; changes are reflected dynamically without recoding.

entries.title: 4. Connect down to your data, keep logic nimble
entries.text: Access data without adding complexity — quickly and easily define the data needed and access it in running applications without worrying about how or where the data is stored or accessed.

entries.title: 5. Manage variations to be scale-ready
entries.text: Start small and fast, then scale big and broad and stay future-proof by adapting to different customer types, lines of business, and geographies using Pega's SITUATIONAL LAYER CAKE.

entries.title: Efficiency
entries.text: Developers define business rules ONCE in a central location, eliminating duplication and reducing inconsistencies across channels and applications.

entries.title: Agility
entries.text: When business requirements change, you update the CENTRAL logic and the system applies those changes across all channel interfaces — making applications more responsive to evolving needs.

entries.title: Governance
entries.text: Centralized business rules simplify auditing, monitoring, and policy enforcement consistently across all interfaces and channels from one authoritative location.

entries.title: Scalability
entries.text: As the organization adds new channel interfaces or customer touchpoints, you REUSE existing business logic to maintain consistency.

entries.title: Model-driven UI
entries.text: An approach in which the underlying data models and business rules GENERATE the user interface. In Center-out, these models reside at the core and the system dynamically generates the UI from them.

entries.title: Patterns
entries.text: Reusable UI templates for model-driven rendering. After defining the Data Model and business rules, authors select and configure patterns; rendering is not a replacement for those design decisions.

entries.title: Separation of logic and presentation
entries.text: A key advantage of patterns: when business rules change, the UI ADAPTS AUTOMATICALLY without manual updates. Pattern-based UIs also support responsive design across devices and channels.

entries.title: Centralized accessibility
entries.text: Shared UI patterns can distribute accessibility improvements across the experiences that use them, reducing repeated implementation work. Custom content, configuration, integrations, and user interactions still need application-specific evaluation.

entries.title: Standards supported
entries.text: The referenced curriculum describes support for WCAG 2.1 and Section 508 through core components. Support for a standard is not proof that a particular application conforms; assess the applicable requirements and the actual experience.

entries.title: Evolving standards
entries.text: Update shared components to distribute relevant fixes to consuming applications. Confirm that each application adopts the changes, then evaluate its content and interactions against the applicable requirements.

entries.title: Constellation accessibility features
entries.text: Built-in features include page landmarks, headings, skip-to-main navigation, keyboard access, semantic roles, associated field labels and accessible validation messages. Theme configuration warns about color combinations that fail contrast requirements. Inspect custom content too.

entries.title: Accessible content and evaluation
entries.text: Use meaningful labels and links, concise helper text and specific errors. Avoid guidance based only on color or position; prefer labels and helper text to unnecessary placeholders. Run manual and automated checks. Accessibility Inspector is not supported for Constellation applications.

entries.title: Modular architecture and enterprise reuse
entries.text: Modular reuse architecture · Studio interoperability and the Reuse Library

entries.title: Modular enterprise reuse
entries.text: A software development approach that uses standardized, reusable components to build applications. Instead of starting from scratch, developers ASSEMBLE pre-built, tested modules to speed up development and maintain consistency across the enterprise.

entries.title: Benefits across the lifecycle
entries.text: Reusing shared modules helps at every project phase: Design: reduces planning time with ready-made components · Development: speeds builds and minimizes coding · Testing: limits defects/scope via pre-tested modules · Deployment: simplifies implementation with standardized components · Maintenance: a shared implementation can deliver fixes to applications that consume the updated asset; adoption and overrides still need review.

entries.title: The Five Guiding Principles of Reuse
Interoperable
entries.text: Use consistent building blocks across applications AND authoring environments (App Studio and Dev Studio).

entries.title: Updateable
entries.text: Design components so they can evolve independently, reducing disruption to consuming applications. This is a design goal, not a guarantee that every update is compatible or needs no regression testing.

entries.title: Configurable
entries.text: Behavior can be adjusted through configuration settings without rewriting the underlying business logic, enabling business-led customization.

entries.title: Modular
entries.text: Applications are assembled from encapsulated, self-contained components rather than built as large monolithic layers that are difficult to maintain or update.

entries.title: Governed
entries.text: Establish governance (for example, a Pega Center of Excellence) to manage, evolve, and ensure the quality of reusable assets.

entries.title: Situational Layer Cake
entries.text: A patented Pega architecture that balances two competing forces: REUSE (economies of scale and consistency) and VARIATION (different products, regions, regulatory needs). It avoids both 'spaghetti' single-app if-then-else and the sprawl of 50–100 near-identical apps.

entries.title: Enterprise Layer
entries.text: Core Pega Platform features and enterprise-wide reusable assets (e.g., a company-wide authentication module used across all applications).

entries.title: Division Layer
entries.text: Reusable components specific to a division (e.g., a claims-processing flow tailored for the insurance division but reused across its applications).

entries.title: Application Layer
entries.text: Application-specific implementations that leverage lower-layer assets (e.g., a customer-service app that uses shared authentication and claims components but adds its own workflows).

entries.title: Implementation Layer
entries.text: Customizations for specific deployment scenarios WITHOUT altering the base application (e.g., localizing the customer-service app for a region by adjusting language and regulatory rules).

entries.title: App Studio role
entries.text: A simplified, collaborative, inclusive authoring experience that lets a wide range of low-code practitioners understand, interpret, and author processes/applications. It hides complexity and raises Case Type literacy so stakeholders express requirements and feedback better.

entries.title: Dev Studio role
entries.text: Robust low-code environment for experienced architects to configure integrations, complex decisions, security, and advanced features beyond App Studio's scope.

entries.title: Relevant records
entries.text: Relevant records control design-time prompting and filtering for applicable Case Types, data types and condition builders. Mark supported Dev Studio rules as relevant so App Studio authors can discover and reuse them; this marker does not grant permissions or make every rule appear in every context.

entries.title: Auto-marked in App Studio
entries.text: When you create Fields, Views, Processes, and user actions in App Studio, Pega automatically marks them as relevant records.

entries.title: Reuse Library
entries.text: The Reuse Library in App Studio helps authors discover, manage and reuse supported assets available to their application. Platform '25 groups them into Case Types, data objects and Business Logic. Relevant records expose supported Case Types and Business Logic Rules; not every relevant rule has a library tile. For example, an SLA can be relevant without appearing in the library.

entries.title: Rules and Rule Types

entries.version: Pega Platform '24.2 / '25 Academy module; Rulesets topic includes '26 naming supplement
entries.title: Rule
entries.text: The basic building block of a Pega application. Each Rule is an instance of a Rule Type (e.g., a Flow Rule models a Process). Rules define application behavior without custom coding.

entries.version: Pega Platform '24.2 / '25 Academy module; Rulesets topic includes '26 naming supplement
entries.title: Rule Type
entries.text: A template for creating a Rule that models a specific behavior — for example, a Flow Rule models a Process, while other Rule Types model UI, automated Decisions, and more.

entries.version: Pega Platform '24.2 / '25 Academy module; Rulesets topic includes '26 naming supplement
entries.title: Automated Rule creation in App Studio
entries.text: App Studio auto-creates Rules as you design: Adding a Process creates its underlying Flow Rule. · Case design and UI configuration generate/manage underlying task and presentation Rules; the exact record types depend on the UI architecture. · The cited rule-creation topic shows a Section example; do not apply Section/Harness assumptions universally to Constellation.

entries.version: Pega Platform '24.2 / '25 Academy module; Rulesets topic includes '26 naming supplement
entries.title: Application Modularity with Rules

entries.version: Pega Platform '24.2 / '25 Academy module; Rulesets topic includes '26 naming supplement
entries.title: Versioning
entries.text: Creating a new version of a Rule whenever Case behavior must change. Pega keeps a full change history, enabling rollback of a specific Rule without affecting others.

entries.version: Pega Platform '24.2 / '25 Academy module; Rulesets topic includes '26 naming supplement
entries.title: Delegation
entries.text: Exposing a specific Rule to business users so they can update Case behavior as conditions change, without filing an IT change request or touching other rules.

entries.version: Pega Platform '24.2 / '25 Academy module; Rulesets topic includes '26 naming supplement
entries.title: Reuse
entries.text: Developers reuse Rules whenever an application needs existing behavior, instead of reconfiguring it every time (e.g., reuse one policyholder-info UI form across auto, property, and marine claims).

entries.version: Pega Platform '24.2 / '25 Academy module; Rulesets topic includes '26 naming supplement
entries.title: Parametrization
entries.text: To increase reusability, use parameters to drive a Rule's logic based on a passed value instead of hard-coded data — reducing code duplication and the time to implement Rule specializations.

entries.version: Pega Platform '24.2 / '25 Academy module; Rulesets topic includes '26 naming supplement
entries.title: Rulesets and Versioning

entries.version: Pega Platform '24.2 / '25 Academy module; Rulesets topic includes '26 naming supplement
entries.title: Ruleset
entries.text: A group that identifies, stores, and manages the Rules defining an application or a significant portion of it. Rulesets enable versioning, access control, and portability.

entries.version: Pega Platform '24.2 / '25 Academy module; Rulesets topic includes '26 naming supplement
entries.title: Ruleset version
entries.text: An instance of a Ruleset collecting individual Rules. To update contents you create a NEW version (unlocked), add/change Rules, then lock it when complete.

entries.version: Pega Platform '24.2 / '25 Academy module; Rulesets topic includes '26 naming supplement
entries.title: Ruleset stack
entries.text: The ordered Ruleset sequence used when selecting applicable Rules. Stack order is one input to resolution alongside class context and other eligibility criteria; it is not a guarantee that the first same-named record always wins.

entries.version: Pega Platform '24.2 / '25 Academy module; Rulesets topic includes '26 naming supplement
entries.title: Rule Creation

entries.version: Pega Platform '24.2 / '25 Academy module; Rulesets topic includes '26 naming supplement
entries.title: Two paths to a Rule
entries.text: In App Studio, Rules are created FOR you as you build the Case Life Cycle, Views, and data. In Dev Studio, you can directly create and manage how a Rule is created and reused to maintain Rule integrity and reusability.

entries.version: Pega Platform '24.2 / '25 Academy module; Rulesets topic includes '26 naming supplement
entries.title: Specialization by copy (Save As)
entries.text: Save As can create a context-specific variant while preserving the original. Change at least one of identifier, class or Ruleset; leaving all three unchanged is rejected. Inspect the target context before creating the copy.

entries.version: Pega Platform '24.2 / '25 Academy module; Rulesets topic includes '26 naming supplement
entries.title: Classes and Class Hierarchy

entries.version: Pega Platform '24.2 / '25 Academy module; Rulesets topic includes '26 naming supplement
entries.title: Class
entries.text: A grouping of Rules according to their capacity for reuse: Work class (process Cases) · Integration class (connect to systems) · Data class (describe data types)

entries.version: Pega Platform '24.2 / '25 Academy module; Rulesets topic includes '26 naming supplement
entries.title: Parent and child classes
entries.text: A class can contain other classes. A parent class contains another class; a child class is contained by another. A child class can reuse/inherit any Rules defined for its parent class.

entries.version: Pega Platform '24.2 / '25 Academy module; Rulesets topic includes '26 naming supplement
entries.title: Class hierarchy
entries.text: The introductory inheritance search starts in the specific class and expands toward general classes. This describes class reuse, not the entire Rule resolution algorithm or a guarantee that every ancestor Rule is eligible.

entries.version: Pega Platform '24.2 / '25 Academy module; Rulesets topic includes '26 naming supplement
entries.title: Rule Reuse Through Inheritance

entries.version: Pega Platform '24.2 / '25 Academy module; Rulesets topic includes '26 naming supplement
entries.title: Pattern inheritance
entries.text: Pattern inheritance uses class-name prefixes to search the naming hierarchy. The Academy topic describes this as automatic; inspect the class configuration rather than assuming all Rule selection is determined solely by its name.

entries.version: Pega Platform '24.2 / '25 Academy module; Rulesets topic includes '26 naming supplement
entries.title: Directed inheritance
entries.text: Inheritance where the parent class is EXPLICITLY specified on the class form. It lets an application class inherit from standard Pega classes outside the naming hierarchy.

entries.version: Pega Platform '24.2 / '25 Academy module; Rulesets topic includes '26 naming supplement
entries.title: Resolution order & @baseclass
entries.text: Pega alternates pattern and directed searches up the class hierarchy. If no Rule is found by @baseclass, Pega returns a Rule-not-found error.

entries.version: Academy module v4; procedural topics v2; historical Infinity '23/'24 notes
entries.title: Pega GenAI in Pega Platform
entries.text: Generative AI in Pega · Generating a Case Type using Pega GenAI Autopilot · Generating Case Data using Pega GenAI Autopilot · Generating Personas using Pega GenAI Autopilot

entries.version: Academy module v4; procedural topics v2; historical Infinity '23/'24 notes
entries.title: Generative AI — Design-Time Tools

entries.version: Academy module v4; procedural topics v2; historical Infinity '23/'24 notes
entries.title: Pega GenAI
entries.text: A suite of generative AI-powered features integrated across Pega Platform, available beginning with Pega Infinity '23. It helps developers, learners, and users build applications, enhance learning, improve operational efficiency, and stay aligned with best practices.

entries.version: Academy module v4; procedural topics v2; historical Infinity '23/'24 notes
entries.title: Pega Blueprint
entries.text: Blueprint is a separate SaaS application-design tool. A business description leads to proposals for workflow, data and Personas that the team reviews before implementation. A proposal is not proof of production readiness or a guaranteed delivery time.

entries.version: Academy module v4; procedural topics v2; historical Infinity '23/'24 notes
entries.title: Pega GenAI Autopilot
entries.text: Autopilot assists application authors with suggestions for workflow, data and Personas. The reviewed curriculum describes it as a design-time accelerator; speed improvements depend on the actual work and are not a measured guarantee for every project.

entries.version: Academy module v4; procedural topics v2; historical Infinity '23/'24 notes
entries.title: Pega GenAI Connect
entries.text: Lets you develop custom Pega GenAI-powered capabilities using the Pega GenAI gateway; an add-on compatible with Pega Platform, Customer Service, or Sales Automation.

entries.version: Academy module v4; procedural topics v2; historical Infinity '23/'24 notes
entries.title: Pega GenAI Coach
entries.text: Provides expert advice and feedback on END-USER tasks at application RUNTIME — ideal for task-specific guidance relevant to a Pega Case.

entries.version: Academy module v4; procedural topics v2; historical Infinity '23/'24 notes
entries.title: Generative AI — Run-Time Tools and Custom AI

entries.version: Academy module v4; procedural topics v2; historical Infinity '23/'24 notes
entries.title: Pega GenAI Agent and Tool Rules
entries.text: Configured Agents support automated Case actions and runtime conversations. Tool Rules describe available actions and their constraints; permissions, review and configuration are still required.

entries.version: Academy module v4; procedural topics v2; historical Infinity '23/'24 notes
entries.title: Pega GenAI Knowledge Buddy
entries.text: Gives employees, agents, and sellers instant answers and real-time guidance via a conversation interface, combining Pega GenAI with the organization's own procedural documents and knowledge bases.

entries.version: Academy module v4; procedural topics v2; historical Infinity '23/'24 notes
entries.title: Search Assistant & OpenAI search
entries.text: The reviewed topic describes Search Assistant as Community search backed by Knowledge Buddy. Its historical documentation-search example uses a trailing question mark for AI answers; that example does not establish the only supported trigger in every later interface.

entries.version: Academy module v4; procedural topics v2; historical Infinity '23/'24 notes
entries.title: Pega GenAI Autopilot at Design Time

entries.version: Academy module v4; procedural topics v2; historical Infinity '23/'24 notes
entries.title: What Autopilot accelerates
entries.text: Autopilot delivers real-time, context-aware guidance and task prioritization during development. For a loan app, it suggests application components including Case Types, fields in the Data Model, and Personas — and developers can review and modify any recommendation before generating it.

entries.version: Academy module v4; procedural topics v2; historical Infinity '23/'24 notes
entries.title: The Autopilot workflow
entries.text: When you create a Case Type, Autopilot suggests names, a workflow, data objects, and Personas — accelerating design-time setup with AI-generated proposals the architect reviews and accepts.

entries.version: Academy module v4; procedural topics v2; historical Infinity '23/'24 notes
entries.title: Human-in-the-loop responsibility
entries.text: Review generated recommendations against the application requirements before accepting them. AI output can contain mistakes; the topic explicitly calls for review.

entries.version: Academy module v4; procedural topics v2; historical Infinity '23/'24 notes
entries.title: Pega Blueprint (within the GenAI suite)

entries.version: Academy module v4; procedural topics v2; historical Infinity '23/'24 notes
entries.title: Blueprint as a SaaS design tool
entries.text: Blueprint operates independently of a Pega Platform instance and supplements the studios. Do not confuse independence from a Platform instance with unrestricted anonymous access: follow the current Blueprint account, invitation and collaboration requirements.

entries.version: Academy module v4; procedural topics v2; historical Infinity '23/'24 notes
entries.title: What Blueprint proposes
entries.text: From a business-terms description, Blueprint proposes Case Types, Case Life Cycles, Data Models, data objects, and Personas, plus best-practice application templates, enabling quick design edits to fit requirements.

entries.version: Academy module v4; procedural topics v2; historical Infinity '23/'24 notes
entries.title: GenAI Connect Step

entries.version: Academy module v4; procedural topics v2; historical Infinity '23/'24 notes
entries.title: Connect Generative AI automation Step
entries.text: A Step (available since Pega Infinity '24) that calls a configured GenAI Connect Rule from App Studio to send a prompt to an LLM and receive a response in one of three structures.

entries.version: Academy module v4; procedural topics v2; historical Infinity '23/'24 notes
entries.title: Three response structures
entries.text: GenAI response types and their Data Model mapping: Structured-Single: one object mapped to a Data Model field · Structured-List: multiple objects mapped to a page list · Unstructured: raw text mapped to a Text (paragraph) field

entries.version: Academy module v4; procedural topics v2; historical Infinity '23/'24 notes
entries.title: Target field requirement
entries.text: You must identify a target field to write the response into, and add that target field to the application UI so the response can be displayed to the user.

entries.version: Academy module v4; procedural topics v2; historical Infinity '23/'24 notes
entries.title: Pega GenAI Agent and Tool Rules

entries.version: Academy module v4; procedural topics v2; historical Infinity '23/'24 notes
entries.title: Agents
entries.text: Configurable AI assistants that automate Case processing and provide run-time guidance. Governed by Tool Rules, they can run automations, start Cases, call other agents, and converse with users.

entries.version: Academy module v4; procedural topics v2; historical Infinity '23/'24 notes
entries.title: Guardrails via Tool Rules
entries.text: Detailed tool descriptions and constraints help guide agent actions. Runtime conversations can include extraction from uploaded documents. These features support the workflow but do not guarantee correct responses or replace access controls.

entries.version: Academy module v4; procedural topics v2; historical Infinity '23/'24 notes
entries.title: Generate and review a Case Type

entries.version: Academy module v4; procedural topics v2; historical Infinity '23/'24 notes
entries.title: Choose the Case Type
entries.text: In App Studio, start Case Type creation. Autopilot proposes names from the application name and metadata; choose a proposal or enter your own name.

entries.version: Academy module v4; procedural topics v2; historical Infinity '23/'24 notes
entries.title: Review lifecycle and fields
entries.text: Select Use Autopilot to suggest a Life Cycle and Data Model. Review and edit the proposed Stages and Steps, then click Next to review fields. Each field has a Name, Type and technical ID; edit, add or remove fields as needed.

entries.version: Academy module v4; procedural topics v2; historical Infinity '23/'24 notes
entries.title: Create and inspect
entries.text: After reviewing the proposals, Submit creates the Case Type. Inspect Workflow and Data model. Embedded Data and Data reference proposals can also create associated data objects; review those relationships.

entries.version: Academy module v4; procedural topics v2; historical Infinity '23/'24 notes
entries.title: Generate Personas

entries.version: Academy module v4; procedural topics v2; historical Infinity '23/'24 notes
entries.title: Review the proposed users
entries.text: The Persona topic uses Users > User management in App Studio. Autopilot proposes names and descriptions from application metadata. Choose a suggestion or enter a custom Persona name.

entries.version: Academy module v4; procedural topics v2; historical Infinity '23/'24 notes
entries.title: Associate with the workflow
entries.text: After creating the Persona, add it in Personas & Channels in the Case Life Cycle. This models user roles in the workflow; it is not proof that a specific account has all required runtime permissions.

entries.version: Academy module v4; procedural topics v2; historical Infinity '23/'24 notes
entries.title: Generate sample records and fill forms

entries.version: Academy module v4; procedural topics v2; historical Infinity '23/'24 notes
entries.title: Sample data-object records
entries.text: Select a data object and its Records tab, then Generate sample records with Autopilot. Review the requested record count and the generated field values. These samples can support testing before an external source integration exists.

entries.version: Academy module v4; procedural topics v2; historical Infinity '23/'24 notes
entries.title: Form data affects the Case
entries.text: While testing a Case, Fill form with AI populates the form fields. Those values become part of the Case data used by the application. Inspect them before continuing; filling a form is different from generating data-object records.

entries.moduleTitle: Accelerating application building with Pega Blueprint
entries.title: Pega Blueprint Overview

entries.moduleTitle: Accelerating application building with Pega Blueprint
entries.title: Pega Blueprint
entries.text: Blueprint combines templates and generative AI to propose application workflows. Stakeholders review and refine the proposed design before implementation.

entries.moduleTitle: Accelerating application building with Pega Blueprint
entries.title: Standalone SaaS tool
entries.text: Blueprint is SaaS, separate from a Pega Platform development instance and Operator login. Follow the SaaS service’s sign-in and collaboration access requirements.

entries.moduleTitle: Accelerating application building with Pega Blueprint
entries.title: Augments, not replaces
entries.text: Blueprint helps teams start design; the implementation team uses App Studio and Dev Studio after import to configure, test and extend the application.

entries.moduleTitle: Accelerating application building with Pega Blueprint
entries.title: Generating a Pega Blueprint

entries.moduleTitle: Accelerating application building with Pega Blueprint
entries.title: Describe in business terms
entries.text: Choose industry, sub-industry and department, or Other with a detailed functional description. Select a template or GenAI, provide organization and language details, and add supporting requirements assets.

entries.moduleTitle: Accelerating application building with Pega Blueprint
entries.title: Generate and modify
entries.text: Review and edit Case Types, Primary/Alternate Stages, Processes and Steps. Use Notes to capture routing, SLA and conditions; Preview my app helps review flow. Check data field types, descriptions, primary fields, single/multiple values and user-input/calculated sources.

entries.moduleTitle: Accelerating application building with Pega Blueprint
entries.title: Best-practice templates
entries.text: Templates provide a starting design that still needs review. Validate Personas, access needs, Channels and release effort, then check the summary for workflow, Data Model and integration completeness.

entries.moduleTitle: Accelerating application building with Pega Blueprint
entries.title: Importing a Pega Blueprint into Pega Platform

entries.moduleTitle: Accelerating application building with Pega Blueprint
entries.title: Export and import
entries.text: Download the technical .blueprint file and a PDF reference. In App Studio, create an application with Build from a Blueprint, upload the technical file and review its details and built-on stack. An existing application must be saved as a template to use it through this New Application wizard.

entries.moduleTitle: Accelerating application building with Pega Blueprint
entries.title: Who imports it
entries.text: The authorized implementation team performs import and configuration. Project responsibilities can assign an LSA; the source does not require an exclusive LSA permission.

entries.moduleTitle: Accelerating application building with Pega Blueprint
entries.title: What import creates (and the exception)
entries.text: In the documented new-application workflow, created assets except Access Roles go into a Branch. The exception concerns branch placement, not whether Access Roles are created. Base Rulesets are locked and merges require the appropriate password.

entries.moduleTitle: Accelerating application building with Pega Blueprint
entries.title: PremBridge not required
entries.text: Pega GenAI PremBridge is NOT required to import Pega Blueprints into a new or existing application.

entries.moduleTitle: Accelerating application building with Pega Blueprint
entries.title: Build, inherit and reuse choices
entries.text: Inheritance creates a new Case Type or data object based on one in the built-on application. Reusing a data object links to the existing built-on object without its own class in the new app. Skip a proposed asset when it does not fit the business design.

entries.moduleTitle: Accelerating application building with Pega Blueprint
entries.title: Validate after import
entries.text: Check existing-app overlaps, merge the appropriate branch Rules, and refine Decision shapes, Flow Actions, locking and the Data Model. Review database mapping, Data Pages and properties, and test approvals, alternate paths, automation and child Cases.

entries.moduleTitle: Accelerating application building with Pega Blueprint
entries.title: Using Blueprint for an Industry App (Customer Service for Insurance)

entries.moduleTitle: Accelerating application building with Pega Blueprint
entries.title: Industry templates
entries.text: In the insurance example, start from the Customer Service template and add a golf-cart Case. Inherit existing Case Types and build the new one. Add a weather Step and field; after import, change the field to Picklist and add it to a View. Configure data, integrations, Channels and users, then simulate an interaction.

entries.version: Pega Platform '24.2; Academy BA Case Life Cycle module v2
entries.title: Case Life Cycle design for Business Architect
entries.text: Pega's Case Life Cycle · Designing a Case Life Cycle · Users, Personas, and Channels · User guidance · Communicating with stakeholders · Benefits of Case Management with Pega

entries.moduleTitle: Case Life Cycle design for Business Architect
entries.version: Pega Platform '24.2; Academy BA Case Life Cycle module v2
entries.title: Microjourney, Case Types, and Cases

entries.moduleTitle: Case Life Cycle design for Business Architect
entries.version: Pega Platform '24.2; Academy BA Case Life Cycle module v2
entries.title: Microjourney
entries.text: The units of work that deliver a meaningful result to customers and users — a part of the overall customer journey. Each Microjourney is captured in App Studio as a Case Type.

entries.moduleTitle: Case Life Cycle design for Business Architect
entries.version: Pega Platform '24.2; Academy BA Case Life Cycle module v2
entries.title: The three pillars of an application
entries.text: Every Microjourney in App Studio is built on three pillars: (1) Case Types and Strategies · (2) Data and Interfaces · (3) Personas and Channels

entries.moduleTitle: Case Life Cycle design for Business Architect
entries.version: Pega Platform '24.2; Academy BA Case Life Cycle module v2
entries.title: Case Type vs. Case
entries.text: Fundamental Pega terminology: CASE TYPE — an ABSTRACT model of a repeatable business transaction (the template) · CASE — a SPECIFIC transaction instance; each submission creates a new Case with a unique ID and its own data and history

entries.moduleTitle: Case Life Cycle design for Business Architect
entries.version: Pega Platform '24.2; Academy BA Case Life Cycle module v2
entries.title: Building Blocks: Stages, Processes, Steps

entries.moduleTitle: Case Life Cycle design for Business Architect
entries.version: Pega Platform '24.2; Academy BA Case Life Cycle module v2
entries.title: Stage
entries.text: The top-level organization of work — a distinct phase or milestone in the Case Life Cycle. Stages organize the process into a sequential, logical collection of activities that drive toward resolution (e.g., an online order's Submission, Processing, Delivery).

entries.moduleTitle: Case Life Cycle design for Business Architect
entries.version: Pega Platform '24.2; Academy BA Case Life Cycle module v2
entries.title: Process
entries.text: A Process groups related Steps within a Stage. Processes normally run sequentially; independently started/completed Processes can instead run in parallel. Completion and transition behavior follows the configured Case Life Cycle.

entries.moduleTitle: Case Life Cycle design for Business Architect
entries.version: Pega Platform '24.2; Academy BA Case Life Cycle module v2
entries.title: Step
entries.text: Either a user action or an automated action within a Process. A Step requiring user action is a Task or Assignment; a Step performed by the system is an Automation Step (e.g., 'Enter customer details').

entries.moduleTitle: Case Life Cycle design for Business Architect
entries.version: Pega Platform '24.2; Academy BA Case Life Cycle module v2
entries.title: Stage Types and Components (Designing)

entries.moduleTitle: Case Life Cycle design for Business Architect
entries.version: Pega Platform '24.2; Academy BA Case Life Cycle module v2
entries.title: Create Stage
entries.text: The FIRST Stage, denoted by a GREEN bar; it holds Processes/Steps to enter initial data on creation. It CANNOT be deleted or repositioned but CAN be renamed. Cases that include the Create Stage are assigned a Case ID upon creation.

entries.moduleTitle: Case Life Cycle design for Business Architect
entries.version: Pega Platform '24.2; Academy BA Case Life Cycle module v2
entries.title: Create Process
entries.text: The default Process in the Create Stage can be modified. Non-Channel-specific Create Processes only include Collect information Steps. Channel-specific Processes can start conditionally for the configured Channel; validate supported Steps for that configuration.

entries.moduleTitle: Case Life Cycle design for Business Architect
entries.version: Pega Platform '24.2; Academy BA Case Life Cycle module v2
entries.title: Primary Stages & primary path
entries.text: Primary Stages lead to an expected outcome (most Cases go through them; they are part of usual processing and required for positive resolution). The path through the Case Life Cycle without deviating from Primary Stages is the PRIMARY PATH.

entries.moduleTitle: Case Life Cycle design for Business Architect
entries.version: Pega Platform '24.2; Academy BA Case Life Cycle module v2
entries.title: Alternate Stage
entries.text: Handles DEVIATIONS from the primary path. Alternate Stages are OPTIONAL and either represent a negative Resolution Stage or are used for exception handling to allow the Case to re-enter the primary path.

entries.moduleTitle: Case Life Cycle design for Business Architect
entries.version: Pega Platform '24.2; Academy BA Case Life Cycle module v2
entries.title: Resolution Stage
entries.text: Denoted by a RED bar; defines Case behavior at the END of the Life Cycle. Every Case Type should have AT LEAST ONE Resolution Stage, and can have more than one if you define alternate paths.

entries.moduleTitle: Case Life Cycle design for Business Architect
entries.version: Pega Platform '24.2; Academy BA Case Life Cycle module v2
entries.title: Stage and Step Transitions

entries.moduleTitle: Case Life Cycle design for Business Architect
entries.version: Pega Platform '24.2; Academy BA Case Life Cycle module v2
entries.title: Stage transitions
entries.text: Configured in the Stage contextual properties pane to control how a Case moves between Stages. You CANNOT configure Stage transitions on the Create Stage.

entries.moduleTitle: Case Life Cycle design for Business Architect
entries.version: Pega Platform '24.2; Academy BA Case Life Cycle module v2
entries.title: Change Stage Automation
entries.text: A Change Stage Automation Step transitions the Case to a specific Stage automatically — most useful for automated transitions to and from Alternate Stages (e.g., return to Verification once rejected IT setup selections are modified).

entries.moduleTitle: Case Life Cycle design for Business Architect
entries.version: Pega Platform '24.2; Academy BA Case Life Cycle module v2
entries.title: Step transitions & Previous button
entries.text: By default at run time, clicking Submit advances the Case to the next Step. Enabling the 'Allow users to go back to the previous Step' option in a Process displays the Previous button at run time.

entries.moduleTitle: Case Life Cycle design for Business Architect
entries.version: Pega Platform '24.2; Academy BA Case Life Cycle module v2
entries.title: Users, Personas, and Channels

entries.moduleTitle: Case Life Cycle design for Business Architect
entries.version: Pega Platform '24.2; Academy BA Case Life Cycle module v2
entries.title: Persona
entries.text: Represents a category of people involved in your processes — the role a user plays and the access they need (e.g., Customer, CSR, Manager). Personas are one of the three pillars and are captured in App Studio.

entries.moduleTitle: Case Life Cycle design for Business Architect
entries.version: Pega Platform '24.2; Academy BA Case Life Cycle module v2
entries.title: Channel
entries.text: The way users interact with a Case — for example a Web portal, mobile, or digital messaging. Personas and Channels together describe who participates and how.

entries.moduleTitle: Case Life Cycle design for Business Architect
entries.version: Pega Platform '24.2; Academy BA Case Life Cycle module v2
entries.title: User Guidance, Communication, and Benefits

entries.moduleTitle: Case Life Cycle design for Business Architect
entries.version: Pega Platform '24.2; Academy BA Case Life Cycle module v2
entries.title: User guidance
entries.text: Assignment instructions explain what users must accomplish and which information to enter. Meaningful Case Status values communicate progress; they can update on Stage or Step entry, with a resolution status after the final Stage’s Processes complete.

entries.moduleTitle: Case Life Cycle design for Business Architect
entries.version: Pega Platform '24.2; Academy BA Case Life Cycle module v2
entries.title: Communicating with stakeholders
entries.text: Pulse supports discussion in Case context. Automated communication must be configured: identify recipients, message content and timing. A Send email Step sends at that point in the flow; Case-level Worklist notifications inform the assigned user when the routed Assignment is entered.

entries.moduleTitle: Case Life Cycle design for Business Architect
entries.version: Pega Platform '24.2; Academy BA Case Life Cycle module v2
entries.title: Case status & benefits
entries.text: Case status communicates where a Case stands in its Life Cycle and supports automated notifications. Case Management with Pega delivers automation, consistency, visibility, and faster, more reliable resolution by modeling work the way users think about it.

entries.title: Building a Data Model
entries.text: Basics of a Data Model · Understanding Data Objects · Fields and Field Types · Application Data Records · Creating data relationships · Accessing data with Data Pages

entries.title: Data Model
entries.text: The visual representation of all data elements and their relationships. It serves as a common language between Business and IT, existing at three levels: Conceptual, Logical, and Physical.

entries.title: Conceptual Data Model
entries.text: A living document built WITH BUSINESS STAKEHOLDERS using Entities, Attributes, and Relationships (cardinality). It describes WHAT data exists, not how it is stored.

entries.title: Logical Data Model
entries.text: The Conceptual model translated and refined for Pega Platform: entities become DATA OBJECTS and attributes become FIELDS. The BA configures the primary elements (data objects, fields, relationships) in App Studio, while System Architects configure advanced requirements in Dev Studio.

entries.title: Physical Data Model
entries.text: Reflects how data is actually stored and accessed — integration settings, local Pega database storage, and external System of Record connectivity. Derived from the Logical model.

entries.title: Data object
entries.text: A structure that groups related fields describing a data entity (e.g., a Customer object with First Name, Last Name, Email). The Pega equivalent of a database table or entity.

entries.title: Data object vs. data type (Dev Studio)
entries.text: The same constructs have different names by studio: APP STUDIO terms: 'Data object' (the entity) and 'field' (an attribute) · DEV STUDIO terms: 'data type' (entity) and 'property' (attribute) — used interchangeably on projects

entries.title: Draft data object
entries.text: A placeholder created when you add a data object from the Case Life Cycle Designer without configuring fields or integration. Must be fully configured before use in production.

entries.title: Field
entries.text: A reusable UI component consisting of a NAME and a FIELD TYPE; each field stores one value associated with a Case. The Field Type determines the format/validation of the data and the input control presented to the user.

entries.title: Choosing the right Field Type
entries.text: Selecting the correct type (rather than Text for everything) enforces a common, valid format across all Case Types, reducing errors and streamlining the workflow.

entries.title: Data Record
entries.text: A unique set of field values for one instance of a data object (e.g., one specific customer). Records are stored locally in Pega or retrieved from external systems.

entries.title: Value change vs. structure change
entries.text: Two types of data model changes with different implications: VALUE change (adding a customer, updating a phone number) — normal business operation; no process change needed · STRUCTURE change (adding/removing fields) — modifies the data object definition; may require schema updates

entries.title: pyGUID
entries.text: Each locally-stored Data Record gets a pyGUID — an automatically-assigned unique identifier. The pyGUID is stored along with the Case so the record can be retrieved later.

entries.title: Data relationship
entries.text: A container that associates a set of related fields but does NOT store data itself. It relates data between a data object and a Case Type, between data objects, and between Case Types.

entries.title: Embedded Data
entries.text: Field type used when data is sourced from user input/action made DIRECTLY inside the Case instance (e.g., credit-card payment info entered each order). The data is stored WITH that specific Case instance and is only retrievable via that Case.

entries.title: Data reference
entries.text: Field type used when data is sourced from Data Records stored locally in the Pega database OR retrieved from an external system of record (e.g., a Customer maintained in an external SOR, or a product catalog).

entries.title: Case reference
entries.text: Field type used when data is sourced from a selected Case Type (e.g., choosing from a list of Service Cases).

entries.title: Data Page
entries.text: The bridge that retrieves data from a source and caches it for use. It decouples the Case from the underlying data source, supporting simulated data and refresh strategies.

entries.title: Pega Live Data
entries.text: The virtualization layer separating the application's business logic and data utilization from the technical details of how/when data is accessed. Data Pages are a key component of Pega Live Data.

entries.title: Three default Data Pages per data object
entries.text: Every data object includes a single-record read-only Data Page, a list read-only Data Page, and a single read-and-write Data Page (2 read-only + 1 read-write).

entries.title: Savable Data Page
entries.text: Saves a page or page list back to its system of record (local or external), enabling real-time updates; governed by a data save plan configured by System Architects in Dev Studio (the BA helps choose the plan).

entries.moduleTitle: Displaying data with App Studio for Business Architects
entries.title: Displaying data with App Studio for Business Architects
entries.text: UI configuration in App Studio · Data capture in Views · Forms in Pega Platform · Adding data through a UI View · Designate Primary Fields

entries.moduleTitle: Displaying data with App Studio for Business Architects
entries.title: UI Configuration in App Studio

entries.moduleTitle: Displaying data with App Studio for Business Architects
entries.title: Separation of Concerns
entries.text: The software design principle the Pega UI layer applies: Divide the application into distinct parts · Each with a single responsibility · So front-end components are decoupled from back-end APIs

entries.moduleTitle: Displaying data with App Studio for Business Architects
entries.title: UI elements: Views, templates, widgets
entries.text: You author applications with Views, templates, and widgets. For new apps, Pega auto-generates a set of Views (built from Templates) so you can start configuring UI immediately.

entries.moduleTitle: Displaying data with App Studio for Business Architects
entries.title: Templates
entries.text: Handle layout and responsiveness of a View — including breakpoints, white-space management, and wrapping — to ensure out-of-the-box accessibility. Each View type uses a different template; available templates vary by the type and location of the View.

entries.moduleTitle: Displaying data with App Studio for Business Architects
entries.title: Full Page View
entries.text: Automatically added when a new Case Type or data object is created. Provides the three-pane framework — navigation, summary panel, and detail area — representing the overall workspace for a Case.

entries.moduleTitle: Displaying data with App Studio for Business Architects
entries.title: Summary panel
entries.text: Displays the most critical Case information in the upper-left pane. Its content is configured by the architect and typically includes the Case's Primary Fields for quick-glance status.

entries.moduleTitle: Displaying data with App Studio for Business Architects
entries.title: Promoted Action
entries.text: Gives quick access to a frequently used Action (e.g., Change Stage) as a button on the Case header — a default pattern requiring no button component. Each Case Type supports ONE promoted Action, and it is the first Case-wide Action.

entries.moduleTitle: Displaying data with App Studio for Business Architects
entries.title: Data Capture in Views

entries.moduleTitle: Displaying data with App Studio for Business Architects
entries.title: View
entries.text: A UI component that gathers data from a user OR displays data to the user, showing the fields and instructions for the current Task/Assignment. Views are reusable across applications with multiple Case Types.

entries.moduleTitle: Displaying data with App Studio for Business Architects
entries.title: Prescribed design system
entries.text: A systemized collection of design rules, patterns, and UI component standards (Cosmos React) that ensures consistent look, feel, and accessibility across all Pega applications.

entries.moduleTitle: Displaying data with App Studio for Business Architects
entries.title: The four View types & editability
entries.text: Full Page View (read-only), Partial (read-only), List (read-only by default; can enable editing), and Form (editable). View type determines whether users can enter data.

entries.moduleTitle: Displaying data with App Studio for Business Architects
entries.title: Forms in Pega Platform

entries.moduleTitle: Displaying data with App Studio for Business Architects
entries.title: View vs. Form
entries.text: Related but distinct UI concepts: VIEW — a reusable configuration of UI elements attached to a data source · FORM — an interface specifically for collecting data, with navigation controls (a type of View)

entries.moduleTitle: Displaying data with App Studio for Business Architects
entries.title: Where Form Views are configured
entries.text: Two entry points: the Workflow tab (clicking Configure View on a Step auto-creates a Form View using the Default template), or the UX tab (manual creation, not auto-generated).

entries.moduleTitle: Displaying data with App Studio for Business Architects
entries.title: Layout
entries.text: 1–3 columns; two-column is best practice. Narrow inputs (Text single line, Currency) take one column; wider/any-height inputs (Rich Text Editor, Text area, Radio group, Checkbox, Booleans, Attachments) span two columns. This keeps tabbing left-to-right.

entries.moduleTitle: Displaying data with App Studio for Business Architects
entries.title: Field groups
entries.text: A cluster of related fields under a single header (collapsible); fields can come from the Case Type Data Model or various data objects. Field groups are specific to that View only — NOT reusable in other Views.

entries.moduleTitle: Displaying data with App Studio for Business Architects
entries.title: Multi-step vs. Hierarchical Forms
entries.text: Two Form types for complex data collection: MULTI-STEP FORM — one Assignment across MULTIPLE Views (linear; default for Create Stage) · HIERARCHICAL FORM — a single View with expandable sub-Views (nested structure for complex data)

entries.moduleTitle: Displaying data with App Studio for Business Architects
entries.title: Adding Data Through a UI View

entries.moduleTitle: Displaying data with App Studio for Business Architects
entries.title: Add fields from a View
entries.text: You can create portions of the Data Model while creating a View — adding new fields to the Case Type Data Model from the Configure/Edit View screen (e.g., adding an Account number field while configuring the Collect customer information View).

entries.moduleTitle: Displaying data with App Studio for Business Architects
entries.title: Designate Primary Fields

entries.moduleTitle: Displaying data with App Studio for Business Architects
entries.title: Primary Fields
entries.text: Fields marked as Primary on the Data Model tab that appear automatically on the Create, Edit, and Details Views without additional configuration. Label and Description are Primary by default.

entries.moduleTitle: Displaying data with App Studio for Business Architects
entries.title: Default Primary Fields on Case Types
entries.text: The Case Type Data Model automatically designates the Label and Description fields as Primary by default; removing the Primary designation removes them from the Details, Create, and Edit Views.

entries.moduleTitle: Displaying data with App Studio for Business Architects
entries.title: Primary Fields & Reference Fields (inheritance)
entries.text: Adding a reference field to a Case Type inherits the referenced object's Primary Fields into the Case Type's Views automatically, without manual field-by-field mapping.

entries.moduleTitle: Assigning and completing work for Business Architects
entries.title: Assigning and completing work for Business Architects
entries.text: Assignment routing · Cross-functional Work Groups · Approving work · Managing work deadlines

entries.moduleTitle: Assigning and completing work for Business Architects
entries.title: Assignment Routing

entries.moduleTitle: Assigning and completing work for Business Architects
entries.title: Assignment routing
entries.text: Routing sends each Assignment to the best-available user so work reaches the right person/team at the right time. It orchestrates workflow across functional teams and improves operational efficiency and customer experience.

entries.moduleTitle: Assigning and completing work for Business Architects
entries.title: Worklist vs. Work Queue
entries.text: Two types of Assignment containers: WORKLIST — Assignments routed to a SPECIFIC user (operator) to work individually · WORK QUEUE — a SHARED queue for a team/Work Group; any qualified member can pull and complete the work

entries.moduleTitle: Assigning and completing work for Business Architects
entries.title: Routing options
entries.text: In App Studio an Assignment Step can route to the current user, a specific named user, or a Work Queue. Routing decisions depend on whether work is personal or shared across a team.

entries.moduleTitle: Assigning and completing work for Business Architects
entries.title: Cross-functional Work Groups

entries.moduleTitle: Assigning and completing work for Business Architects
entries.title: Work Group
entries.text: A Work Group associates a set of users and Work Queues under a manager, organizing who collaborates on work. Cross-functional Work Groups bring members from different teams together to complete work that spans functions, improving process efficiency.

entries.moduleTitle: Assigning and completing work for Business Architects
entries.title: Approving Work

entries.moduleTitle: Assigning and completing work for Business Architects
entries.title: Approval Step
entries.text: An approval routes a Case to a user to approve or reject; the outcome determines the path (approved continues the primary path; rejected branches to rework or rejection handling). Approvals are a key OOTB workflow-automation feature.

entries.moduleTitle: Assigning and completing work for Business Architects
entries.title: Single vs. Cascading approval
entries.text: Two approval scopes: SINGLE — one approver only · CASCADING — MULTIPLE approvers in sequence (e.g., up a reporting hierarchy or via an authority matrix for higher amounts)

entries.moduleTitle: Assigning and completing work for Business Architects
entries.title: Managing Work Deadlines: SLAs and Urgency

entries.moduleTitle: Assigning and completing work for Business Architects
entries.title: Service-Level Agreement (SLA)
entries.text: An SLA defines time targets for completing an Assignment or Case. App Studio exposes a GOAL interval and a DEADLINE interval (Dev Studio adds advanced options). In Dev Studio terms, a goal/deadline IS the Service-Level Agreement rule.

entries.moduleTitle: Assigning and completing work for Business Architects
entries.title: Goal vs. Deadline
entries.text: Two SLA time thresholds on an Assignment or Case: GOAL — the EARLIER target; work SHOULD be completed by this time · DEADLINE — the LATER limit; work MUST be completed by this time

entries.moduleTitle: Assigning and completing work for Business Architects
entries.title: Case Urgency
entries.text: A numeric priority value that ensures work is completed on time. Urgency starts at an initial value and increases automatically as the SLA's Goal and Deadline thresholds pass.

entries.moduleTitle: Controlling Case workflow for Business Architects
entries.title: Controlling Case workflow for Business Architects
entries.text: Processes and Process Flows · Automation shapes in the Process Flow · Automating Decisions in the Process Flow · Conditional execution · Skipping a Stage or Process · Optional actions in workflow

entries.moduleTitle: Controlling Case workflow for Business Architects
entries.title: Processes and Process Flows

entries.moduleTitle: Controlling Case workflow for Business Architects
entries.title: Process
entries.text: A building block of the Case Life Cycle (within a Stage) that groups a series of Steps users complete. In App Studio you design Processes visually as part of the Life Cycle.

entries.moduleTitle: Controlling Case workflow for Business Architects
entries.title: Process Flow
entries.text: The underlying Flow Rule that Pega generates for a Process — the detailed flow diagram (seen in the Dev Studio process modeler) made of shapes and connectors that defines exactly how the Process executes.

entries.moduleTitle: Controlling Case workflow for Business Architects
entries.title: Automation Shapes in the Process Flow

entries.moduleTitle: Controlling Case workflow for Business Architects
entries.title: Automation shapes
entries.text: Shapes in the Process Flow that execute system actions WITHOUT user interaction — yellow-coded steps such as Send Email, Create PDF, Create Case, Wait, and Change Stage.

entries.moduleTitle: Controlling Case workflow for Business Architects
entries.title: Automating Decisions in the Process Flow

entries.moduleTitle: Controlling Case workflow for Business Architects
entries.title: Decision shapes
entries.text: Shapes that branch the Process Flow along different paths based on evaluating conditions, so the Case follows the correct route automatically rather than a single fixed path.

entries.moduleTitle: Controlling Case workflow for Business Architects
entries.title: Two-way vs. multi-way decisions
entries.text: Choose the decision type based on outcome count: Two-way (true/false) branch → use a When Condition · Multi-way (multiple outcomes) → use a Decision Table or Decision Tree

entries.moduleTitle: Controlling Case workflow for Business Architects
entries.title: Conditional Execution: The When Condition Rule

entries.moduleTitle: Controlling Case workflow for Business Architects
entries.title: When Condition Rule
entries.text: A rule that evaluates a Boolean (true/false) statement comparing field values. The result drives conditional logic — skipping Stages, Processes, or controlling which Steps execute.

entries.moduleTitle: Controlling Case workflow for Business Architects
entries.title: The three elements of a When Condition
entries.text: Every When Condition has three parts: (1) an INPUT VALUE (a field or another condition) · (2) a COMPARATOR (equals, greater than, contains, etc.) · (3) a VALUE to compare against

entries.moduleTitle: Controlling Case workflow for Business Architects
entries.title: App Studio vs. Dev Studio When Conditions
entries.text: Scope of When Conditions differs by studio: APP STUDIO — single context within one Case Type · DEV STUDIO — reusable; available across the entire application Ruleset stack

entries.moduleTitle: Controlling Case workflow for Business Architects
entries.title: Skipping a Stage or Process

entries.moduleTitle: Controlling Case workflow for Business Architects
entries.title: Skip with a When Condition
entries.text: A Stage or Process can be configured to skip when a When Condition evaluates to true, or to start only when the condition is true — enabling conditional path control.

entries.moduleTitle: Controlling Case workflow for Business Architects
entries.title: Optional Actions in the Workflow

entries.moduleTitle: Controlling Case workflow for Business Architects
entries.title: Optional actions
entries.text: Actions a user can take OUTSIDE the sequential Step flow, available on demand from the Case actions menu rather than required at a specific point in the process.

entries.moduleTitle: Controlling Case workflow for Business Architects
entries.title: Case-wide vs. Stage-wide
entries.text: Scope of an optional action: CASE-WIDE — available throughout the ENTIRE Case Life Cycle · STAGE-WIDE — available only while the Case is in a specific Stage

entries.moduleTitle: Managing Case relationships for the Business Architect
entries.title: Managing Case relationships for the Business Architect
entries.text: Creating Case relationships · Managing Case workflow dependency · Duplicate Case search

entries.moduleTitle: Managing Case relationships for the Business Architect
entries.title: Creating Case Relationships (Parent and Child Cases)

entries.moduleTitle: Managing Case relationships for the Business Architect
entries.title: Parent and child Cases
entries.text: Case relationships let you decompose complex business processes into focused, modular Case Types that work together. A parent Case orchestrates child Cases and waits on their completion.

entries.moduleTitle: Managing Case relationships for the Business Architect
entries.title: Business value of child Cases
