entries.text: Child Cases break a large, complex workflow into smaller, manageable, reusable units that can run in PARALLEL, be owned by different teams, carry their own data/SLAs, and be reused across applications — reducing complexity and improving operational efficiency.

entries.moduleTitle: Managing Case relationships for the Business Architect
entries.title: Managing Case Workflow Dependency (Wait Steps)

entries.moduleTitle: Managing Case relationships for the Business Architect
entries.title: Wait Step
entries.text: A Wait Step PAUSES a Case until a defined condition is met, which is how you manage dependencies between Cases (e.g., a parent waiting on its child Cases) or time-based pauses.

entries.moduleTitle: Managing Case relationships for the Business Architect
entries.title: Two Wait types
entries.text: (1) Case-dependency Wait — pauses until one or more specified Cases reach a particular status. (2) Timer Wait — pauses until a specific date and time is reached, then continues automatically.

entries.moduleTitle: Managing Case relationships for the Business Architect
entries.title: Duplicate Case Search

entries.moduleTitle: Managing Case relationships for the Business Architect
entries.title: Why detect duplicates
entries.text: A user might create a Case with the same data values as an existing Case (e.g., same customer, request date, items). Identifying and resolving duplicates saves time and money, so it is important to know how Pega detects them.

entries.moduleTitle: Managing Case relationships for the Business Architect
entries.title: Search duplicate Cases Step
entries.text: Pega provides the Search duplicate Cases Process, implemented as a Search duplicate Cases Step. When a Case enters the Step, the system uses BASIC conditions and WEIGHTED conditions to compare specific property values against Cases already in the system.

entries.moduleTitle: Managing Case relationships for the Business Architect
entries.title: Basic vs. weighted conditions & threshold
entries.text: Two ways to configure duplicate Case search conditions: BASIC — conditions MUST match (mandatory; all must be true) · WEIGHTED — each condition carries a numeric score; the SUM must reach a configured threshold (more flexible)

entries.moduleTitle: Managing Case relationships for the Business Architect
entries.title: Resolving a duplicate
entries.text: When a user decides the current Case is a duplicate, they resolve it with a Resolved-Duplicate status and processing ends; the flow can be customized to let the user open the original Case to make updates.

entries.moduleTitle: Managing data values for Business Architects
entries.title: Managing data values for Business Architects
entries.text: Performing calculated values · Calculations with Decision tables · Set default property values · Manipulate application data · Validation of data

entries.moduleTitle: Managing data values for Business Architects
entries.title: Performing Calculated Values

entries.moduleTitle: Managing data values for Business Architects
entries.title: Calculated value field
entries.text: A field computed AUTOMATICALLY from an expression or formula referencing other fields. The system owns the value; users cannot edit it directly and it recalculates as input fields change.

entries.moduleTitle: Managing data values for Business Architects
entries.title: When the calculation runs
entries.text: You configure when a calculated value recalculates — for example each time the underlying data changes — so the result stays current as users edit inputs. Calculated fields are typically presented as read-only because the system maintains them.

entries.moduleTitle: Managing data values for Business Architects
entries.title: Calculations with Decision Tables

entries.moduleTitle: Managing data values for Business Architects
entries.title: Decision Table
entries.text: A rule returning a value based on conditions arranged in rows. It evaluates rows TOP TO BOTTOM and returns the first matching row's result, with an 'otherwise' default for non-matching cases.

entries.moduleTitle: Managing data values for Business Architects
entries.title: When to use one for calculations
entries.text: Use a Decision Table to compute a value that depends on combinations of conditions — for example a shipping cost by region and weight, or a discount tier by order total — instead of writing complex nested logic.

entries.moduleTitle: Managing data values for Business Architects
entries.title: Setting Default Property Values

entries.moduleTitle: Managing data values for Business Architects
entries.title: Default value
entries.text: A starting value pre-populated into a field when a Case is created, so users don't have to enter commonly-used values (e.g., default Country = 'USA', default Date = today). This reduces Case processing time and improves consistency.

entries.moduleTitle: Managing data values for Business Architects
entries.title: Business value
entries.text: Defaults speed data entry, reduce errors, and standardize commonly-used values across Cases — improving efficiency and the user experience.

entries.moduleTitle: Managing data values for Business Architects
entries.title: Manipulating Application Data with Data Transforms

entries.moduleTitle: Managing data values for Business Architects
entries.title: Data Transform
entries.text: A rule that manipulates data — it SETS, COPIES, and TRANSFORMS values between pages/fields. Data Transforms ensure values are consistent between Views and between related (parent/child) Cases without manual re-entry.

entries.moduleTitle: Managing data values for Business Architects
entries.title: Common uses
entries.text: Common Data Transform use cases: Initialize/seed values on Case creation · Copy data from one Case or page to another (e.g., copy billing address to shipping address) · Keep parent and child Case data synchronized

entries.moduleTitle: Managing data values for Business Architects
entries.title: Validation of Data (Business Logic Validation)

entries.moduleTitle: Managing data values for Business Architects
entries.title: Business logic validation
entries.text: Rules that check entered data against business requirements before the Case proceeds — ensuring accuracy and completeness. They block Case advancement until all conditions are satisfied.

entries.moduleTitle: Managing data values for Business Architects
entries.title: When validation helps
entries.text: Use business-logic validation whenever invalid or inconsistent data could cause downstream errors or rework — it enforces data integrity at the point of entry rather than failing later.

entries.moduleTitle: Managing application access for Business Architects (Roles and Personas)
entries.title: Managing application access for Business Architects (Roles and Personas)
entries.text: Personas, operators, and work access · Authentication and authorization

entries.moduleTitle: Managing application access for Business Architects (Roles and Personas)
entries.title: Personas, Operators, and Work Access

entries.moduleTitle: Managing application access for Business Architects (Roles and Personas)
entries.title: User vs. Persona
entries.text: Two levels of identity in Pega access control: USER (operator) — an individual person who interacts with the application · PERSONA — a CATEGORY (role) grouping users with similar access needs, goals, and channels

entries.moduleTitle: Managing application access for Business Architects (Roles and Personas)
entries.title: Operator record (Operator ID)
entries.text: Each user has an Operator ID record that stores their profile and credentials and links them to an Access Group. The Operator record is how an individual user is represented in Pega.

entries.moduleTitle: Managing application access for Business Architects (Roles and Personas)
entries.title: Access Group
entries.text: Associates an operator with an APPLICATION, a set of ACCESS ROLES, the available PORTALS, and available work pools. The Access Group determines which application, portal, and roles a user receives. A Persona corresponds to an Access Group.

entries.moduleTitle: Managing application access for Business Architects (Roles and Personas)
entries.title: Access Role
entries.text: Defines WHAT a user is permitted to do — the permissions to classes and actions (role-based access control, RBAC). Access Roles are granted via the Access Group.

entries.moduleTitle: Managing application access for Business Architects (Roles and Personas)
entries.title: Authentication and Authorization

entries.moduleTitle: Managing application access for Business Architects (Roles and Personas)
entries.title: Authentication
entries.text: Verifies WHO the user is — confirming identity at login (e.g., username/password, SSO, multi-factor). Authentication answers 'Are you really you?' and happens FIRST.

entries.moduleTitle: Managing application access for Business Architects (Roles and Personas)
entries.title: Authorization
entries.text: Determines WHAT an authenticated user is allowed to access and do — enforced through Access Roles/Access Groups (RBAC). Authorization answers 'What are you allowed to do?' and happens AFTER authentication.

entries.moduleTitle: Customizing the user interface for Business Architects
entries.title: Customizing the user interface for Business Architects
entries.text: Identifying Portals and landing pages · User interface controls and presentation · Dynamic functionality on user interface elements

entries.moduleTitle: Customizing the user interface for Business Architects
entries.title: Identifying Portals and Landing Pages

entries.moduleTitle: Customizing the user interface for Business Architects
entries.title: Portal
entries.text: A portal is the user's workspace — the overall interface a user sees when they log in. Tailoring portals by CHANNEL and PERSONA lets each type of user perform their job efficiently with the right tools and information front-and-center.

entries.moduleTitle: Customizing the user interface for Business Architects
entries.title: Business benefit of portals
entries.text: Portals deliver a role-appropriate, branded, productive experience: each Persona gets a workspace suited to their tasks, improving efficiency and the user experience while keeping branding consistent.

entries.moduleTitle: Customizing the user interface for Business Architects
entries.title: Elements of a portal
entries.text: A portal is composed of regions such as a HEADER (logo, search, utilities), NAVIGATION (menu to move between areas), and LANDING PAGES / dashboards that present content and work in the main area.

entries.moduleTitle: Customizing the user interface for Business Architects
entries.title: Landing pages
entries.text: Landing pages are configurable pages within a portal (e.g., dashboards, reports, custom content). You can UPDATE a portal by adding new landing pages and corresponding navigation entries so users reach the information they need.

entries.moduleTitle: Customizing the user interface for Business Architects
entries.title: User Interface Controls and Presentation

entries.moduleTitle: Customizing the user interface for Business Architects
entries.title: Control styling at runtime
entries.text: Style formats and conditional formatting change how a control is displayed at run time — for example, highlighting overdue values — without altering the underlying field value.

entries.moduleTitle: Customizing the user interface for Business Architects
entries.title: Presentation vs. data
entries.text: Styling is separate from stored data: PRESENTATION (styling) — affects only HOW information is DISPLAYED; does not change the stored value · DATA (value) — the actual stored information, independent of visual appearance

entries.moduleTitle: Customizing the user interface for Business Architects
entries.title: Dynamic Functionality on UI Elements

entries.moduleTitle: Customizing the user interface for Business Architects
entries.title: Dynamic visibility
entries.text: You can control the VISIBILITY of fields and UI elements dynamically — showing or hiding them based on conditions (for example, show the 'Reason for rejection' field only when the decision is 'Rejected'). This tailors the View to the context.

entries.moduleTitle: Customizing the user interface for Business Architects
entries.title: Attributes used to dynamically display information
entries.text: Visibility and dynamic behavior are driven by conditions/attributes such as 'visible when' a condition (When rule) is true, or comparisons against field values — so the UI adapts to the data and the user's situation in real time.

entries.moduleTitle: Evaluating application data with Insights for Business Architects
entries.title: Evaluating application data with Insights for Business Architects
entries.text: Application data for Insights

entries.moduleTitle: Evaluating application data with Insights for Business Architects
entries.title: Exploring and Analyzing Application Data

entries.moduleTitle: Evaluating application data with Insights for Business Architects
entries.title: The Explore Data landing page
entries.text: Pega Platform lets you easily explore and analyze your application's data from the Explore Data landing page in App Studio. Organizations analyze operations to understand the performance of their teams and processes.

entries.moduleTitle: Evaluating application data with Insights for Business Architects
entries.title: Insight
entries.text: An Insight transforms a data query into a TABLE or a VISUALIZATION (chart) that you can save and SHARE between users. Insights turn raw Case/application data into something stakeholders can read and act on.

entries.moduleTitle: Evaluating application data with Insights for Business Architects
entries.title: Benefits of Insights
entries.text: Insights provide self-service, low-code data analysis: Business users can answer operational questions · Monitor team/process performance · Share results — without writing code or exporting to another tool

entries.moduleTitle: Evaluating application data with Insights for Business Architects
entries.title: Table and Chart Insights

entries.moduleTitle: Evaluating application data with Insights for Business Architects
entries.title: Table Insight
entries.text: Presents query results as rows and columns — ideal for detailed, record-level review (e.g., a list of Assistance Request Cases created in the last 30 days with key fields).

entries.moduleTitle: Evaluating application data with Insights for Business Architects
entries.title: Chart Insight
entries.text: Presents query results as a visualization (e.g., bar, line, or pie chart) — ideal for spotting trends, comparisons, and distributions at a glance (e.g., Cases per day, by status, or by region).

entries.moduleTitle: Evaluating application data with Insights for Business Architects
entries.title: The Role of BIX in Data Analysis

entries.moduleTitle: Evaluating application data with Insights for Business Architects
entries.title: BIX (Business Intelligence Exchange)
entries.text: BIX is Pega's data EXTRACT capability that pulls application data OUT of Pega into external databases or files so it can be analyzed in external business-intelligence/reporting tools — suited to large-scale, enterprise, or cross-system analytics.

entries.moduleTitle: Evaluating application data with Insights for Business Architects
entries.title: Insights vs. BIX
entries.text: Two Pega data analysis options: INSIGHTS — analyze and visualize data IN Pega (in-platform, self-service) · BIX — EXTRACTS data to external systems for analysis OUTSIDE Pega (use when combining with external BI tools)

entries.title: Application deployment for Business Architects
entries.text: Release management with Pega · Release management best practices · Application deployment with Pega Cloud

entries.title: DevOps & CI/CD
entries.text: Pega Platform uses DevOps best practices — Continuous Integration and Continuous Delivery (CI/CD) — to quickly and reliably move application changes from development, through testing, to deployment on the production system.

entries.title: Continuous Integration (CI)
entries.text: Developers frequently integrate and merge their changes, with automated builds and tests running to catch problems early. CI keeps the application in a consistently working, testable state.

entries.title: Continuous Delivery (CD)
entries.text: Uses repeatable testing and staged promotion to keep changes ready for release. Production deployment may still require approval; Continuous Deployment additionally automates shipping validated changes.

entries.title: Pega Deployment Manager
entries.text: Pega's tool that provides a model-driven CI/CD PIPELINE to automate deploying application changes across environments (for example development → QA → staging → production), orchestrating merges, packaging, automated testing, and promotion with approval gates.

entries.title: Branch-based parallel development
entries.text: Teams develop features in Branches and merge them into the target application Ruleset when stable, conflict-free, and approved — keeping parallel work isolated until ready (ties back to Branches from earlier modules).

entries.title: Lock and version
entries.text: Lock older Ruleset versions and develop in the topmost Application Layer; increment versions to track changes. Locking promotes stability and predictable releases.

entries.title: Automated testing & governance
entries.text: Use automated tests (e.g., unit/scenario tests) within the pipeline and enforce governance/approval gates so only validated changes promote toward production.

entries.title: Pega Cloud
entries.text: Pega's managed cloud environment for running and deploying Pega applications, reducing the burden of managing infrastructure and supporting scalable, reliable operations.

entries.title: Pega Cloud Choice
entries.text: Offers deployment models suited to organizational needs. Pega Cloud provides managed operations; client-managed cloud leaves infrastructure operations with the client and provides Pega platform support. Responsibility depends on the selected model.

entries.moduleTitle: Pega tools that support Scrum for Business Architects
entries.title: Pega tools that support Scrum for Business Architects
entries.text: Collaboration tools in App Studio · Using Agile Studio and Agile Workbench · User story readiness · Maintaining the backlog

entries.moduleTitle: Pega tools that support Scrum for Business Architects
entries.title: Collaboration Tools in App Studio

entries.moduleTitle: Pega tools that support Scrum for Business Architects
entries.title: Pulse
entries.text: A collaboration feed that lets team members post messages, comment, and reply IN CONTEXT (e.g., on a Case or feature), keeping conversations attached to the work and the relevant stakeholders informed.

entries.moduleTitle: Pega tools that support Scrum for Business Architects
entries.title: Tags
entries.text: Labels you apply to work items and posts so they can be ORGANIZED and easily FOUND/grouped later — improving discoverability and collaboration across the team.

entries.moduleTitle: Pega tools that support Scrum for Business Architects
entries.title: Developer Assistant
entries.text: An App Studio helper that surfaces guidance/feedback and helps team members view and track application development work as they build.

entries.moduleTitle: Pega tools that support Scrum for Business Architects
entries.title: Agile Workbench vs. Agile Studio

entries.moduleTitle: Pega tools that support Scrum for Business Architects
entries.title: Agile Workbench
entries.text: A lightweight tool built into App Studio for capturing and tracking user stories, bugs, and feedback in real time alongside Case design. Separate from the standalone Agile Studio application.

entries.moduleTitle: Pega tools that support Scrum for Business Architects
entries.title: Agile Studio
entries.text: A separate, COMPREHENSIVE Pega application for managing Agile/Scrum at scale — organizing backlogs, sprints, teams, releases, user stories, and bugs across projects. Business team members use it to create and organize the artifacts used to manage Scrum.

entries.moduleTitle: Pega tools that support Scrum for Business Architects
entries.title: How to choose
entries.text: Use Agile Workbench for quick, in-context capture/tracking inside App Studio; use Agile Studio for full, end-to-end Agile project and backlog management across the program.

entries.moduleTitle: Pega tools that support Scrum for Business Architects
entries.title: User Story Readiness

entries.moduleTitle: Pega tools that support Scrum for Business Architects
entries.title: User story
entries.text: A concise statement of a business requirement from the user's perspective, used by the team to build and test functionality. BAs author user stories that System Architects implement.

entries.moduleTitle: Pega tools that support Scrum for Business Architects
entries.title: Readiness (Definition of Ready)
entries.text: Teams agree their Definition of Ready for the project. Common checks before selecting a story for a sprint include: Clearly written (unambiguous requirements) · Defined ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA · Appropriately SIZED/estimated · PRIORITIZED by the Product Owner · Free of blocking dependencies

entries.moduleTitle: Pega tools that support Scrum for Business Architects
entries.title: Maintaining the Backlog

entries.moduleTitle: Pega tools that support Scrum for Business Architects
entries.title: Product backlog
entries.text: The prioritized list of user stories, bugs, and other work for the application. It is the single ordered source of what the team will build next, driving Sprint Planning.

entries.moduleTitle: Pega tools that support Scrum for Business Architects
entries.title: Backlog maintenance / refinement
entries.text: The Product Owner OWNS and PRIORITIZES the backlog; ongoing refinement keeps items clear, sized, and correctly ordered so the most valuable, ready work is at the top for upcoming sprints. BAs collaborate with the PO to refine and prioritize.

entries.title: Low-code defined
entries.text: Low-code application development · Studios · App Studio · Dev Studio · Integrating with external applications

entries.title: Low-code development
entries.text: Low-code tools turn visual configuration into executable behavior. Business contributors and developers share a model; developers can still extend advanced behavior. The source’s historical slogan is not a guarantee that every requirement is automatically implemented.

entries.title: Value of low-code
entries.text: Low-code bridges business stakeholders and developers with a COMMON VISUAL LANGUAGE. Teams become more agile, deliver faster, and minimize disruption. Shortened feedback loops free limited resources to tackle the backlog and innovate quickly.

entries.title: Omnichannel reach
entries.text: The same Pega application can be a web page, mobile app, or chatbot — data can arrive by email or robot. Organizations maintain ONE codebase for all channels instead of separate code per channel.

entries.title: Low-code AND professional developers
entries.text: Visual, end-to-end tools make everyone more productive. Citizen developers create application code; experienced developers extend robust applications more rapidly, hide implementation, and build patterns once to reuse many times across the ecosystem.

entries.title: App Studio
entries.text: A low-code authoring space providing CORE features: Case design, data management, and user experience (UI). Users: citizen developers plus technical staff — application developers, front-end developers, data engineers, business analysts, and System Architects. The place to get applications operating quickly.

entries.title: Dev Studio
entries.text: A low-code authoring space with ADVANCED features. Technical users: full-stack developers, System Architects, and database/security administrators. Used for complex Rule configuration, security/access control, reuse management, and performance.

entries.title: Prediction Studio
entries.text: An ANALYTICS space for data scientists and business decision-makers, providing features to build machine-learning models for adaptive, predictive, and text analytics. Access requires pxPredictionStudio among the Portals on the user's access group.

entries.title: Admin Studio
entries.text: A software ADMINISTRATION space managed by IT for system administration — runtime information and configuration options for monitoring and debugging system resources.

entries.title: Three areas of every studio
entries.text: (1) Header — studio-switcher drop-down (upper-left), menus, and tools. (2) Navigation pane — explorers such as Case Type and Data explorers. (3) Authoring space — where you configure application behavior and review the application overview.

entries.title: Support for agile development
entries.text: App Studio supports agile best practices and REAL-TIME UI design while processing work. A team testing an online-shopping UI can add fields and change controls (e.g., drop-downs) live — ideal for stakeholder reviews where feedback is implemented in real time.

entries.title: Application profile
entries.text: Captures and presents user stories, bugs, and feedback items to support agile best practices and collaboration across technical and business members. Provides traceability from objectives to development tasks to implementation.

entries.title: Rules
entries.text: Instructions that govern application behavior (like the rules of chess govern the pieces). As you build visually, Pega auto-generates Rules in the background using the SAME names you choose — which is why business-friendly names matter.

entries.title: Layers & Rulesets
entries.text: Rules are organized into LAYERS (each a unique application built on one or more Layers). RULESETS group and share Rules across applications — reuse an entire Ruleset rather than rebuilding individual Rules.

entries.title: Application Layers Widget & OOTB architectures
entries.text: The App Studio overview's Application Layers Widget visualizes your Rulesets and identifies the application type. Two OOTB architectures: Constellation architecture (Constellation Ruleset, new View-based UI) and Traditional UI architecture (Theme Cosmos Ruleset, Section-based UI).

entries.title: Dev Studio: Co-development, Reuse, and Naming
Domain vs. Implementation experts
entries.text: Two groups defined by Pega for co-development: DOMAIN experts (Business Analysts, Citizen Developers, front-end developers) — provide process/user insight; primarily work in App Studio · IMPLEMENTATION experts handle complex configuration in Dev Studio when needed, and use App Studio for supported application work.

entries.title: Co-development
entries.text: Both groups work together: e.g., a Business Analyst designs shipping-address Views in App Studio; a System Architect adds logic in Dev Studio to auto-copy the billing address and builds test cases.

entries.title: Promote reuse by extending Rule scope
entries.text: In Dev Studio, extend a rule's scope from one Case Type to an application, division, or entire organization — creating a shared library that citizen developers can reuse without rebuilding from scratch.

entries.title: Advanced SLA options in Dev Studio
entries.text: Beyond App Studio's basic goal/deadline, Dev Studio exposes: Initialization behavior (custom initial urgency, delayed timer start) · Variable interval length (programmatic durations per Case) · Account-for-business-days (exclude holidays/weekends) · Additional escalation actions (reassign a task or resolve a Case)

entries.title: Integration connectors
entries.text: Pega supports many integration standards and communication protocols (e.g., external database or web service) so you focus on business requirements, not connectivity. A standard API connector exchanges data in REAL TIME when both systems support the protocol.

entries.title: Robotic Process Automation (RPA)
entries.text: Used when NO other integration option is feasible — typically legacy systems with no API. A robot interacts with the system's front end (desktop, web, or terminal UI) to perform the same task a person would, far faster.

entries.title: Attended RPA
entries.text: Automation that works ALONGSIDE a human in the process, in real time. Example: a CSR triggers a robot mid-call to update an address by driving the legacy system's UI while the customer waits.

entries.title: Unattended RPA
entries.text: The request is placed in a QUEUE for later background processing. Advantages: optimizes system resources, reduces peak loads, and lets the CSR keep serving the customer instead of waiting for the update to finish.

entries.title: Pega Robot Manager
entries.text: A control-tower application that lets you monitor and schedule RPA robots and provides performance analytics for all robots.

entries.title: Defining a customer Microjourney
entries.text: Case Life Cycle · Case Life Cycle design · Multi-step forms · Draft mode

entries.title: Microjourney
entries.text: A Microjourney scopes work toward a meaningful customer outcome. Case Types model that work, and the Case Life Cycle visualizes the path to completion; the terms are related, not universally identical artifacts.

entries.title: Case Type vs. Case
entries.text: Fundamental Pega terminology: CASE TYPE — an ABSTRACT model of a repeatable business transaction (the template) · CASE — a SPECIFIC instance with a unique Case ID; assigned to operators who perform the work

entries.title: Case Life Cycle model
entries.text: Organize the end-to-end work for a customer or business outcome into Stages, Processes and Steps. This model connects the repeatable Case Type design to how its individual Cases progress.

entries.title: Case Life Cycle: Stages, Processes, Steps
Stage
entries.text: The top-level organization of work — a distinct phase or milestone. You begin Case Life Cycle design by organizing work into Stages arranged left-to-right in the order work generally proceeds (e.g., Submission, Processing, Delivery).

entries.title: Process
entries.text: A Stage contains one or more Processes; each Process groups a sequence of Steps. A Case moves to the next Process after completing the current one (unless Processes are configured to run in parallel).

entries.title: Step
entries.text: The smallest unit: a user action (a Collect information Step / Assignment, shown green) or a system action (an Automation Step, shown yellow). Steps define exactly what happens within a Process.

entries.title: Case Life Cycle Design (Stage types & transitions)
Create Stage
entries.text: The Create Stage is first and captures initial data. It cannot be deleted or moved. Cases using it receive their Case ID at creation. The source permits renaming and excludes configurable Stage transitions on it; older Case Types may predate this Stage.

entries.title: Primary Stage vs. primary path
entries.text: Two related Case Life Cycle concepts: PRIMARY STAGE — a defined Stage that leads to the expected/successful outcome · PRIMARY PATH — the complete route through all Primary Stages without deviation; most Cases take this path

entries.title: Alternate Stage
entries.text: Handles deviations/exceptions from the primary path (optional); often a negative resolution or a place to fix issues and re-enter the primary path, typically reached via a Change Stage automation.

entries.title: Resolution Stage
entries.text: Marked red; defines end-of-life-cycle behavior. Every Case Type should have at least one Resolution Stage; a Case can resolve through more than one (e.g., approved vs. rejected). Case statuses beginning with Resolved- (e.g., Resolved-Completed, Resolved-Rejected) typically close the Case.

entries.title: Step transitions versus form navigation
entries.text: For ordinary Process Steps, enable Allow users to go back to the previous step to expose Previous at runtime. This Process setting is distinct from the three Multi-step Form navigation layouts.

entries.title: Multi-step Form
entries.text: A single Assignment completed by a single user, broken into multiple focused, concise Views shown in sequence — a guided, linear set of screens. The default Create Process in the Create Stage is a Multi-step Form.

entries.title: Navigation
entries.text: Horizontal, vertical and standard layouts use Next/Previous across the form Views; Submit is on the final View. Required-field constraints and final submission limit navigation. Do not generalize this form behavior to every Process Step.

entries.title: Draft mode
entries.text: A design state for rapidly outlining a Case Life Cycle — adding Stages, Processes, and Steps WITHOUT fully configuring each element. Ideal for capturing the shape of the Microjourney with stakeholders before detailing every rule.

entries.title: Draft data objects
entries.text: Creating a new object in the designer’s Data & Interfaces area produces a draft data placeholder. Merely enabling Process draft mode is not the trigger. Configure its fields and integration through the Data Objects and Integrations page or Dev Studio.

entries.title: Draft mode and release checks
entries.text: Process draft mode permits development runs with configuration issues. Resolve them before release. Saving the Case Type in App Studio turns it off for issue-free Processes; manual disabling is available in Dev Studio. A draft data object and Process draft mode are different concepts.

entries.title: Inviting users to an application
entries.text: Users and personas

entries.title: User
entries.text: An individual who interacts with the application to perform work. Each user is represented by an Operator ID record that stores their profile and credentials and links them (via an Access Group) to an application, portal, and roles.

entries.title: Persona
entries.text: A CATEGORY of users who interact with a Case in the same way and share the same access needs — for example Customer, CSR, or Manager. Many individual users can be assigned to a single Persona for role-based access.

entries.title: Users-to-Persona relationship
entries.text: Assign individual users to the Persona appropriate to their responsibilities. A Persona includes an associated role and groups common security and Assignments. Configure and verify permissions, routing and Channel access; assigning a Persona is only one aspect of application security.

entries.title: Channel interface
entries.text: The user interface through which people interact with the application, such as web or mobile. Associate Personas with suitable Channels; multiple Personas can share one Channel, and Persona/Channel access can be configured for each Case Stage.

entries.title: Managing Personas/Channels in App Studio
entries.text: In App Studio, open Users > User Management > Persona to add a Persona. The application starts with the Users Persona. A new Persona receives default permissions and a Work Queue, which can be modified along with its Channel experience.

entries.title: Inviting a user and adding a Persona
Inviting a user
entries.text: In App Studio, open Users > User management > People, create a user with an email address, and assign an appropriate Persona or developer role. Use an account unique to each individual. Do not assume the invitation sends credentials or bypasses the configured authentication method.

entries.title: Adding a Persona to a user
entries.text: Assign a business user to the appropriate Persona and verify the associated permissions and work configuration. Each Persona has an associated role, but not every role has a Persona. A Persona and an Access Group are distinct concepts; do not assume a universal one-to-one mapping.

entries.title: Pega Center-out architecture
entries.text: Pega's Center-out business architecture · Accessibility in Center-out development

entries.title: Top-down approach
entries.text: Designs applications around the PRESENTATION layer's delivery Channels (web, mobile, digital messaging, voice-AI). Its most significant disadvantage: the same business logic must be implemented MULTIPLE TIMES to deliver a consistent experience across the different Channels.

entries.title: Bottom-up approach
entries.text: Designs applications around the DATA access layer. Risk: each system has its own data view; legacy systems built in silos duplicate data, and no single solution provides a complete view of a business entity like a Customer.

entries.title: Center-out business architecture
entries.text: Puts the BUSINESS LOGIC layer at the center, with customer outcome at the core. Presentation and data-access layers stay SEPARATE from business logic — so Channels and databases can change without touching the logic.

entries.title: Presentation layer (connects UP)
entries.text: The business logic is connected up into the presentation layer so delivery Channels dynamically RESPOND to changes in the central business logic — no recoding per channel.

entries.title: Application & business logic layer (the hub)
entries.text: The central hub containing all the business logic needed to achieve the desired strategic outcome for the organization.

entries.title: Data access layer (connects DOWN)
entries.text: Connections down to data are insulated from the business logic, so changes in systems of record — for example, moving from on-premise to Cloud storage — do NOT require changes in the application's business logic.

entries.title: 1. Manage intelligence centrally
entries.text: Center-out principle 1 — start with the business logic: Business outcomes guided by real-time customer information · Rules consistently enforced across all channels · Everyone uses the SAME intelligence (single source of truth)

entries.title: 2. Focus on outcomes, align your process
entries.text: Get the work done using Case Management and a MICROJOURNEY approach — implementing a part of the customer journey that is tied to a specific outcome.

entries.title: 3. Connect experiences up to your Channels
entries.text: Provide a consistent user experience by keeping front-end and back-end logic coordinated; changes are reflected dynamically without recoding.

entries.title: 4. Connect down to your data, keep logic nimble
entries.text: Access data without adding complexity — quickly and easily define the data needed and access it in running applications without worrying about how or where the data is stored or accessed.

entries.title: 5. Manage variations to be scale-ready
entries.text: Start small and fast, then scale big and broad and stay future-proof by adapting to different customer types, lines of business, and geographies using Pega's SITUATIONAL LAYER CAKE.

entries.title: Efficiency
entries.text: Developers define business rules ONCE in a central location, eliminating duplication and reducing inconsistencies across channels and applications.

entries.title: Agility
entries.text: When business requirements change, you update the CENTRAL logic and the system applies those changes across all channel interfaces — making applications more responsive to evolving needs.

entries.title: Governance
entries.text: Centralized business logic means rules are defined once and enforced consistently across all channels — simplifying auditing, monitoring, and policy enforcement.

entries.title: Scalability
entries.text: As the organization adds new channel interfaces or customer touchpoints, you REUSE existing business logic to maintain consistency.

entries.title: Model-driven UI
entries.text: An approach in which the underlying data models and business rules GENERATE the user interface. In Center-out, these models reside at the core and the system dynamically generates the UI from them.

entries.title: Patterns
entries.text: Reusable templates for model-driven UIs. Define the Data Model and business rules at the center, then SELECT and CONFIGURE patterns to render the interface — maintaining consistency and keeping business logic centralized across devices and channels.

entries.title: Separation of logic and presentation
entries.text: A key advantage of patterns: when business rules change, the UI ADAPTS AUTOMATICALLY without manual updates. Pattern-based UIs also support responsive design across devices and channels.

entries.title: Centralized accessibility
entries.text: Shared patterns allow accessibility improvements to benefit multiple application experiences. Developers still need to evaluate the actual content, configuration and user interactions, including customizations and assistive-technology behavior.

entries.title: Standards supported
entries.text: The architecture supports compliance with major standards including Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1 and Section 508 requirements, embedded into the core patterns and components.

entries.title: Evolving standards
entries.text: Shared components centralize accessibility support and improvements. Application-specific content, configuration, keyboard behavior, and assistive-technology interactions still require evaluation; shared patterns are not a complete compliance guarantee.

entries.title: Constellation accessibility features
entries.text: Built-in support includes page regions, heading structure, a skip-to-main mechanism, keyboard interaction, semantic roles, associated field labels and helpful validation messages. Theme configuration warns about color combinations that miss contrast requirements. These features do not remove the need to check custom content.

entries.title: Accessible content and evaluation
entries.text: Use clear labels, meaningful link text and specific errors. Helper text should add guidance rather than repeat labels or refer only to visual position or color. Prefer labels/helper text over unnecessary placeholders. Test manually and with automated scans; Accessibility Inspector is not supported for Constellation applications.

entries.title: Pega GenAI in Pega Platform
entries.text: Generative AI in Pega · Generating a Case type using Pega GenAI Autopilot · Generating Case data using Pega GenAI Autopilot · Generating personas using Pega GenAI Autopilot

entries.title: Pega GenAI
entries.text: A suite of generative AI-powered features integrated across Pega Platform, available beginning with Pega Infinity '23. It helps developers, learners, and users build applications, enhance learning, improve operational efficiency, and stay aligned with best practices.

entries.title: Pega Blueprint
entries.text: A separate SaaS design tool for collaborative application proposals. Review its suggested Case Types, data and Personas, then import the Blueprint into Pega Platform to accelerate development. The proposal is not automatically a production-ready application or a delivery-time guarantee.

entries.title: Pega GenAI Autopilot
entries.text: Design-time AI features in App Studio assist with workflow, fields, Personas and testing data. Review recommendations in context; claims about development-speed improvements are not a measured guarantee for an individual project.

entries.title: Pega GenAI Connect
entries.text: Lets you develop custom Pega GenAI-powered capabilities using the Pega GenAI gateway; an add-on compatible with Pega Platform, Customer Service, or Sales Automation.

entries.title: GenAI Run-Time Tools and Custom AI
Pega GenAI Coach
entries.text: Provides expert advice and feedback on END-USER tasks at application RUNTIME — ideal for task-specific guidance relevant to a Pega Case.

entries.title: Pega GenAI Agent and Tool Rules
entries.text: Automate Case processing and provide conversational support for run-time users. Agents perform automated actions and offer run-time guidance to accelerate Case processing; Tool Rules add governance, security, and compliance.

entries.title: Pega GenAI Knowledge Buddy
entries.text: Conversational answers grounded in an organization’s procedural documents and knowledge bases, useful while learning, developing or working. It can provide client-specific context; it is not restricted to generic employee questions.

entries.title: Search Assistant & OpenAI search
entries.text: Search Assistant integrates with Pega Community search (powered by Knowledge Buddy) to link relevant materials. OpenAI search on the Pega Documentation site answers questions when you add a question mark to the end of a search query.

entries.title: Pega GenAI Autopilot at Design Time
What Autopilot accelerates
entries.text: Autopilot delivers real-time, context-aware guidance and task prioritization during development. For a loan app, it suggests application components including Case Types, fields in the Data Model, and Personas — and developers can review and modify any recommendation before generating it.

entries.title: The Autopilot workflow
entries.text: When creating a Case Type, Autopilot can suggest: Case Type name · Workflow (Stages/Processes/Steps) · Data Model fields · Personas · Sample data records · Form fill with sample data at runtime · Natural-language-generated Insights

entries.title: Human-in-the-loop responsibility
entries.text: Pega is NOT responsible for the content of Autopilot suggestions — always review AI-powered recommendations before accepting them.

entries.title: Blueprint as a SaaS design tool
entries.text: Blueprint rapidly and collaboratively designs new applications and Case Types and operates INDEPENDENTLY as a SaaS tool — no Pega instance required to collaborate. The result imports into Pega Platform to jumpstart development.

entries.title: What Blueprint proposes
entries.text: From a business-terms description, Blueprint proposes Case Types, Case Life Cycles, Data Models, data objects, and Personas, plus best-practice application templates, enabling quick design edits to fit requirements.

entries.title: Connect Generative AI automation Step
entries.text: Since Pega Infinity '24, configure a Connect Generative AI Step in App Studio. A Connect Rule begins with a Prompt — the request for information sent to the Pega GenAI engine, custom to the Step or reused from Dev Studio.

entries.title: Three response structures
entries.text: GenAI response types and their Data Model mapping: Structured - Single: one page/paragraph or field+value, auto-mapped to a Data Model field · Structured - List: bulleted fields/values mapped to an embedded data list · Unstructured: long/complex output — best practice is to map to a Text (paragraph) field

entries.title: Target field requirement
entries.text: You must identify a target field to write the response into, and add that target field to the application UI so the response can be displayed to the user.

entries.title: Pega GenAI Agent and Tool Rules
Agents
entries.text: Configurable AI assistants that automate Case processing and offer run-time guidance. An agent can run an automation, start a Case, call another agent, or launch a user action. Extend reach via agent-to-agent or MCP protocols.

entries.title: Guardrails via Tool Rules
entries.text: Detailed descriptions and guardrails ensure the agent responds precisely; at run time users converse with agents in natural-language chat. Agents can also process and extract data from uploaded documents, saving manual analysis time.

entries.title: Generating a Case Type and Data Model
Case Type proposal
entries.text: In App Studio’s Case Type tab, choose a suggested name or enter your own. Suggestions use the application name and metadata. Select the Autopilot option to propose a Life Cycle and Data Model.

entries.title: Review before creation
entries.text: Check and modify Stages and Steps against stakeholder requirements. Next proposes fields with Name, Type and technical ID. Edit names/types, add fields or remove unsuitable suggestions. Embedded Data and Data reference proposals can create associated data objects.

entries.title: Create and inspect
entries.text: Submit after review. Inspect the created Life Cycle on Workflow and the fields on Data model. A generated proposal is not proof that workflow, integration or security requirements are satisfied.

entries.title: Sample data records
entries.text: Select a data object and open Records. Generate sample records with Autopilot and specify the desired number. The generated values correspond to field types; they can support tests before external data integration is available.

entries.title: Fill a running test form
entries.text: While testing a Case, Fill form with AI populates its form fields. These values become part of the Case data used during processing; they are test samples rather than verified production records.

entries.title: Persona proposals
entries.text: Open Users > User management in App Studio. Autopilot proposes Persona names and descriptions from application metadata. Choose a proposal or enter a custom name, then review it against real stakeholder responsibilities.

entries.title: Associate the Persona
entries.text: After creation, add the Persona through the Case Life Cycle’s Personas & Channels area. Generating the business user model is not a guarantee of complete authorization or routing configuration.

entries.moduleTitle: Accelerating application building with Pega Blueprint
entries.title: Accelerating application building with Pega Blueprint
entries.text: Pega Blueprint overview · Generating a Pega Blueprint · Importing a Pega Blueprint into Pega Platform · Using Pega Blueprint to create a Customer Service for Insurance application

entries.moduleTitle: Accelerating application building with Pega Blueprint
entries.title: Pega Blueprint Overview

entries.moduleTitle: Accelerating application building with Pega Blueprint
entries.title: Pega Blueprint
entries.text: Blueprint supports collaborative workflow design using industry templates or generative AI. It proposes a starting point that teams review against their requirements.

entries.moduleTitle: Accelerating application building with Pega Blueprint
entries.title: Standalone SaaS tool
entries.text: Blueprint is SaaS, independent of a Pega Platform development instance and Operator login. SaaS sign-in and collaboration access still apply; knowing a URL does not imply unrestricted access. Its interface evolves continually.

entries.moduleTitle: Accelerating application building with Pega Blueprint
entries.title: Augments, not replaces
entries.text: Blueprint accelerates initial design; App Studio and Dev Studio support implementation and review after import. Templates are starting points, not substitutes for configuration and testing.

entries.moduleTitle: Accelerating application building with Pega Blueprint
entries.title: Generating a Pega Blueprint

entries.moduleTitle: Accelerating application building with Pega Blueprint
entries.title: Describe in business terms
entries.text: Provide industry, sub-industry, department, purpose and a functional description. Use Other for an unlisted industry. Choose a template or GenAI, supply organization/language details and upload relevant supporting assets.

entries.moduleTitle: Accelerating application building with Pega Blueprint
entries.title: Generate and modify
entries.text: Review Case Types with stakeholders. Edit Primary/Alternate Stages, Processes and Steps; use Notes for routing, SLA and conditions. Preview my app supports design review. Check fields, types, descriptions, primary fields, single/multiple records and user-input/calculated sources.

entries.moduleTitle: Accelerating application building with Pega Blueprint
entries.title: Best-practice templates
entries.text: Templates offer an industry starting point. Review Personas, access needs, Channels and release effort, then check the summary for workflow, data and integration completeness. Export PDF for reference or .blueprint for import; revision history and dashboard support ongoing changes. A live-demo option can provision an instance and import the design.

entries.moduleTitle: Accelerating application building with Pega Blueprint
entries.title: Importing a Pega Blueprint into Pega Platform

entries.moduleTitle: Accelerating application building with Pega Blueprint
entries.title: Export and import
entries.text: In App Studio, create an application with Build from a Blueprint and upload the technical file. Verify its details and intended built-on stack. Using an existing application through the New Application wizard requires saving that application as a template.

entries.moduleTitle: Accelerating application building with Pega Blueprint
entries.title: Who imports it
entries.text: The authorized implementation team imports and reviews the application. Assign technical responsibility within the project; the source does not impose an LSA-only permission or a separate import ceremony.

entries.moduleTitle: Accelerating application building with Pega Blueprint
entries.title: What import creates (and the exception)
entries.text: For the documented new-application workflow, created assets except Access Roles go into a Branch. This is about placement, not whether Access Roles are created. Base Rulesets are locked; use the provided password for appropriate merges and store it securely.

entries.moduleTitle: Accelerating application building with Pega Blueprint
entries.title: PremBridge not required
entries.text: Pega GenAI PremBridge is NOT required to import Pega Blueprints into a new or existing application.

entries.moduleTitle: Accelerating application building with Pega Blueprint
entries.title: Review import choices
entries.text: For Case Types choose build, inherit or skip. For data objects choose build, inherit, reuse or skip: inheritance creates a new object; reuse links to the built-on object without its own new class. Build or skip Personas. Check class layers and Case/data classes before Submit, then inspect the result and add users with Personas.

entries.moduleTitle: Accelerating application building with Pega Blueprint
entries.title: Post-import validation
entries.text: Check existing-app overlap before extending it. After import, prepare developer configuration and merges, refine Decision shapes, Flow Actions and locking, and validate database mappings, Data Pages and properties. Test alternate paths, approvals, automation and child Cases.

entries.moduleTitle: Accelerating application building with Pega Blueprint
entries.title: Using Blueprint for an Industry App (Customer Service for Insurance)

entries.moduleTitle: Accelerating application building with Pega Blueprint
entries.title: Industry templates
entries.text: The insurance example starts with a Customer Service template and adds a golf-cart Case. It inherits existing service Case Types and builds the new Case Type; infrastructure Cases also appear. A weather Step and field are separate design changes. After import, change the field to Picklist and add it to a View. Configure data, integrations, Channels and user groups, then simulate an interaction and review wrap-up/recent Cases. The example’s creation time is not a project guarantee.

entries.title: Capturing and presenting data
entries.text: Fields · Calculated values · Views

entries.title: Field
entries.text: A named, reusable UI component that stores a value associated with a Case. The field name and stored value form a data element. Its Field Type controls the kind of information stored and its display format.

entries.title: Field Type
entries.text: Determines the information stored and how it is formatted. Pega predicts a type from the field name and defaults to Text (single line), but the author must verify the type before submitting.

entries.title: Simple and specialized Field Types
entries.text: Choose the type for the business value, not for its appearance: Simple types: Text (single line or paragraph), Boolean, Currency, Date & time, Date only, Time only, Decimal, Integer, Percentage, Email, Phone, URL, Picklist, Address, User reference and Prediction · Email, Phone and URL are action-oriented: the stored value is displayed as a link that opens mail, a phone call or the browser · Fancy types: Attachment stores documents or files; Location accepts an address or automatic geolocation · Prediction requires decision nodes (Pega Process AI); Address shows country-specific fields after the Country selection · An Integer stores the value from its first non-zero digit. Use Text for numeric-looking values that need no arithmetic, such as identifiers with leading zeros

entries.title: Calculated value field
entries.text: A calculation sets a field from one or more input fields, for example an item total from unit price and quantity. Calculation occurs whenever a user updates an input, which removes manual arithmetic and reduces errors. The App Studio configuration shown in this topic marks the calculated field as read-only; users change its inputs rather than typing over the result.

entries.title: Recalculation
entries.text: Each calculation joins the application's calculation network. A calculated field can feed another calculation, so one input change (such as item quantity) can update several dependent fields. In the documented App Studio calculated-field configuration, the result is read-only. This UI setting does not establish whether the value is persisted or describe every declarative property configuration in Dev Studio.

entries.title: Three calculation approaches
entries.text: App Studio offers three approaches. Functions Sum of, Average of, Maximum of and Minimum of iterate over items in a data relationship and support Decimal, Currency and Integer fields. Expressions combine simple fields, fancy fields and data relationships. Decision tables test field values and return a result.

entries.title: Expression context
entries.text: Reference fields with the dot operator, which lists fields available in the current Case; prefix a field with its data relationship when needed. Operators include + - * /, parentheses, Boolean AND and OR. Text can be concatenated with quoted static text. Expressions are available for every simple type except Email, Phone and Picklist.

entries.title: Decision tables and where calculations live
entries.text: Create a custom decision table in App Studio only in a Constellation application, or reference a Dev Studio decision table that a System Architect has marked as a relevant record. Calculated fields are added on the Data model tab of either a Case Type or a data object, depending on the use case.

entries.title: View
entries.text: A reusable configuration of fields and other UI elements that collects or displays information. A View states what users need to see and when; Pega supplies a consistent, responsive presentation. Each field and its value is a data element that can be shown editable or read-only.

entries.title: Views, forms and field settings
entries.text: A form is a View that collects user input and processes work, usually with submit, cancel or navigation actions; not every View is a form. A Multi-step Form splits many fields into several focused Views. Other Views show read-only summaries or confirmations. For each task choose the fields, value types and order, and whether each field is editable or read-only, visible or hidden, required or optional.

entries.title: The Data Model
entries.text: Data modeling · Data records · Data Pages and the Visual Data Model · Integration Designer

entries.title: Data object (data type)
entries.text: A structure that groups related fields to describe a business entity (e.g., Customer with Name, Email, Phone). Reusable across all Case Types. In Dev Studio, a data object is called a data type and a field is a property.

entries.title: Why model data
entries.text: A well-designed Data Model promotes reuse, accuracy, consistency, and scalability. You model the data an application needs to complete work, then connect it to Case Types so the workflow has the right data at the right time.

entries.title: Sourcing data objects
entries.text: Data for a data object can be stored LOCALLY in the Pega database, or sourced from an EXTERNAL system of record (e.g., a client database or web service). Pega ships pre-configured objects (e.g., Address-Postal, Address-Email) to reuse or extend.

entries.title: Three design perspectives
entries.text: Conceptual: business entities, attributes and relationships. Logical: translate them into Pega data objects and fields. Physical: storage and integration details. Treat the conceptual model as evolving; involve stakeholders and have the LSA review the design before creating objects.

entries.title: Data Record
entries.text: The unique set of fields and values for one instance of a data object (e.g., one Customer = Ian / Mitchell / email / phone). Records live in a system of record — Pega DB or external.

entries.title: Value change vs. structure change
entries.text: Two types of data model changes with different implications: VALUE change (add a customer, update a phone number) — normal business operation; no process change needed · STRUCTURE change (adding/removing fields) — modifies the data object definition; requires careful planning

entries.title: pyGUID & local entry
entries.text: Use the Records tab for data configured to local Pega storage. Inspect its configured keys; a generated identifier such as pyGUID is not a workflow status. Do not assume every data object or external source uses the same identifier.

entries.title: Data Pages and the Visual Data Model
Data Page
entries.text: The bridge between a data object and its data — retrieves from a source and CACHES it in Clipboard memory. Hides integration details so developers work with sourced data without knowing where it lives.

entries.title: Pega Live Data & default Data Pages
entries.text: Data Pages separate application data usage from integration. The source describes three defaults for data objects configured to a system of record: single read, list read and a save page. These generated defaults are not the general taxonomy: Page/List structures, Read-only/Editable/Savable modes, and Thread/Requestor/Node scopes are separate settings.

entries.title: Simulation and production readiness
entries.text: A simulated source is temporary for development and testing. Connect and validate the final source before production; a diagram showing the object does not establish that its integration is ready.

entries.title: Visual Data Model
entries.text: The Visual Data Model shows objects and their relationships and supports field changes. Inspect configured cardinality rather than inferring physical foreign keys from a diagram.

entries.title: Data objects and Integrations landing page
entries.text: The Integration Designer is the single place in App Studio to see the application's data objects, their Data Pages, the systems of record (SOR) that source them, which Case Types reference each object (Referenced By), and simulated data sources.

entries.title: Visual Data Model & Integration Map
entries.text: From the Integration Designer you open the Visual Data Model (objects and relationships) and the Integration Map (a diagram of data objects and the systems of record from which they are sourced).

entries.title: Creating a data relationship
entries.text: Data objects · Data relationships

entries.title: Data object
entries.text: A structure that groups related fields to model a single entity and establish common context (e.g., a Customer grouping First name, Last name, Email, Phone). Data objects are reusable across an application's Case Types.

entries.title: Extending a data object
entries.text: You can extend a data object by referencing another data object; the referenced object's fields become part of the referencing object. Any object can be referenced once or many times.

entries.title: Reuse, inheritance and sourcing
entries.text: Prefer a suitable existing data object, extend it when necessary, and create a new one when none fits. Related objects can be nested. Source records locally in Pega or externally; Case participants can also enter Case-owned values without a system of record.

entries.title: Data relationship
entries.text: A container that associates related fields. Unlike a data object or field, it does NOT store data — it relates data-storing elements to the elements that need that data to resolve a Case (object↔Case, object↔object, or Case↔Case).

entries.title: Single record vs. list of records
entries.text: Two ways a data relationship references data: SINGLE RECORD — one related set of fields and values. · LIST OF RECORDS — multiple related records. A list Data Page uses pxResults; an embedded Page List uses its own property name and indexed entries.

entries.title: Embedded Data
entries.text: Use Embedded Data to capture Case-specific input. The values are owned by the Case rather than shared source records. Ownership does not specify a universal physical table layout; the Academy credit-card example describes a persisted keyed record associated with the Case.

entries.title: Data reference
entries.text: Use when you need to REUSE another data object from OUTSIDE the Case — data sourced from locally-stored Data Records or an external system of record (e.g., reference the facility where a medical appointment is booked).

entries.title: Case reference
entries.text: Use when you want to REUSE data from another CASE (e.g., a user selects from a list of Service Cases from the Service Case Type).

entries.title: Query
entries.text: Use for READ-ONLY access to information that is external to the Case; the Query Field Type allows PARAMETERS to query for specific data (e.g., return a medical professional's next appointment, or all appointments in a given time frame).

entries.title: Application user interface design
entries.text: Views (Constellation) · UI configuration in App Studio · Form views · Exploring fields · Model-driven UI controls · Portals and landing pages · Dynamic field behavior · Constellation form error handling

entries.title: View
entries.text: A reusable configuration of UI elements used to capture or display data for a Case. Constellation applications are built on a View-based UI architecture (the Constellation Ruleset), and Views are reusable across Case Types.

entries.title: Prescribed design system
entries.text: Constellation supplies reusable UI patterns and supported configuration choices. Its accessible defaults support implementation, but the finished application still needs accessibility testing.

entries.title: The four View types
entries.text: Full Page supplies Case or data-object context; Partial presents read-only information; List presents collections; Form supports task input and can include read-only content.

entries.title: Separation of Concerns
entries.text: The UI layer follows the Separation of Concerns principle — the application is divided into distinct parts, each addressing one concern — so front-end components connect cleanly to back-end APIs.

entries.title: Templates
entries.text: Generated Views use templates for layout and responsiveness. Template options depend on View type and location; test the resulting application with the intended users and devices.

entries.title: Full Page View
entries.text: Auto-added per new Case Type/data object; the three-pane visual framework representing a single Case. Edited on the UX tab. While authoring, the Preview shows only placeholder text — run a Case instance to preview with real data.

entries.title: Summary panel & Promoted Action
entries.text: The Summary panel sits upper-left and by default includes the Details View (showing Primary Fields) and Pulse View. A Promoted Action gives header access to a frequent Case-wide Action (e.g., Change Stage) — one per Case Type.

entries.title: Creating a Form View
entries.text: Two ways: on the Workflow tab (configuring a Step's View auto-creates a Form View) or on the UX tab's Other Views pane. Form Views use the Default template; Step-associated Views can also use the Hierarchical template.

entries.title: Layout
entries.text: Set 1–3 columns; two-column is best practice. Narrow inputs (Text single line, Currency) take one column; wider/any-height inputs (Rich Text Editor, Text area, Radio group, Checkbox, Booleans, Attachments) span two columns, keeping tabbing left-to-right.

entries.title: Field groups & multi-step vs hierarchical
entries.text: Three UI structuring concepts: FIELD GROUP — clusters related fields under one header; specific to the View (not reusable) · MULTI-STEP FORM — one Assignment split across MULTIPLE Views (linear; default for Create Stage) · HIERARCHICAL FORM — one Form View divided into Form-group tabs; useful when users can complete groups in any order

entries.title: Field settings
entries.text: Each field has a name and a Field Type that determines its format/validation and the control shown. You configure field settings (label, required, visibility, etc.) to tailor capture and presentation.

entries.title: Primary Fields
entries.text: Primary Fields identify important information and populate applicable standard Views, including Create, Edit, Details and List. A designation is not a required-field constraint; related data objects can supply their designated fields.

entries.title: Model-driven UI
entries.text: Field types and metadata determine the supported controls. Date fields use date input; Picklists support dropdown, search and radio presentation where appropriate. Model-driven does not mean every supported presentation is immutable.

entries.title: Patterns and consistency
entries.text: Because controls derive from the model via reusable patterns, the UI stays consistent and responsive across devices/channels, and adapts automatically when rules change. You can still customize a control's presentation where needed.

entries.title: Portal and task context
entries.text: A Portal is a web Channel. Configure its landing pages and navigation for its users; a task Form is a different interface within a Case. Responsive templates usually adapt the same UI to smaller screens.

entries.title: Presentation and processing
entries.text: Views present and collect information. Configure workflow processing with the appropriate Automations and Rules. Hiding a field does not authorize access, and client feedback does not replace server validation.

entries.title: User guidance
entries.text: Case status · Assignment instructions · Form instructions · Field settings and additional text · Case status property (legacy reference) · Constellation form error handling

entries.title: Case status
entries.text: Case status communicates progress. It uses Work-.pyStatusWork; configured Rules and notifications may refer to it, but the value does not by itself guarantee a particular notification.

entries.title: Status categories
entries.text: Four conventional Case status prefix categories: New — just created · Open — in progress · Pending — waiting on something or someone · Resolved — processing is complete, with no remaining open Assignments; examples include Resolved-Completed and Resolved-Rejected

entries.title: Setting status
entries.text: Configure status at meaningful Stages or Steps. A configured transition updates status; the final Stage’s resolution status applies after its Processes complete. Not every transition needs a different status.

entries.title: Guiding users: instructions, help text, and visual cues
Step (Assignment) instructions
entries.text: Text added to a Collect-information Step/Assignment that tells the user exactly what they must do to complete the Task. Instructions render at runtime on the assignment form, reducing confusion and errors.

entries.title: Contextual field text
entries.text: Additional text beside an input can clarify the expected value. Instruction text explains the task; neither replaces validation or authorization.

entries.title: Instruction overrides
entries.text: The Form can show the configured Step instructions, override them with task-specific text, or hide them. Choose guidance that helps the user complete the current Assignment.

entries.title: Routing Assignments to users
entries.text: Routing work · Work Queue role restrictions · Personas, operators and work access

entries.title: Routing
entries.text: Routing assigns responsibility for completing a Task to one or more users. It increases business efficiency by ensuring the most appropriate users receive the right work at the right time, orchestrating the workflow across teams.

entries.title: Worklist vs. Work Queue
entries.text: Two types of Assignment containers: WORKLIST — holds Assignments routed to a SPECIFIC user (operator) who owns the work · WORK QUEUE (work basket) — a SHARED queue for a team/Work Group; any qualified member can pull and complete the work

entries.title: Route to the current user
entries.text: Keep the Assignment with the user already working the Case — appropriate when the same person should continue.

entries.title: Route to a specific user
entries.text: Send the Assignment to a named operator's Worklist when one accountable individual must own the Task.

entries.title: Route to a Work Queue
entries.text: Send the Assignment to a shared Work Queue when any qualified member of a team can perform the work.

entries.title: Route using business logic
entries.text: Use configured business conditions to choose a user or Work Queue. A shared destination does not by itself select the least-loaded worker or enforce a skill policy.

entries.title: Separate destination from permission
entries.text: Work Groups organize shared work. Access Groups and Roles govern permissions. A Work Queue can require specified roles to process its Assignments; a Persona label alone is not a security boundary.

entries.title: Designing an approval Process
entries.text: Work approval · Cascading approvals · Reporting structure challenge (24.2) · Authority matrix challenge (24.2)

entries.title: Approval gate
entries.text: A user decision controls the approval path. Choose the reviewer and configure both outcomes.

entries.title: Default versus configured rejection
entries.text: Default rejection resolves the request as Resolved-Rejected. Revision requires an explicit destination; it is not implied by the word Reject.

entries.title: Outcome configuration
entries.text: Approval can continue work or select a Stage, with an optional status update. Rejection can resolve, continue, or select a Stage.

entries.title: Outside the application
entries.text: Enabled email or mobile approval lets the routed stakeholder decide outside the application. Check the recipient and enablement rather than assuming every Step sends these notifications.

entries.title: One decision or a series
entries.text: A single approval may use a named recipient, request-dependent routing, or a shared queue. Several required decisions need an explicit sequence or a cascade.

entries.title: Routing policy
entries.text: Choose between one particular reviewer and any eligible reviewer. Do not turn a shared Assignment into a claim that all queue members receive independent approvals.

entries.title: Cascade models
entries.text: Reporting structure follows manager relationships. Authority matrix supplies an ordered list and can include other departments. The next module explores both.

entries.title: Cascading approvals
entries.text: Cascading approvals · Work approval · Reporting structure challenge (24.2) · Authority matrix challenge (24.2)

entries.title: Ordered series
entries.text: A cascade represents several required decisions in order. It is not an any-one broadcast or majority vote.

entries.title: Two models
entries.text: Reporting structure uses management relationships; authority matrix uses a populated approver list.

entries.title: Design questions
entries.text: Which people are required? In what order? Does the number of management levels vary? Does anyone sit outside the reporting line?

entries.title: Rejected outcome
entries.text: Configure rejection flow explicitly. Resolution and revision are different policies; neither majority override nor restart should be assumed.

entries.title: Reporting source
entries.text: At runtime the current-user context and selected Reporting Manager or Workgroup Manager source identify the reviewer. Do not assume the original creator is always the current user.

entries.title: Depth
entries.text: One requests the immediate manager; All uses the whole hierarchy; Custom uses When Rules to select the required depth. Depth is not a promise of arbitrary middle-tier skipping.

entries.title: Challenge configuration
entries.text: The linked v7 reporting-structure challenge uses Dev Studio, an Approve/Reject Step, Cascading and Reporting structure. Its When conditions select one or two levels; the walkthrough targets Platform 24.2.

entries.title: Approver data
entries.text: An authority matrix needs a data structure of approvers. A Decision table, Data Page, Activity or Data Transform can populate it; a table is one supported approach.

entries.title: Decision table example
entries.text: The linked v7 challenge configures a Page List and an approver property, then a Decision table that appends required recipients. Evaluate all rows allows multiple matching results.

entries.title: Other departments
entries.text: Use the matrix when required reviewers are outside the chosen management line. List ordering still matters; population rules are not a parallel voting mechanism.

entries.title: Completing work on time
entries.text: Service Level Agreements · Setting goals and deadlines · Enforcing SLAs challenge (24.2) · Passed deadline interval

entries.title: Service-Level Agreement (SLA)
entries.text: Establishes a work-completion deadline to enforce on-time performance. Can be defined on an ASSIGNMENT or the overall CASE, and uses MILESTONES (goal, then deadline) to mark expected turnaround times.

entries.title: Goal vs. Deadline
entries.text: Goal and deadline use the SLA’s configured start reference. Case-resolution configuration can refer to this Case, its parent or the top-level Case. GOAL — desired completion time, normally the earlier target; calculate from the configured start reference · DEADLINE — the longest time work MAY take before it is 'late'

entries.title: Escalation actions at milestones
entries.text: When a milestone is missed, the SLA can increase Urgency AND run an escalation: NOTIFY (assignee, manager, participants, or Case creator), REASSIGN to another user/queue, or RESOLVE the Case. Repeating post-deadline escalation is covered by the passed deadline interval.

entries.title: Three timed responses: worked example
entries.text: For a calendar-time policy, Goal at day 3 can notify; Deadline at day 7 can reassign; a passed deadline interval of three days with one event can resolve still-open work at day 10. Configure every action explicitly and account for processing delay and calendars. The post-deadline Rule configuration is covered in SA-M16.

entries.title: Urgency (Case vs. Assignment)
entries.text: Urgency is numeric priority with maximum 100: CASE Urgency — priority of the Case itself · ASSIGNMENT Urgency — initial value equals Case Urgency (default 10); Stage/Process-level SLA adjustments affect Case Urgency

entries.title: Setting and increasing Urgency
entries.text: Set the Case Type’s initial urgency in Settings. Updating a Case’s urgency supplies the new value for new Assignments, not existing ones. This does not prevent an existing Assignment’s own SLA from adjusting its urgency.

entries.title: Get Next Work
entries.text: Pega prioritizes work by Urgency. GET NEXT WORK hands users the highest-Urgency Assignment they can perform first, so high-priority work finishes on time. Design SLAs/Urgency so the right work outranks the rest.
