entries.text: The Security Checklist · Security policies · User authentication and authorization

entries.title: AIC Triad
entries.text: Availability, Integrity, Confidentiality — Pega's shared security goal. Unauthorized individuals cannot access or modify the application or its data. Authorized individuals only access what they need to perform their jobs.

entries.title: Security Checklist
entries.text: A guideline Rule instance automatically installed per app version to harden Pega applications. Tasks are organized by timing and key area: monitoring, authentication, authorization, auditing, production testing. Not all tasks are required for every app.

entries.title: Security Checklist — enforcement
entries.text: The source describes Deployment Manager blocking production promotion when the Security Checklist is incomplete. Applicable tasks depend on the application and deployment; not every listed task applies to every release.

entries.title: Guardrail compliance — #1 security requirement
entries.text: The source emphasizes guardrail compliance because custom code can bypass built-in security enforcement. Use platform security features; do not treat compliance as a replacement for MFA, authorization design or security testing.

entries.title: Two types of security
entries.text: Pega security operates at two distinct layers: Application-level security: protects from outsiders and unauthorized users (passwords, auth policies, MFA, third-party tools) · Feature security: controls what authorized users can and cannot access within the app (RBAC, ABAC, CBAC)

entries.title: Where to configure Security Policies
entries.text: The earlier Security policies v5 source documents these navigation routes; v6 focuses on policy behavior. Verify the interface in the target version: App Studio: Authentication landing page → Security Policies tab · Dev Studio: Configure → Org & Security → Authentication → Security Policies (applies to the entire Pega Platform server) · ⚠ CAUTION: authentication service settings may OVERRIDE Security Policy page settings

entries.title: Security Policy: Password
entries.text: Sets rules for password strength: Minimum length · Required character types (uppercase, digits, symbols) · Restrictions on predictable or reused passwords

entries.title: Security Policy: CAPTCHA
entries.text: Presents a challenge on initial login or after failed login attempts. Can use a custom or default CAPTCHA.

entries.title: Security Policies — Access Control and Monitoring
Security Policy: Lockout
entries.text: Controls account lockout behavior after failed logins: Enabled penalty: configure a failed-attempt threshold and initial seconds; repeat failures escalate the penalty. · Disabled penalty: configure failed-attempt count and lock duration in minutes. Disabling the penalty option does not mean all lockout protection disappears.

entries.title: Security Policy: Audit
entries.text: Controls the level of detail recorded in the system log for security-related events.

entries.title: Security Policy: Multi-factor Authentication (MFA)
entries.text: The built-in OTP policy delivers a time-limited code by email or SMS. MFA is broader than this delivery mechanism; 2FA uses two factors. The source lists knowledge, possession and an inherent characteristic such as a fingerprint.

entries.title: Security Policy: Operator disablement
entries.text: Automatically disables access for users who have been inactive for a specified number of days. An exclusion list can protect users who still require access despite inactivity.

entries.title: Authentication — WHO can access
entries.text: Authentication verifies identity for application and service access. An Operator ID is commonly an email address, but not necessarily one. SAML, OpenID Connect and token credentials support SSO; the authentication service configures applicable policies.

entries.title: Authorization — WHAT users can do
entries.text: Controls what authenticated users can access and perform within the application. Three models: RBAC, ABAC, and CBAC.

entries.title: Authorization model: RBAC
entries.text: RBAC assigns permissions through user Roles. It can complement other authorization models; it is not automatically sufficient for every security requirement.

entries.title: Authorization model: ABAC
entries.text: Attribute-Based Access Control. Access is determined by comparing object characteristics (Case, field, document) to user attributes. More granular than RBAC — the same role can have different access depending on contextual attributes.

entries.title: Authorization model: CBAC
entries.text: Client-Based Access Control. Tracks and processes requests to view, update, or remove personal customer data. Designed to address GDPR and similar data privacy regulations.

entries.title: Managing application access
entries.text: Application access · Access control

entries.title: Personas, Access Roles, and Access Groups
Persona
entries.text: Defines how users align with an application by BUSINESS OUTCOMES. Example: 'Loan Applicant' and 'Loan Officer' have different goals in the process. Creating a Persona in App Studio auto-creates a corresponding Access Group in Dev Studio.

entries.title: Role
entries.text: Defines how users INTERACT with the application. Example: Manager, User. Each Role has a default Channel interface — this determines which screen users see upon login.

entries.title: Access Role
entries.text: Categorizes users by job function. For each Access Role, you configure permissions to control Actions on instances of a specific class. Example: 'Manager' and 'User' can be separate Access Roles with different permissions.

entries.title: Access Group
entries.text: Represents a group of privileges. Each Access Group references one or more Access Roles. Multiple Access Groups can reference the same application for different access levels and align with roles assignable to users in App Studio.

entries.title: Access Group — conflicting permissions rule
entries.text: In the lesson’s ordinary conflicting-role example, the most permissive setting applies. Do not extend this example into a promise that other security checks, Access Deny conditions or authorization models are bypassed.

entries.title: ARO — Access of Role to Object
entries.text: Access of Role to Object binds an Access Role to permissions for a class. Permissions can allow actions or specify No Access; the record is not limited to unconditional grants.

entries.title: Access Deny
entries.text: Access Deny supplies explicit denial over the applicable ARO permission. Evaluate its conditions and production-level settings; do not assume every role’s grant and every denial combine identically in all configurations.

entries.title: Best practice: use management tools, not direct record edits
entries.text: Prefer App Studio User management when sufficient. Some permissions, including Case deletion, require Access Manager. Both simplify the underlying role permissions: App Studio: Users → User management (Persona access landing page) · Dev Studio: Configure → Org & Security → Access Manager

entries.title: Production levels (on-premises)
entries.text: On-premises levels: 5 Production, 4 Staging, 3 Quality assurance, 2 Development, 1 Sandbox. Access value 0 denies; otherwise the permission value must be at least the system production level. A value of 2 can permit Development while denying Production.

entries.title: Configuring UI elements
entries.text: Controls and presentation · Dynamic functionality on UI elements

entries.title: Examples of out-of-the-box controls
entries.text: The source lists Autocomplete, Check boxes, Drop-down lists, Links, Rich-text editors and Text input. This is an illustrative list, not proof that every unlisted control is unsupported or requires custom development.

entries.title: Themes
entries.text: Themes style UI elements consistently across the application. The source illustrates the Pegasus theme. Visibility, disabling and required-value behavior use separate dynamic configuration.

entries.title: Dynamic UI — purpose
entries.text: Designing UI elements to adapt according to user choices. Provides: Real-time response to end-user behavior · Robust functionality for most interactions · Reduced visual clutter · Fewer full-page refreshes for improved responsiveness

entries.title: Visible attribute
entries.text: Controls whether a UI element is shown: Default: Always. · Source table: Always, Custom Condition, When Rule, If not blank, If not zero.

entries.title: Disabled attribute
entries.text: Disabled prevents interaction with the configured field. This UI behavior does not replace server-side authorization or data integrity checks. Default: Never (always editable) · Options: Never | Always (always read-only) | Custom Condition | When Rule

entries.title: Required attribute
entries.text: Controls whether a field must be filled before the form submits: Default: Never (optional) · Options: Never | Always | Custom Condition (required when expression is true) | When Rule · The source lists If not blank and If not zero under Visible, not under Required or Disabled.

entries.title: Custom Condition vs When Rule
entries.text: Two ways to configure conditional display in Dynamic UI: CUSTOM CONDITION — for SHORT, one-off expressions (e.g., check one dropdown value) · WHEN RULE — for COMPLEX or REUSABLE conditions shared across multiple UI elements

entries.title: 'If not blank' and 'If not zero' — Visible ONLY
entries.text: 'If not blank' shows an element only when the field value is not blank. 'If not zero' shows when the value is not zero. These options appear ONLY under the Visible attribute — not under Disabled or Required.

entries.title: Configuring Portal content
entries.text: Channel interfaces · Portals and landing pages · Dashboards · Out-of-the-box landing page widgets · Themes and styles for Constellation applications

entries.title: Channel interface
entries.text: A Channel allows you to create tailored interactive UIs for specific interaction types. Examples: messaging service, voice service, web portal, mobile portal. Channels are created from templates with predefined layouts and navigation.

entries.title: Conversational Channels
entries.text: Facebook Messenger, WhatsApp, Apple Messages, SMS/MMS (Twilio), Embedded chat window, Amazon Alexa, Email. IVA (Intelligent Virtual Assistant): understands user intent across channels. Email Bot: auto-detects email intent and routes.

entries.title: Channels landing page
entries.text: Create, view, and edit all Channel interfaces from one place. Download additional Channels from Pega Marketplace. Lock icon on a Channel = the Channel component has NOT yet been added to the application (not a permission restriction).

entries.title: Persona-Channel associations in Case lifecycle
entries.text: Drafting Persona-Channel associations in the Case Life Cycle does not configure access. The source describes all pages as the default for a Persona; restrict the appropriate Portal through Portal configuration, rather than assuming lifecycle labels grant or restrict access.

entries.title: 2 Portal types in Constellation
entries.text: A Portal is a web Channel that supports browser access on desktop and mobile. Choose a Portal type for the user profile; use configured privileges and visibility in one Portal, or provide separate Portals. Standard work Portals: for professional users completing complex, recurring workflows requiring collaboration and data analysis · Self-service Portals: minimalistic design with a guided experience for simple, goal-oriented tasks

entries.title: Landing pages
entries.text: Consolidate Case-related information. Contain data lists, Widgets, Views, and Insights. Out-of-the-box pages: Dashboard, Home, Explore Data, My Work, Self-service Main page. Landing pages added to the Portal menu appear in Portal navigation.

entries.title: Landing page templates
entries.text: 4 templates: Default page (column-based with/without banner), Tabbed page, Dashboard page, Inline Dashboard page. The Default page supports both column-based layout and dynamic layout (drag, drop, and resize widgets).

entries.title: Dashboard structure
entries.text: Dashboard = a landing page accessed in the Portal. Contains Widgets that consolidate summary info and KPIs. A Template divides the work area into Regions (containers for widgets). Each Persona gets a tailored dashboard view.

entries.title: Dashboard visibility — 3 options
entries.text: Three visibility levels for dashboards: Private: only the creator sees it · Shared — Users with Access: all users or a specific Access Group · Public: all users in the application

entries.title: Widget locations
entries.text: Widgets appear in two places: Portal landing pages AND Full Case View (Utilities pane). The Utilities pane is HIDDEN when no Widgets are added — it doesn't show an empty state.

entries.title: Portal landing page widgets
entries.text: The v3 topic lists these Portal Widget examples: Pulse: team collaboration (posts, comments, attachments) — available in landing pages AND Full Case View · To do: configurable to show My Worklist, team members, or Work Queue · App announcement: custom welcome text + link

entries.title: Home landing page defaults
entries.text: The source’s Home example contains Pulse, To do and App announcement. Do not treat this illustration as a guarantee that every configured Portal has the same defaults.

entries.title: Utilities pane widgets (Full Case View)
entries.text: The source lists Attachments, Case operator, Tags, GenAI Coach, Followers, Prediction, Stakeholders and Related Cases as Utilities examples. Pulse is also supported in the Full Case View. This is not an exhaustive support matrix.

entries.title: 4 ready-to-use Constellation themes
entries.text: Pegasus, Aries, Self-Service, Bootes. MUST SAVE UNDER A NEW NAME before customizing any of them — you cannot edit the original built-in themes directly. Configure at App Studio → Settings → Themes. The Themes landing page also provides accessibility configurations.

entries.title: Enterprise layer = COE layer
entries.text: The source also calls the Enterprise layer a COE layer. Reuse shared themes, fonts, icons and templates across applications. UI elements can be inherited, but themes do not support inheritance: share high-level design tokens, or save a specialized theme copy into a higher Ruleset.

entries.title: Design tokens
entries.text: Store component styling in one central place. The system auto-generates platform-specific styling from those tokens, ensuring visual consistency across mobile, desktop, and other surfaces. All Constellation library components use design tokens.

entries.title: Application development management
entries.text: Agile Workbench · Release management with Pega Platform · Agile development best practices

entries.title: Application profile & Developer Assistant
entries.text: Application profile tracks development work; Developer Assistant organizes work and provides AI-assisted aids. The source names Guidance, Knowledge, Work and Checklists tabs without saying every tab is independently AI-powered. Application profile: up-to-date view of all work items, features, and status · Developer Assistant pane: AI-powered aids with 4 tabs — Guidance, Knowledge, Work, Checklists

entries.title: Features and subfeatures
entries.text: Features = capabilities the application supports. Subfeatures = features nested within a feature. When you create a new Case Type, Pega automatically creates a feature with the same name. Work items are associated with features or subfeatures.

entries.title: 3 work item types
entries.text: Work items tracked in the Application profile: Stories (User stories): describe business requirements; make up the majority of development work; can be uploaded from Excel in bulk · Bugs: document feature defects; major bugs are addressed before minor ones · Feedback items: enhancement requests identified during playback sessions

entries.title: Two ways to change work item status
entries.text: To do, Doing and Done are the listed statuses. Change status by dragging the card to a column or using the Status list on the work item itself.

entries.title: Agile Workbench integrations
entries.text: Integrates with Agile Studio (expanded functionality: release management, progress tracking, team capacity, analytics). Also integrates with external tools: Jira, CA Agile Central — allowing customers to use their existing infrastructure.

entries.title: DevOps
entries.text: A collaborative practice between development, quality, and operations: Goal: deliver high-quality software in an automated, agile way · Reduces time to market without compromising quality · CI/CD pipeline = the automated process from development through testing to deployment

entries.title: Continuous Integration (CI)
entries.text: Developers frequently check in changes. Automated build verifies each change — identifies issues EARLY. 'Ready to share' step: new changes work with existing app. 'Integrate changes' step: critical tests pass → changes published to development repository.

entries.title: Continuous Delivery (CD)
entries.text: The deployment pipeline stages after CI: Rigorous automated regression testing · Changes deployed to staging for further testing · 'Ready to accept': acceptance criteria tests pass · 'Ready to deploy': performance and compatibility tests pass · Deploy: validates in preproduction → production → post-deployment tests with rollback option

entries.title: Deployment Manager
entries.text: Deployment Manager orchestrates Pega CI/CD. The source describes Admin Studio for designing and managing pipelines and a configured App Studio integration for Publishing. Manage pipelines through Admin Studio in the described workflow. · After integration, App Studio Settings > Versions exposes the application pipeline for Publishing. · Automate Branch merging, packaging and environment promotion. · The source lists Jenkins and Microsoft Azure DevOps as third-party examples.

entries.title: 3 Pega agile best practices
entries.text: ① Real-time updates: frequent small-scope development iterations. ② Testing: continuous validation to identify and address issues early. ③ Branches: concurrent team development environment to maximize productivity.

entries.title: CI best practices
entries.text: Best practices for Continuous Integration in Pega: Test early and often: run Pega unit tests + critical integration tests before packaging · If tests fail → STOP the release pipeline until fixed · Automate: trigger merges and builds via Deployment Manager · Update the referenced product Rule (Rule-Admin-Product). · Maintain deployable version history by publishing exported application archives to a repository.

entries.title: CD best practices
entries.text: ① Create test environments (Docker/UAT). ② Run regression tests — UI and service layer. ③ Use version control: target specific Ruleset versions for production. ④ Define a rollback strategy. ⑤ Annotate passing packages as deployment-ready.

entries.title: DevOps in Pega Platform
entries.text: Unit tests · Creating unit test Cases · Test coverage

entries.title: Unit testing — purpose
entries.text: Test individual Rules with defined inputs to isolate configuration errors. The earlier Unit tests v5 topic describes Actions > Run on a supported Rule form in Dev Studio; available interfaces depend on the Rule type.

entries.title: Binary file Rules — cannot be unit tested
entries.text: Unit tests v5 identifies binary file Rules as lacking a unit-test Run option. This is a version-scoped source detail, not a universal statement about every testing mechanism.

entries.title: Rule resolution applies during unit testing
entries.text: Normal Rule Resolution selects the applicable Rule in the test context. A higher version can run when eligible; version number alone does not override Ruleset availability, class and other resolution criteria.

entries.title: Test case and assertions
entries.text: A reusable test compares actual results with assertions. The current v6 examples include Property, Decision result, Expected run time and Page. Assertion availability depends on the Rule type.

entries.title: Test suites
entries.text: Unit tests v5 describes sequential bulk suite execution and a Ruleset configured for test storage. This does not imply test dependencies: keep tests portable and independent. Configure execution through PegaUnit and run at least on each merge/check-in.

entries.title: High-priority vs low-priority test candidates
entries.text: Test prioritization for Pega Unit Testing: HIGH-PRIORITY — predictable results, executed frequently, complex logic, Rules with wide usage · LOW-PRIORITY automation examples: frequent maintenance, easy manual testing, complexity that resists automation, or database persistence. This is prioritization, not a reason to omit risk-based testing.

entries.title: Test cases for Rules
entries.text: Convert a unit test run into a reusable test case. Define assertions (expected results). When the test case runs, results are compared to assertions — mismatch → test FAILS.

entries.title: Test cases for Processes and Case Types
entries.text: Actions → Record test Case (toolbar) → step through the flow entering input → click 'Create test Case' (lower-right) to save the recording. Modify pxCapturePropertyIgnore Data Transform to EXCLUDE unwanted properties from the test.

entries.title: v8.5+ restriction on Case Type test recording
entries.text: Creating unit test Cases v7 retains the 8.5+ restriction for running/recording a process with a Create Stage in a new Case Type. It describes an exception for migrated pre-8.5 Case Types; it does not guarantee all other recording prerequisites.

entries.title: Test Pyramid
entries.text: Industry best practice for test strategy. Bottom of pyramid (unit tests): least expensive, easiest to maintain, fastest, should be the MOST tests. Top (end-to-end tests): most expensive, hardest to maintain, slowest, fewest tests. Higher up = higher cost.

entries.title: Test coverage tool
entries.text: Coverage reports identify executable Rules exercised or not exercised in included applications. Application-level reports combine multiple users; user-level results appear in Coverage history. A covered Rule is not proof that every internal path was tested.

entries.title: Test coverage configuration
entries.text: Distinguish suite execution, coverage contribution and session initiation: SysAdm4: role required by this topic to run test suites. · SysAdm4 or User4: tests can contribute to coverage. · pzStartOrStopMasterAppRuleCoverage: privilege required to initiate application-level coverage. · Application-level results: Application Quality Dashboard; user-level results: Coverage history. Merge application-level reports for consolidated results.

entries.title: Debugging application errors
entries.text: The Tracer · Tracer settings management · Developer tools for examining applications

entries.title: The Tracer — Overview and Reading Events
Tracer — purpose and access
entries.text: Troubleshooting tool that traces events that led to an error during application runtime. Access: App Studio → hover lower-right corner → Toggle runtime toolbar. OR Dev Studio → Developer toolbar.

entries.title: Tracer event color codes
entries.text: Each event is logged as a separate row. Gray = Activity processing. Orange = Events from flow, Decision, or declarative Rules. Light blue = PegaRULES database and cache operations.

entries.title: Status: Good vs Fail
entries.text: Good and Fail describe processing-step outcomes, not unit-test assertion statuses. GOOD — step completed successfully · FAIL — error occurred; a failed step may be only the LAST in a chain — trace backwards to find the root cause

entries.title: Constellation request IDs
entries.text: Constellation uses stateless DX API requests. The Tracer results organize events by request ID to distinguish simultaneously active requests.

entries.title: Performance and limits
entries.text: Key Tracer constraints to know before use: ⚠ CAUTION: Tracer is resource-intensive and DRAMATICALLY slows application performance · Only ONE Tracer per operator, per node is allowed · Pause logging until ready to trace the specific section · Toolbar (upper-right corner): Pause, Clear, Save buttons

entries.title: Refining event logging
entries.text: Filter options to narrow Tracer output: Filter by: event, event type, Ruleset, break Conditions · Can exclude local variables or view only activities (not their steps) · Selection options: Events to Trace, Break Conditions, General Options, Event Types to Trace, Rulesets to Trace

entries.title: Break Conditions
entries.text: A Tracer settings option (NOT a toolbar button). Stops the Tracer automatically when the system generates an error. Different from Breakpoints — Break Conditions are passive error-triggered stops; Breakpoints are manually placed on specific activities.

entries.title: Breakpoints
entries.text: In a supported tracing context, a breakpoint pauses tracing and its processing thread at the configured activity event. Resume with Play; the source also describes automatic resumption after an hour. Breakpoints and Watch are unsupported for Service Rules and Constellation applications.

entries.title: Watch Function
entries.text: Monitors specific property value(s) for changes. Useful for tracing calculation consistency and value-change patterns. Tracer highlights the property change in YELLOW and shows the Property Inspector. NOT supported for Service Rules and Constellation applications.

entries.title: React DevTools
entries.text: Browser extension; adds Components tab to console. Select any element to highlight screen. Run $r.props.getPConnect() to view component metadata. Used for Constellation application UI debugging.

entries.title: Redux DevTools
entries.text: Free browser plugin; adds Redux tab. Logs every action (type and payload). Visualizes state changes. Inspect state tree at any point. Client-side Data Pages are NOT in Redux — stored in the datastore.

entries.title: Client-side Data Pages — NOT in Redux
entries.text: Client-cached Data Pages reside in the application datastore, not Redux. PCore.getDataPageUtils() logs cached-page information. PCore/PConnect APIs are unavailable in the App Studio shell; launch the Portal from Dev Studio for these methods.

entries.title: Xray, DebugPegaAPI, and UI Inspector
entries.text: Three supplementary debugging tools: Xray overlays screen metadata, field metadata and state properties. · DebugPegaAPI is a dynamic system setting: verbose DX API inputs, actions, error fields/descriptions/codes and exception numbers in Pega logs. · UI Inspector exposes UI hierarchy, metadata, field properties and View properties.

entries.title: Exploring application data with Insights
entries.text: The Explore Data landing page · Applying Insights across Pega Platform components · Troubleshooting Insights issues

entries.title: Explore Data landing page
entries.text: A View-based landing page where you can explore and analyze application data. Query data, then sort, filter, and group results. It is the preferred data exploration tool for Constellation design system applications.

entries.title: Insights — definition
entries.text: Rules that Pega Platform uses to transform data queries into tables or visualizations (lists or interactive charts). Insights can be saved and shared between users. Created via the Explore Data landing page.

entries.title: Table-based Insights
entries.text: Display a custom data query as a table on the Explore Data landing page. You can create a new table-based Insight or select a previously-created one to view or modify.

entries.title: Chart-based Insights
entries.text: Visualize a custom data query as a chart (e.g., bar, line). You can create a new chart-based Insight or select a previously-created one to view or modify.

entries.title: Simple value chart — Measures only
entries.text: A chart sub-type providing a high-level summary of data. To configure: in the Fields section, select fields in the Measures area ONLY. The Display as list then updates to include simple value options.

entries.title: Traditional UI + Explore Data
entries.text: For apps built with Traditional UI architecture, you must enable the option to 'use Constellation UI to render landing pages' before you can use Explore Data.

entries.title: Insights in full Page Case Views
entries.text: Add Insights to tabs in a full Page Case View. The source explicitly excludes adding them directly to a View. For example, the Order Details tab can show an order-trend chart.

entries.title: Insights in Portal landing pages
entries.text: Use the Portal configuration pane to place an existing public Insight in a landing-page region alongside fields, Views and Widgets. Add the landing page to Portal navigation for discoverability.

entries.title: Dashboards — definition
entries.text: Dashboards arrange multiple Insights using templates. The Dashboards landing page lists available dashboards, including Work metrics. It is available by default in App Studio and Work Portals and is not configured through the Portal authoring page.

entries.title: Dashboard visibility settings
entries.text: Three visibility levels for dashboards: Private: visible only to you · Shared with Access Group: visible to members of that Access Group · Public: accessible to all users in the application

entries.title: Promoted filter
entries.text: A filter added to a dashboard that applies across ALL Insights in that dashboard. Helps users refine data views across multiple Insights simultaneously. Example: adding 'Item Category' filter to a dashboard with 3 sales Insights.

entries.title: Repeated login prompts
entries.text: Troubleshooting: login loop issue: CAUSE: inappropriate access token lifetime · FIX: update the token lifetime to match session requirements

entries.title: Number separators confuse users
entries.text: Troubleshooting: number formatting issue: CAUSE: default UI controls display numbers with separators (e.g., 1,000) · FIX: modify UI controls to remove separators

entries.title: Wrong object name in Explore Data list
entries.text: Troubleshooting: incorrect data object name displayed: CAUSE: Pega sources object names from the class short description · FIX: update the class short description to the correct name

entries.title: Missing columns: optimization and relevant records
entries.text: A missing column can indicate configuration or stale browser state; the source does not identify permissions as the typical cause. If absent from Show/hide columns, optimize the backing property in parent classes and the specific Class. · If the property is not a relevant record, mark it relevant in Dev Studio. · Check stale browser state and Portal/customization/authentication configuration as appropriate.

entries.title: Localizing application content
entries.text: Localization · Design considerations for localization

entries.title: Localization — 3 aspects
entries.text: Adapts an application for a specific language or region by: (1) translating text · (2) converting locale-specific components (currency symbols, calendar settings) · (3) adapting the UI for right-to-left (RTL) text direction if relevant

entries.title: Locale priority
entries.text: Pega first checks the browser locale. If the operator profile specifies a different locale, the profile locale takes precedence. If no Ruleset exists for the selected locale, the UI displays English (default).

entries.title: Language packs
entries.text: A translated Ruleset with values for fields that typically appear in every application (button labels, prompts). Import via the Localization landing page. The pack must match the same version AND UI architecture (e.g., Constellation v8.8).

entries.title: Localization process — 3 steps
entries.text: Create a package, translate it and import it on the App Studio Localization page. Depending on the content, translation uses JSON/Excel and packaged Paragraph HTML. GenAI-assisted text needs review. Test each target locale before relying on automatic Ruleset selection.

entries.title: Verifying localization
entries.text: Change the current operator locale in Dev Studio and test the application. A fresh login may be needed. Review messages and correspondence as well as visible labels; correct missing translations and test again.

entries.title: Localization limitations in Constellation
entries.text: What can and cannot be localized in Constellation: CAN localize: labels, captions, tooltips, instructions in Views and Portals · CANNOT localize: Decision tables and decision trees, Case Statuses, radio buttons and drop-down controls in a table

entries.title: Studio scope
entries.text: App Studio and generated user Portals support localization. Dev Studio is not fully localized; untranslated developer content does not alone prove the user Portal translation failed.

entries.title: Picklist properties — omitted from package
entries.text: When generating a translation package, Pega OMITS local properties with multiple values (e.g., picklist properties). You must add these manually by editing the localization file in Dev Studio.

entries.title: Dynamic values — must also be localized
entries.text: Translate the phrase around a dynamic placeholder, preserving its substitution purpose. The topic uses a pyMessages phrase with a user-name placeholder; changing the customer name itself is not phrase translation.

entries.title: Paragraph instructions — packaged HTML, manual translation
entries.text: Step-instruction Paragraph text is included in the ZIP as source HTML in paragraph/base. Translate the corresponding paragraph/translated HTML, upload the compressed package and test the target locale. Manual translation does not mean absence from the package.

entries.title: Data Page controls — not auto-included
entries.text: For Data Page-backed radio/drop-down entries, add the missing values as separate rows in the Additional text localization record, then rebuild and import the package. If the Data Page is absent from Views, create its localization Rule manually. This is a package omission, not a blanket localization ban.

entries.title: Creating a Pega Platform application
entries.text: Class hierarchy structure · Modular architecture and Enterprise reuse · New Pega Platform applications

entries.title: Decision rule
entries.text: Place assets at their reuse scope: enterprise-wide → Organization; regional or brand-wide → optional Division; unit-wide → optional Unit (requires Division); a specific business application → Implementation. Platform supplies the foundation. Constellation starts with the Data Model and generates a prescribed experience; its design system, architecture, DX API and business engine have distinct roles.

entries.title: Decision rule
entries.text: Keep Enterprise lean. Put reusable customer data, single-system integration and utility capabilities in modules; place workflow-specific Cases in business applications. Specialize geographic or segment differences in innovation applications. Reuse modules through built-on applications or the wizard. Prefer parameters, extension points and Configuration Sets to copies; shared changes affect consumers.

entries.title: Decision rule
entries.text: Blueprint captures a collaborative application design: Case Types, lifecycle, data and Personas. App Studio’s New Application wizard turns an existing or newly created Blueprint into an initial application. Treat generated design as a starting point to review against requirements. Reusable designs speed repeated application creation.

entries.title: Application versioning
entries.text: Application versioning

entries.title: Decision rule
entries.text: Version format is major-minor-patch. Lock and roll creates an empty higher version for incremental edits; untouched Rules remain resolved from accessible earlier versions. Skimming consolidates latest eligible Rules from a selected major into a higher minor or major. Available, Final and Blocked are copied; Not Available is excluded; Withdrawn survives minor skims only. Check in work before versioning. New major/minor releases require application and Access Group updates; patch changes typically do not.

entries.title: Application Rulesets
entries.text: Application and production Rulesets · Ruleset validation · The Ruleset list

entries.title: Decision rule
entries.text: Rulesets package related Rules. Application Rulesets define application behavior; organizational Rulesets support reuse. Int conventionally groups integration Rules. Production Rulesets support controlled maintenance in production, including delegation; keep a version unlocked and give intended operators access through their Access Groups.

entries.title: Decision rule
entries.text: AV validates references against the defining application and its built-on stack. RV uses explicit version prerequisites and their prerequisites; prerequisite cycles are invalid. Validation happens at design time, not as runtime ranking. Use RV for portable shared assets. Revalidate after changes to built-on applications or the Ruleset list.

entries.title: Decision rule
entries.text: At login, Pega starts from the Access Group’s versioned application and walks its built-on applications to assemble the runtime stack. Higher entries have precedence within Rule resolution. Eligible developers also get a personal Ruleset for checked-out Rules at the top. Inspect Operator Profile when two users see different behavior.

entries.title: Circumstancing Case processing
entries.text: Circumstancing · Circumstance Rules · Single-variable circumstancing · Multi-variant circumstancing

entries.title: Decision rule
entries.text: Keep normal behavior in a base Rule and implement focused exceptions as variants. Rule resolution chooses the applicable behavior without duplicating the whole Process. Use this when the same Rule purpose needs situational differences.

entries.title: Decision rule
entries.text: Choose by the requirement: one property → single-variable; a combination → multi-variant; a Case date → date-property; today’s date/time → as-of. If no eligible variant matches, normal behavior comes from the base Rule.

entries.title: Decision rule
entries.text: Specify a property and matching value for one-variable exceptions. A date property evaluates Case data; as-of evaluates system time. A higher accessible Rule marked Base resets earlier instances in the same major with lower minor/patch versions. Withdrawing a circumstanced instance removes that variant, not every sibling. Inspect variants in Application Explorer or the Rule header.

entries.title: Decision rule
entries.text: The template declares the properties to evaluate; a definition supplies conditions for their values. Attach the template/definition to a specialized Rule. A template alone does not provide the exception’s matching values. Test matching and nonmatching combinations.

entries.title: Rule resolution
entries.text: Rule resolution · Rule filtering by purpose · Remaining Rule candidates and ranking · The Rule resolution process · Rule resolution process and Rule availability

entries.title: Decision rule
entries.text: Rule resolution chooses behavior for a purpose in the current requestor context. A Rule being saved in the database does not make it accessible or the winner. Diagnose the class, runtime Ruleset stack, version, circumstance and availability together.

entries.title: Decision rule
entries.text: Purpose combines Rule name and Rule type. Candidate filtering excludes Not Available instances, inapplicable Rulesets/versions and classes outside the inheritance path. Do not compare version numbers until the candidates are eligible.

entries.title: Decision rule
entries.text: Ranking considers class, Ruleset, circumstance/date qualifiers and version. An unqualified default provides fallback; lower-ranked candidates below it are discarded. Withdrawal removes matching same-class/purpose instances at or below its version in its Ruleset, while eligible other scopes remain. The cache retains candidates for later selection.

entries.title: Decision rule
entries.text: Check the cache, build candidates on a miss, find the best matching eligible circumstance or default, then check blocking and authorization. Equally correct matches cause a duplicate-Rule error. A candidate being cached does not guarantee it runs.

entries.title: Rule resolution process and Rule availability
Decision rule
entries.text: Available can run. Final can run but prevents same-name overrides in another Ruleset; a higher version in its own Ruleset is the exception. Not Available is skipped. A selected unqualified Blocked Rule stops execution. Withdrawn suppresses its matching earlier scope and allows other eligible fallback. Circumstanced Blocked/Withdrawn variants are excluded while remaining siblings can be considered.

entries.title: Application migration
entries.text: Product Rule · Exporting an application, product Rule, or Ruleset using the Export wizard

entries.title: Decision rule
entries.text: A Product Rule (RAP) is the migration manifest; its generated ZIP/JAR archive carries the selected contents. Use Packaging wizard and Preview to verify Rules, associated data and required dependencies. Standard platform assets usually already exist on the target. A data instance’s Ruleset association supports packaging, not runtime access control. Accessible imported Rules may execute before the whole import finishes.

entries.title: Exporting an application, product Rule, or Ruleset using the Export wizard
Decision rule
entries.text: Export scope can be application, Ruleset/version, Product or patch. Check in intended edits: a checked-out personal copy is not the exported version. Export the selected package and import it on the target. Inspect errors and Preview rather than assuming every required component is included. Production/delegated Rulesets may need explicit inclusion and permission to package unlocked versions.

entries.title: Extending Service-Level Agreement configurations
entries.text: Delayed Service-Level Agreement processing · Assignment Urgency

entries.title: Choose the right mechanism
entries.text: Assignment Ready defines when an assignment SLA starts: immediately, after a fixed delay, or at a DateTime property. Creation and readiness can differ. This setting applies to assignment SLAs; do not assume it delays every case-level deadline.

entries.title: Choose the right mechanism
entries.text: GetNextWork uses assignment urgency. Assignment urgency combines the case contribution at assignment creation, assignment SLA increments and a manual assignment adjustment, capped at 100. A later manual change to case urgency does not retroactively update an existing assignment's case contribution.

entries.title: Parallel processing
entries.text: Parallel processing in Pega applications · Running multiple instances of the same subprocess with a Split for Each shape · Running multiple instances of different subprocesses with a Split Join shape · Adding additional configuration to a subprocess

entries.title: Choose the right mechanism
entries.text: Independent stage processes can run concurrently. Split Join coordinates different subprocesses; Split For Each repeats one subprocess over a page list or page group. A spinoff lets the parent continue without joining back.

entries.title: Running multiple instances of the same subprocess with a Split for Each shape
Choose the right mechanism
entries.text: Use Split For Each when each eligible list/group item needs the same subprocess. Choose a join rule deliberately: All waits for every branch; Any continues after one completes and cancels remaining open assignments. Iterate processes qualifying pages sequentially.

entries.title: Running multiple instances of different subprocesses with a Split Join shape
Choose the right mechanism
entries.text: Split Join starts different subprocesses and resumes according to All, Any or Some join criteria. Some can express a completion count or condition; do not silently assume every branch must finish.

entries.title: Adding additional configuration to a subprocess
Choose the right mechanism
entries.text: Subprocess configuration controls the flow, page context and parameters. Review locking when branches share a case. A subprocess invoked on an embedded page must use that page's class and data rather than an unrelated top-level context.

entries.title: Managing concurrent Case access
entries.text: Case locking

entries.title: Choose the right mechanism
entries.text: Allow one user applies an exclusive lock when opening a case for editing. Allow multiple users permits concurrent opening and checks whether the persisted case changed when saving; a stale user must refresh. Locking protects data consistency and is separate from authorization.

entries.title: Flow Action processing
entries.text: Pre- and post-processing in Flow Actions · Pre- and post-processing configuration for Flow Actions

entries.title: Pre- and post-processing in Flow Actions
Choose the right mechanism
entries.text: Pre-processing runs when a Flow Action is presented or selected; post-processing runs after successful submission. Pre-processing can execute again on revisit, so defaults must not overwrite intentional edits. Prefer a Declare Expression for a value that should remain derived rather than recalculating it on each action.

entries.title: Pre- and post-processing configuration for Flow Actions
Choose the right mechanism
entries.text: Configure pre/post Data Transforms, activities or supported automations on the Flow Action's Action tab. Post-processing can save one or more savable Data Pages, with parameters and When conditions. Define persistence timing deliberately; displaying a form is not committing its external data.

entries.title: Organization records
entries.text: Organization records · Configuring Work Groups and Work Queues · Additional tasks for organizational records

entries.title: Choose the right mechanism
entries.text: Organization, division and unit describe the enterprise hierarchy; units can have children. Work groups represent operational teams that can span business units. These records support routing and reporting but do not replace access roles.

entries.title: Configuring Work Groups and Work Queues
Choose the right mechanism
entries.text: A work queue holds shared assignments; a work group associates operators, managers and queues. A worklist holds assignments for an individual operator. Match team-level routing to a queue and individual ownership to a worklist.

entries.title: Choose the right mechanism
entries.text: Maintain operator organizational membership, work group/queue associations and routing references together. Test that eligible team members can retrieve shared work and that managers can oversee the intended group; renaming an organization is not a substitute for updating routing.

entries.title: Field values
entries.text: Field values

entries.title: Choose the right mechanism
entries.text: Field Value rules define allowed values separately from a property. Apply To class and ruleset context allow the same inherited property to have different permitted values. A short, static list shared by all contexts may instead live on the property. Frequently changing external data belongs in a data source rather than hundreds of field-value rules.

entries.title: Validating data against a pattern
entries.text: Data validation against a pattern

entries.title: Choose the right mechanism
entries.text: An Edit Validate rule checks a property's character format. A Validate rule can enforce broader business conditions and call Edit Validate at submission. Built-in patterns may validate on field exit; custom Java Edit Validate logic executes server-side. A valid format does not establish that an identifier exists or belongs to the user.

entries.title: Keyed Data Pages
entries.text: Keyed Data Pages

entries.title: Choose the right mechanism
entries.text: A keyed Data Page selects embedded records from one cached list using configured keys, reducing repeated source calls for individual items. Keyed access is supported for read-only pages with thread or requestor scope. Define keys, uniqueness and refresh strategy; keyed access is not a guarantee that a stale or incomplete source list contains every current record.

entries.title: Exchanging data with other applications
entries.text: Connectors and services · External data sources for data types

entries.title: Choose the right mechanism
entries.text: A connector lets Pega call an external system; a service lets an external caller invoke Pega. Choose the direction first, then protocol, authentication, mapping and failure behavior. SOAP uses a WSDL contract; REST integrations use HTTP resources and operations.

entries.title: External data sources for data types
Choose the right mechanism
entries.text: A Data Type can use a local Pega system of record, transient case data, or an external source. External-source configuration creates connector and mapping assets. Parameterize requests, map response fields, use authentication profiles and vary endpoints by environment rather than copying hard-coded production URLs.

entries.title: Integration errors
entries.text: Error handling in connectors · Error detection configuration · Integration testing and security

entries.title: Choose the right mechanism
entries.text: Distinguish transient failures from persistent configuration or request errors. Temporary unavailability can justify a controlled retry; malformed requests or invalid configuration need correction. Communicate failure early rather than silently returning misleading success.

entries.title: Choose the right mechanism
entries.text: For Data Page connector loads, inspect errors in the response Data Transform and invoke reusable handling such as a copy of pxErrorHandlingTemplate. The connector error-handler flow covers errors not handled earlier; the default ConnectionProblem flow is not automatically invoked after a response transform has already handled the error.

entries.title: Choose the right mechanism
entries.text: Test success, incorrect data, timeout and authentication failures. Assert mappings on Data Pages and use appropriate credentials, certificates, keystores and approved endpoints. Secure transport does not make all incoming data safe; validate inputs and avoid exposing credentials in logs.

entries.title: Access control
entries.text: Role-based access control (RBAC) · Permission inheritance and dependent roles · Attachment categories · Attribute-based access control (ABAC) security model · Client-based access control

entries.title: Choose the right mechanism
entries.text: Authentication establishes identity; authorization determines allowed operations. An Access Group selects application access and roles. RBAC assigns capabilities through roles, Access of Role to Object rules and privileges. Hiding a button alone is not server authorization.

entries.title: Choose the right mechanism
entries.text: Dependent roles reuse standard permissions while allowing targeted overrides. Parent-class permissions can be inherited by child classes. Inspect explicit grants/denials and dependent-role order; do not treat permission inheritance as an unconditional union of all permissions.

entries.title: Choose the right mechanism
entries.text: Attachment categories organize documents and restrict attachment actions through privileges, When conditions and applicable team constraints. All configured When conditions must be true; at least one required privilege must be held. Use When rules for category conditions, not Access When rules.

entries.title: Choose the right mechanism
entries.text: ABAC supplements RBAC by comparing operator and object attributes for granular access. An Access Control Policy identifies the controlled action; an Access Control Policy Condition expresses the decision logic. Evaluate row and property restrictions in every relevant access path.

entries.title: Choose the right mechanism
entries.text: CBAC supports client requests to inspect, correct or erase their own personal data through a request-management application and participating repositories. Configure the permitted data and operations; CBAC is not ordinary role authorization or proof of legal compliance by itself.

entries.title: Securing and auditing data
entries.text: Data encryption · Field-level auditing

entries.title: Choose the right mechanism
entries.text: Encryption protects sensitive persisted data using managed cryptographic keys. Individual properties and BLOB data can have different encryption configurations; consider exposed columns as well as serialized data. Password hashing is a different, irreversible mechanism. Encryption does not replace authorization or safe key handling.

entries.title: Choose the right mechanism
entries.text: Standard case history records actions; field-level auditing records configured field changes, including old/new values, actor and time. Enable auditing for relevant fields and inspect embedded data fields when needed. Auditing is evidence after a change, not a mechanism that blocks the change.

entries.title: Define run-time settings
entries.text: Application Settings feature

entries.title: Choose the right mechanism
entries.text: Application Settings externalize environment-dependent values such as endpoint addresses and resource settings. Configure typed settings and useful categories, reference them from integrations, and resolve the appropriate environment values at runtime. Avoid hard-coded QA URLs in migrated rules; settings are configuration, not permission to expose secrets.

entries.title: Activities and Automations
entries.text: Activities · Activity structure · Declare OnChange Rules

entries.title: Choose the right mechanism
entries.text: Activities run ordered steps for procedural processing. Prefer a suitable out-of-the-box automation, Data Transform or specialized rule before custom activity code. Activities increase maintenance cost; a requirement for an activity should be explicit rather than a default for every data update.

entries.title: Choose the right mechanism
entries.text: An activity step specifies a method, parameters and optional step page. The step page supplies the data context; Pages & Classes declares page/class references. Preconditions, loops and transitions control execution. Call returns to the caller; Branch transfers execution without returning to subsequent caller steps.

entries.title: Choose the right mechanism
entries.text: Declare OnChange watches configured property changes and can execute activities or suspend work through a business-exception condition. Its trigger is a change, unlike a Declare Expression's derived-value dependency. Keep frequently triggered processing small and guard it with suitable conditions.

entries.title: Background processing
entries.text: Background processing · Background process management · Node classification · Admin Studio

entries.title: Choose the right mechanism
entries.text: Queue processors handle queued items asynchronously; job schedulers wake on a schedule to run an activity. Queue individual work with Run in Background or Queue-For-Processing. Schedule recurring scans with a job scheduler. Neither choice removes the need for safe retries and observable failure behavior.

entries.title: Choose the right mechanism
entries.text: Queue processors manage their processing transactions; avoid adding conflicting object-save/commit steps to their activity. Job scheduler activities manage the read/write work they perform. Investigate broken items and repair the underlying cause before reprocessing; design external effects so retries do not duplicate them.

entries.title: Choose the right mechanism
entries.text: Node classification assigns runtime work to suitable node types. Separate background workloads from web-user workloads where appropriate; moving work to another node does not fix inefficient code or eliminate shared database contention.

entries.title: Choose the right mechanism
entries.text: Admin Studio exposes runtime management for queue processors, jobs, nodes, requestors and listeners. Use it to inspect health, failure counts and running resources. A configured but disabled processor is not evidence that queued work is being completed.

entries.title: Measuring system performance
entries.text: Performance testing tools · The Performance Analyzer (PAL) · The Database Trace · Performance Profiler tool · Pega Diagnostic Center introduction

entries.title: Choose the right mechanism
entries.text: Measure a reproducible operation before changing configuration. PAL summarizes requestor resource consumption; Database Trace examines SQL; Performance Profiler traces procedural rule execution; PDC aggregates runtime health. Choose the tool for the evidence required.

entries.title: Choose the right mechanism
entries.text: PAL uses continuously collected statistics with little additional collection cost. Reset before a focused scenario and take incremental readings around individual interactions. DELTA readings isolate changes; TOTAL reflects accumulated work. Compare equivalent warm/cold runs rather than unrelated totals.

entries.title: Choose the right mechanism
entries.text: Database Trace records database operations, timings and related details. Use targeted short traces because collection adds overhead. Investigate expensive queries and commits in context; stack traces add further cost and should be collected only when needed.

entries.title: Choose the right mechanism
entries.text: Performance Profiler records activities, Data Transforms and When rule execution. It adds substantial overhead. Start, reproduce, stop and analyze; separate inclusive time from time excluding called children to avoid double-counting cost.

entries.title: Choose the right mechanism
entries.text: Pega Diagnostic Center provides aggregated application health, alerts and trends. Correlate events for the same time and interaction, prioritize recurring issues, and confirm improvements after a change. Monitoring evidence supports diagnosis but does not automatically repair every application defect.

entries.title: Reviewing log files
entries.text: Log files · Alerts

entries.title: Choose the right mechanism
entries.text: The PEGA log contains operational information, warnings and errors. ALERT contains threshold-based performance events; ALERTSECURITY contains security alerts. Additional logs depend on configured appenders, such as BIX extracts or security-event logging. Capture timestamp, node and requestor context before correlating evidence.

entries.title: Choose the right mechanism
entries.text: An alert identifies a threshold or security event, not a fully established root cause. My Alerts focuses on session events by default; broader logs and PDC provide wider context. Use event frequency and affected interactions to prioritize investigation, while avoiding unnecessary sensitive data in diagnostics.

entries.title: Debugging system performance
entries.text: Application performance issues · Rule assembly and performance · Diagnosis of database issues · Performance debugging tools for Constellation applications

entries.title: Choose the right mechanism
entries.text: A slow interaction can arise in the client, application server, rule processing, database or external service. Reproduce the reported path and use guardrail warnings plus measured evidence. A high compliance score is useful but does not prove the absence of performance defects.

entries.title: Choose the right mechanism
entries.text: Rule assembly generates and compiles executable code for rules; rule caches avoid repeating resolution and retrieval. Newly deployed rules can make initial use slower. Compare cold and warm behavior; numerous distinct ruleset lists can increase cache resource demands.

entries.title: Choose the right mechanism
entries.text: Use PAL deltas to locate database cost, then inspect expensive statements with Database Trace and database tools. Consider filters, indexes, reporting-property optimization, data volume and transaction boundaries. Do not add arbitrary indexes or expose sensitive columns without analyzing the query and data requirements.

entries.title: Performance debugging tools for Constellation applications
Choose the right mechanism
entries.text: Constellation uses stateless DX API requests with significant client orchestration. Inspect browser network/timing information and trace the relevant Service REST processing. Request context differs from a traditional stateful portal session; use the trace's step-page context rather than assuming a persistent portal Clipboard.

entries.title: Extending UI options
entries.text: Extensions to the Constellation UI · Constellation Web embed · Constellation DX Components · Constellation SDKs · The Constellation DX API

entries.title: Choose the right mechanism
entries.text: Prefer configured Constellation portals and existing view patterns before custom frontend code. Choose the smallest extension that meets the need. A custom portal experience remains governed by the application's case rules and authorization; grouping related information should preserve useful labels and validation.

entries.title: Choose the right mechanism
entries.text: Web Embed inserts a Constellation case or page experience into an existing website through generated HTML web-component markup. Configure a Web Embed channel and supported theme options. It uses Constellation rendering rather than giving arbitrary control over every UI implementation detail.

entries.title: Choose the right mechanism
entries.text: Constellation DX components extend the component library with purpose-specific React components integrated into App Studio view authoring. Use supported APIs and package the component for Pega; only customize when existing patterns do not meet a justified requirement.

entries.title: Choose the right mechanism
entries.text: Constellation SDKs connect Constellation orchestration to alternative design systems and supported frontend frameworks. They reduce work compared with hand-building every orchestration step, but a custom presentation still needs development, testing and upgrade maintenance.

entries.title: Choose the right mechanism
entries.text: The Constellation DX API is a model-driven REST interface exposing case data and view metadata. It uses OAuth 2.0. Preserve response eTag and send it as If-Match on updates to protect against stale writes. Handle conflicts by refreshing and reconciling; do not bypass concurrency checks.

entries.text: Each section owns one job; together they form the automation workflow. Modules — the technical map of the SUT, collected via XScan. TestSheet
entries.text: A TestSheet organizes test data into a logical testing structure. It can use Attributes for data-oriented cases or Steps for process-oriented cases; it is not itself a completed execution run.

entries.title: Attributes
entries.text: An Attribute represents a business object characteristic and can contain sub-Attributes or Instances. Its icon color reflects business relevance, which can be changed; do not identify its meaning solely from a fixed red icon.

entries.title: Instances
entries.text: An Instance supplies a concrete variant. Attribute-level variants supply values; TestSheet-level Instances describe complete combinations for later generation.

entries.title: ValidValues / StraightThrough
entries.text: Straight Through is the Instance Character for the frequently used path with fewest dependencies; it is required for linear expansion. ValidValues can be an example name, but neither that name nor the leftmost column position makes an Instance Straight Through. Set Character deliberately.

entries.title: Practical preparation
entries.text: Understand basic API and HTTP concepts and Tosca Modules/TestCases. Use a permitted test environment and the access and licenses required by your organization; exact Academy prerequisites were not accessible.

entries.title: Launch outside Commander
entries.text: Current Tosca 2026.1 docs name ApiScan.exe in %COMMANDER_HOME% as the filesystem launch entry. Running independently of Commander does not establish that an arbitrary copied executable needs no installation, license or supporting files.

entries.title: Check organization access
entries.text: Confirm with your administrator that your account belongs to the cloud license server. This connection workflow is documented; a pop-up alone does not prove a single root cause.

entries.title: Why test at the API boundary
Software interface
entries.text: API requests can exercise a service without driving a graphical interface. A callable interface and usable test environment can permit testing before a UI is ready.

entries.title: Getting Started - API & Webservice Theory
entries.text: Primary documentation or specification · Primary documentation or specification · Primary documentation or specification · Primary documentation or specification · Primary documentation or specification · Primary documentation or specification

entries.title: API
entries.text: An application programming interface defines how software components interact. It can be local or exposed through a network service; it is not necessarily a separate messenger program.

entries.title: Network service
entries.text: A service interface can be reached across a network. The HTTP examples here use request and response messages; the public World Wide Web is not required for every private network API.

entries.title: Different kinds of abstraction
entries.text: SOAP defines a messaging framework; REST is an architectural style with constraints including a uniform interface and stateless interactions. Neither term means every endpoint implements every possible method.

entries.title: XML
entries.text: Extensible Markup Language represents document data and logical structure through markup. It can be used in messages or local files. Well-formed XML is not automatically valid against a schema or correct according to business rules.

entries.title: Choose a permitted test service
entries.text: Use an authorized sandbox with a published API contract. The historical DemoWebShop/Coffeeshop course mapping and training endpoint availability were not verified, so these notes do not require either service.

entries.title: Follow the service contract
entries.text: Configure credentials in the required location: the API Scan message section exposes authentication, parameters and headers separately. A query parameter named key and a 24-hour lifetime are not universal REST requirements.

entries.text: Save as saves an API Scan project to a chosen file; Save or Ctrl+S saves to the same file after it has been saved before. Open opens a project and Close closes the current project. These are project operations, distinct from Payload-tab file operations and export to Commander.

entries.title: Duplicate
entries.text: Duplicate copies the selected folder or message; it is also available in the context menu. Inspect the copy and rename it deliberately; the accessed article does not certify an incrementing-name algorithm or exact destination for every object type.

entries.title: Delete
entries.text: Delete removes the selected folder or message. Confirm the intended selection and save a recoverable checkpoint before deletion.

entries.title: Rename
entries.text: Use Rename in the Home menu or the context menu of the selected project object. The accessed API Scan pages do not verify an F2 shortcut; a Commander shortcut list is not proof of API Scan behavior.

entries.title: Independent naming convention
entries.text: An optional 01 / 02 / 03 prefix can communicate intended sequence to reviewers. Do not assume display sorting defines TestCase execution order; inspect and configure the exported test steps separately. The accessed docs do not establish universal alphabetical sorting of every object.
