entries.title: Where TDS1 fits in the testing lifecycle

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Requirements
entries.text: Define expected functional and non-functional behavior with stakeholders, then organize criteria and prioritize business risk.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: TestCase-Design
entries.text: Plan logical tests and data variation before execution. TestSheets organize Attributes or Steps, Instances hold concrete variations, and Classes support reuse. Templates can instantiate executable TestCases from the design.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Distinct responsibilities
entries.text: Requirements express expected behavior. A TestSheet structures data and processes; an executable TestCase performs checks. These artifacts are related but are not interchangeable.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Why invest time up front in test design

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Planned variation
entries.text: Select a combination method for the risks and interactions under test. All combinations expands the full defined dataset; Orthogonal covers each value, Pairwise covers value pairs, and Linear expansion varies one non-StraightThrough value at a time around a baseline.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Reporting needs recalculation
entries.text: Link executable tests to their Requirements. After changes, Requirement values need recalculation: AutoCalculateRequirements is off by default in 2026.1. Use Update Outdated Values, or enable automatic calculation and restart Tosca; large repositories can incur delays.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Quilyn study roadmap

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Lesson 1 - Requirements
entries.text: Work with Requirements (2026.1) · Link Requirements to TestCases (2026.1) · Requirement columns and properties (2024.1)

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Building the Requirements structure

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Requirement
entries.text: A criterion the system under test is expected to fulfil — functional (e.g. 'a customer can pay with a Visa card') or non-functional (e.g. system security). Requirements are gathered from workshops with stakeholders, or from existing specs/BA documents.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Structuring principle
entries.text: Independent design recommendation: organize broad areas and refine only as needed for traceability. A readable hierarchy helps navigation; depth alone does not establish more accurate coverage.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Basic Weighting

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Weight column
entries.text: New Requirements have weight 1. Set weights with stakeholders to express relative business risk; the Weight column contains those values. Do not confuse direct weights with the 0–10 input scale documented for Frequency class and Damage class.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Top-down entry order
entries.text: Independent planning technique: agree on broad business areas before detailed criteria so priorities are consistent. This is a suggested workflow, not an enforced Tosca entry order.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Complex Weighting

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Why complex weighting exists
entries.text: A single linear scale often can't distinguish importance clearly enough (is this a 3 or a 4?). Complex Weighting instead asks two separate business questions per Requirement and lets Tosca calculate the Weight for you.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: The formula
entries.text: The 2024.1 column reference documents Weight = 2^Frequency class × 2^Damage class; each class ranges from 0 to 10. For Frequency 3 and Damage 2, the result is 8 × 4 = 32. These are relative risk estimates, not exact monetary predictions.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Using Requirements as a dashboard

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Contribution (%)
entries.text: The 2024.1 reference describes Contribution (%) as a Requirement’s weighted share of its RequirementSet, with sub-Requirements calculated relative to their parent. Contribution is an importance allocation, not proof that tests passed.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Relative Weight (%)
entries.text: The reference defines Relative Weight (%) as the Requirement weight divided by the total RequirementSet weight. For a flat set with positive total weight, the percentages sum to 100. Do not treat this as an unconditional rule for every level, filtered view or zero-total-weight structure.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Downstream links
entries.text: Link TestCases to Requirements directly or through TestCase Links. Reporting distinguishes completed specification, executed tests and pass/fail state. Execution State also depends on result aggregation, which the 2024.1 reference says defaults to First. TestCase Design Coverage is separate and independent of Weight and WorkState.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Keeping Requirements up to date

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Current documented update behavior
entries.text: Tosca On-Premises 2026.1 documents AutoCalculateRequirements as off by default. A linked test change can leave calculated Requirement values outdated; the blue exclamation indicator identifies stale RequirementSets.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Manual refresh
entries.text: Right-click a RequirementSet and choose Update Outdated Values, or use Update Outdated Values in the Requirements dynamic menu to recalculate all outdated values.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Lesson 2 - Attributes
entries.text: Work with Attributes · Use TestSheets · Work with TestCase-Design · Use TestCase-Design Steps

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: TestSheets and Attributes

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: TestSheet
entries.text: A TestSheet organizes logical test data. The documentation recommends covering each Requirement with a TestSheet; creating a sheet alone does not prove its generated tests fully cover the criterion.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Attribute
entries.text: A characteristic or business object involved in the behavior being tested — for example, a credit-card drop-down on a checkout form. Attributes describe *what varies*; the specific values an Attribute can take (e.g. Visa, Mastercard) are added later as Instances (Lesson 3).

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Structuring Attributes
entries.text: Like Requirements, Attributes can be layered — every Attribute may have sub-Attributes, depending on how much detail the TestSheet needs.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Nested structure versus business relevance

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Two different concerns
entries.text: Attributes can contain sub-Attributes and Instances. BusinessRelevant separately identifies input relevance or verification data. The accessed 2026.1 pages do not establish the earlier lesson’s claim about a non-editable AttrType property; do not rely on that unverified UI rule.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: The four core Attributes

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Recommended structure
entries.text: Independent Quilyn organizational example: group metadata, setup, inputs and expected results under four named Attributes when that makes a TestSheet easier to understand. These exact names are not a mandatory or verified universal Tricentis recommendation.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: BusinessRelevant property

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Three possible values
entries.text: BusinessRelevant is user-controlled. Yes is the default; No identifies non-relevant data and Result identifies verification data. Changing the parent setting also changes its sub-Attributes.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Building it in Tosca

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.version: Tosca On-Premises 2026.1 documentation; independent boundary examples
entries.title: Lesson 3 - Instances
entries.text: Work with Instances · Generate and combine Instances

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.version: Tosca On-Premises 2026.1 documentation; independent boundary examples
entries.title: What is an Instance

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.version: Tosca On-Premises 2026.1 documentation; independent boundary examples
entries.title: Instance
entries.text: An Instance specifies a variation of an Attribute. Create it with Create Instance or Ctrl+N, Ctrl+I; use a unique name. Tosca can also create Instances from entered Attribute values or an XModuleAttribute.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.version: Tosca On-Premises 2026.1 documentation; independent boundary examples
entries.title: Character: Valid, Invalid, StraightThrough

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.version: Tosca On-Premises 2026.1 documentation; independent boundary examples
entries.title: Valid (default)
entries.text: Valid is the default Character: the value fits the business process and no validation error is expected.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.version: Tosca On-Premises 2026.1 documentation; independent boundary examples
entries.title: Invalid
entries.text: Invalid means the input should be rejected. Independent example: a wrong password test passes only if the implemented checks confirm the required rejection, message and absence of a session; the Character label does not itself execute assertions.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.version: Tosca On-Premises 2026.1 documentation; independent boundary examples
entries.title: StraightThrough
entries.text: StraightThrough identifies a frequently used path with few dependencies and high business risk if it fails. Linear expansion needs this baseline. It is not merely any default Valid value.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.version: Tosca On-Premises 2026.1 documentation; independent boundary examples
entries.title: Position: Inner vs Boundary

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.version: Tosca On-Premises 2026.1 documentation; independent boundary examples
entries.title: Boundary Value
entries.text: Boundary values are at or around an accepted range edge. Independent integer-age example: 0/1 and 99/100 exercise rejection and acceptance around an inclusive 1–99 range; verify the business rule rather than assuming every range has identical boundaries.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.version: Tosca On-Premises 2026.1 documentation; independent boundary examples
entries.title: Regression risk at boundaries
entries.text: Do not assume a boundary defect is permanently impossible after one test. Changes in validation, data conversion or surrounding logic can reintroduce it even when the published range is unchanged. Keep relevant boundary checks in regression according to risk.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.version: Tosca On-Premises 2026.1 documentation; independent boundary examples
entries.title: Inner Value (default)
entries.text: Inner values are away from a chosen boundary. Independent grouping example: if all ages 2–98 follow the same business behavior, choose a representative from that group. If additional age thresholds change behavior, split the group instead of treating all inner values as equivalent.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Lesson 4 - Combinatorial Methods
entries.text: Generate and combine Instances · Work with Instances · Dynamic menu - TestCaseDesign · Keyboard shortcuts

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: The four combinatorial methods

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: All Combinations
entries.text: Generates the product of defined value choices. Independent unconstrained example: three Attributes with three choices yield 27 datasets. Generated combinations are design Instances, not already executed TestCases.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Orthogonal
entries.text: Uses every defined value at least once while keeping the combination set small. Independent unconstrained example: three Attributes with four choices can cover all values in four rows; this is value coverage, not all pair coverage.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Pairwise
entries.text: Covers every value pair between two Attributes. This is stronger interaction coverage than merely using every value once, but does not establish full higher-order coverage.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Linear expansion
entries.text: Starts with a defined StraightThrough baseline and varies one non-baseline value per row. In a simple model with one baseline choice per Attribute and nine alternate values in total, this gives ten datasets. The relation-aware variant can add, exclude or constrain combinations.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Choosing a method

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: It depends on the project
entries.text: The current documentation offers methods for different project needs; it does not establish a universal default or an industry-wide legal mandate. Select a method based on specified coverage, business dependencies and applicable project constraints.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Building combinations manually in Tosca

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Instances as combination columns
entries.text: Right-click a TestSheet, TestCase-Design Class or Attribute and select Generate Instances, then the desired method. These design combinations can later support TestCase organization and template instantiation.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Combining at Attribute level vs TestSheet level
entries.text: You can generate on a selected Attribute or a TestSheet, and can select particular Attributes or Instances. Confirm the generated values in the selected scope rather than assuming a particular highlight color proves coverage.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Keeping a TestSheet manageable

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Arrange Instances
entries.text: Optimize Instances → Arrange Instances arranges the selected Attribute’s Instances; the dynamic-menu reference documents Ctrl+R. The accessed reference does not specify the earlier lesson’s exact five-category sort order.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Merge Instance Duplicates
entries.text: Merge Instance Duplicates merges duplicates with matching values, Character and Position. Matching display names or values alone do not establish every property is identical.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Lesson 5 - TestCase Specifications
entries.text: Dynamic menu · Combination/filter operations · Template linking · TestCases from TestSheet

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: From combinations to physical values

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Why more filling-in is needed
entries.text: Generated combinations still need the input, metadata and expected values required by your test implementation. Independent Administration/Verification labels describe their intended purpose; filling them does not by itself create or execute assertions.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Fill Empty Values

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Fill Empty Values → Specific
entries.text: The documented Fill empty Values → Specific action fills empty fields using a selected value; if an Attribute has no Instances, you can supply a custom value. Orthogonal filling instead uses child Instance values. Confirm the target selection and the resulting fields before generating tests.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Filtering before filling

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: When one value per row isn't enough
entries.text: Independent example: use different stage labels for selected tests according to your plan. Boundary checks can belong in regression; they are not automatically one-time tests.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Using the Filter Column
entries.text: Add the Filter column with Column Chooser to filter Instances at TestSheet or Attribute level. Inspect the active selection and resulting values rather than relying only on display color.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Direct values and template data binding

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Custom values
entries.text: The dynamic-menu reference allows a user-specific value when an Attribute has no Instances. Confirm that the selected data scope and intended row agree; the previous blanket claim that higher-level entry always corrupts combinations is not established by the accessed documentation.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Template binding
entries.text: For automated tests, link the TestSheet or Class to a TestCase Template. SchemaName identifies the linked source. Automatic XL paths require empty TestStepValues whose names uniquely match Attributes; manually check those paths before creating the TemplateInstance.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Review before generation

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Lesson 6 - Classes
entries.text: Classes · Class references

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: What a Class is

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Class
entries.text: A reusable Tosca object — conceptually similar to a Library in the TestCase section — that lets you define an Attribute structure (with its Instances and combinations) once and reuse it across many TestSheets via a Class Reference. A typical candidate is data that shows up repeatedly, like a Customer Attribute structure used by every TestSheet that touches customer data.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Why it matters
entries.text: Class and reference editing are bidirectional: source changes update references, and editing an unresolved reference changes the corresponding Class. Resolve the reference first if you need an independent local variation.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Documented Class creation

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Dragging an Attribute WITHOUT top-level combinations
entries.text: If selected Attributes have no child elements, the documented prompt offers Create Class from Attribute (Class plus Instance collection) or Create Structure from Attribute (Class without an Instance collection). The reference does not describe this as importing all source TestSheet combinations.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Working with Class References

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Editing a Class
entries.text: Once created, a Class can be modified exactly like a TestSheet — add or remove Attributes, create or delete Instances, adjust combinations, and set Character/Position on its Instances.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Resolve Class Reference
entries.text: Resolve Class Reference removes the shared reference and returns it to an Attribute. Use this before making an independent local variation. Do not assume resolving one consumer removes other live references or makes deleting the source safe for all of them.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Unused Instances vs irrelevant Attributes
entries.text: Unused combinations and deactivated Attributes are different concerns. Add the Relevance column, select a reference and disable the checkbox for an irrelevant Attribute. It becomes gray; F11 shows or hides deactivated Attributes. Deactivation is more than renaming or deleting a data value.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Hands-on

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Lesson 7 - Link to Requirements
entries.text: Primary documentation · Additional primary documentation · Additional primary documentation · Additional primary documentation

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Why link TestCase Design back to Requirements

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Purpose
entries.text: Requirement links distinguish planned design data from physical TestCases and execution evidence. A TestSheet or selected Instances can establish planned coverage before executable tests exist; this is not proof that the application was tested successfully.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: How to link

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Drag and drop
entries.text: Drag Instances from the TestSheet onto their matching Requirement. If every Instance on the TestSheet belongs to that Requirement, the whole TestSheet can be dragged at once. If only some Instances are in scope right now — for example, only the ones planned for the current sprint — select and drag just those individual Instances instead.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: TestCase-Substitute link
entries.text: Linking TestSheet, Class or Instance data creates a substitute for each linked Instance. A substitute represents planned test data, not an executed or passed test.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: TestCase link
entries.text: Creating a physical TestCase does not by itself replace its substitute. Drag the TestCase onto the corresponding substitute link. Alternatively, use Replace Substitutes by Testcases on the RequirementSet; the required TestCases must be used in an ExecutionList and that ExecutionList must be linked to the RequirementSet.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: TestSheet-to-Requirement ratio

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Organize coverage around Requirements
entries.text: The documentation recommends TestSheet coverage for application Requirements. Choose a structure that keeps each Requirement traceable; the same Requirement can receive selected Instances or Class data. One TestSheet per Requirement is a useful organizational choice, not a prohibition on other documented link scopes.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Building the project dashboard

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Link an ExecutionList to a RequirementSet
entries.text: Drag an ExecutionList onto a RequirementSet to create its link. Merely creating the list does not establish this relationship. An ExecutionEntry can separately be dragged onto an individual Requirement to create a TestCase link. Its LinkExecutionEntryHandleExecutionList setting controls whether the associated ExecutionList is added to the set: AlwaysAdd, AskUser or NeverAdd.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Hands-on

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Lesson 8 - Integration of New Attributes
entries.text: Primary documentation · Additional primary documentation · Additional primary documentation

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Why this comes up

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: The scenario
entries.text: Applications evolve — new features get added to the system under test after a TestSheet already exists. When a new feature affects existing test data, the TestSheet needs a new Attribute (and its Instances) integrated into the structure that's already in place, without starting over.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Where to add it
entries.text: Create the new Attribute wherever it logically fits in the existing structure — it can be added right alongside Attributes that already have combinations, even if that means the existing combination set now needs to account for it.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Updating combinations at every level

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: The core rule
entries.text: Inspect combinations at every affected level. Fill missing baseline values where appropriate, then complete or propagate uncovered variations according to the chosen method and constraints. The documented Complete Instances command adds uncombined combinations without duplicating existing ones; Propagate Instance(s) adds chosen combinations without applying a combinatorial method.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Independent worked example: extending shipping choices

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: The change
entries.text: Independent Quilyn example, not a verified Academy exercise: assume an unconstrained Linear Expansion design with Ground as the shipping baseline and two previously uncovered alternatives, Next Day Air and Second Day Air. Pickup has N/A shipping. Real business constraints must be modeled rather than inferred from these labels.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Updating the lower (Checkout) level
entries.text: Fill Ground in the existing checkout baseline and N/A where shipping does not apply. In this example, neither air-shipping alternative is represented yet. Add two checkout scenarios, each varying only the shipping choice while keeping the other fields at their valid StraightThrough baselines.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Updating the TestSheet level
entries.text: At the TestSheet level, inspect existing rows and select appropriate checkout data. Assume the two new checkout alternatives are not represented there either: this simple Linear Expansion example adds two upper-level baseline variations, one for each checkout alternative. Other methods or Relations can require different combinations; there is no fixed original count of nine rows.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Inspect Requirement coverage and refresh calculations

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Lesson 9 - Best Practices
entries.text: Primary documentation · Additional primary documentation · Additional primary documentation · Additional primary documentation

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Design for reuse

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Spot reuse early
entries.text: Use a centrally managed Class for repeated Attribute structures. Unresolved references share changes in both directions: editing the reference also changes the Class. Resolve a reference before making a consumer-specific change; other consumers can remain shared. Decide on reuse from actual maintenance needs, not a mandatory two-use threshold.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: An optional organizational layout
entries.text: Independent Quilyn layout: Administration for non-business data, Precondition for setup, Process for actions and Verification for expected results. This four-group skeleton is one modeling choice, not a documented requirement for every TestSheet. Match the hierarchy and relevance to the test objective.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Structuring for Agile: Given-When-Then

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Given-When-Then
entries.text: A template for writing acceptance tests for user stories, useful when TestCase Design needs to reflect an Agile way of working. An acceptance test built this way has three parts: Given (the context and preconditions), When (the action being carried out), Then (the observable, expected outcome).

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Worked example
entries.text: Independent example: Given a returning customer is logged in and has a saved shipping address, When the customer opens checkout, Then the saved address is displayed for confirmation. Keep the observable address result separate from a later order-submission action; each assertion should state the behavior being tested.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: The goal
entries.text: Generate Instances produces design datasets from Attributes and their values. These rows are not executed tests; template mapping and instantiation are separate steps. Choose the method and scope according to required coverage, rather than assuming automatic generation establishes completeness.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: How it works
entries.text: Right-click a TestSheet, TestCase-Design Class or Attribute and choose Generate Instances with the desired method. You can Ctrl-select specific Attributes or Instances for a narrower scope. The documented default maximum is 1000 combinations; generation is not promised to be instantaneous for every dataset.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Generating at an Attribute or selected scope

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Documented target and Instance collection
entries.text: The generation article documents TestSheet, Class and Attribute targets without requiring a manually created empty folder. The Instances article states that creating the first Instance in an Attribute automatically creates its Instances Collection. The historical add-then-delete folder workaround is not established as a universal prerequisite by these accessed articles.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Generating
entries.text: For a selected scope, hold Ctrl while selecting the Attributes or Instances, right-click one of them and choose Generate Instances followed by the method. Inspect the generated combinations and unused values; do not assume all other Attributes were included.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Generating at the TestSheet level

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Generate at the TestSheet
entries.text: Right-click the TestSheet and select Generate Instances followed by the desired method. Inspect the resulting combinations, nested data usage and scope. Generated rows are held in an Instances Collection beneath the relevant TestSheet.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Generate Instances vs Complete Instances

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Initial generation versus extending coverage
entries.text: Use Generate Instances for generation with the selected method. When additional values need to join existing combinations without duplicates, the documented operation is Complete Instances. The accessed article does not justify calling every Generate operation a destructive rebuild.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Complete Instances
entries.text: Complete Instances combines values not previously combined, without creating duplicates. Uncombined Instances appear in bold. Right-click a TestSheet, Class or Attribute, select Complete Instances, then choose the method. Inspect the resulting coverage; this does not guarantee completeness beyond the chosen method and scope.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Independent capstone
entries.text: This is an independent Quilyn worked example and set of practice prompts using documented Tosca design concepts. It is not a transcription or certification of the Academy capstone. Define business rules, modeled choices, expected outcomes, coverage method and traceability separately.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Worked example: a Loyalty Tier discount

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Business context
entries.text: Independent assumptions: a checkout grants Guest 0%, Bronze 5%, Silver 10% and Gold 15% discounts on a subtotal of 100, before tax and shipping. An expired loyalty account is rejected. Assume Guest is the most frequent, least-dependent checkout path and a failure there has the greatest business impact. These are exercise assumptions, not facts about a real webshop.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Step 1 — Requirement
entries.text: Create a Requirement for loyalty-discount behavior and assess its risk using project evidence. The exercise does not determine a universal Frequency or Damage class from the feature name. Keep expected amounts and rejection behavior traceable to the specified business rules.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Step 2 — Attributes
entries.text: Use an optional layout with Administration (No), Precondition (Yes), Process (Yes) and Verification (Result). Model Loyalty Tier as the only varying business input; keep other inputs fixed for this exercise. Verification holds the expected amounts or rejection outcome.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Step 3 — Instances
entries.text: Create Guest as StraightThrough under the stated frequency, dependency and impact assumptions; Bronze, Silver and Gold as Valid; Expired Account as Invalid. For subtotal 100, verify totals 100, 95, 90 and 85 respectively; for Expired Account verify the specified rejection and absence of a completed discounted order. Invalid data passes a test only when all relevant assertions hold.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Step 4 — Combinatorial method
entries.text: With exactly one varying Attribute containing five choices and no constraints, Linear Expansion produces five datasets: one baseline and four alternatives. All Combinations also produces five in this single-Attribute case; it does not create an unnecessary larger suite here. Neither generation operation executes the tests.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 1 (TDS1)
entries.title: Step 5 — Reuse and linking
entries.text: A Class is useful if centralized sharing benefits other designs; a mandatory second-use threshold is not established here. Link the five design Instances to the Requirement as substitutes, replace them explicitly after linking physical tests, and inspect execution evidence and recalculated coverage separately.

entries.title: Test-data management
entries.text: A test-data workflow must provide usable inputs, keep necessary state and define how data is reused or retired. This lesson concentrates on Test Data Service, not a verified catalog of Tricentis product offerings.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 2 (TDS2)
entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS (documentation baseline; Academy video version unverified)
entries.title: Coverage planning with TestCase-Design
entries.text: TestCase-Design models test combinations and concrete values through TestSheets, Attributes and Instances. It helps plan coverage and instantiate TestCase templates; it does not make an application input inherently safe for simultaneous use.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 2 (TDS2)
entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS (documentation baseline; Academy video version unverified)
entries.title: Item management with Test Data Service
entries.text: TDS stores items that tests can select and change. Reuse depends on the test scenario and current data state. Stored items are not inherently single-use: a read can be non-locking, and a selected item can be used again after its lock is released if the scenario permits.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 2 (TDS2)
entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS (documentation baseline; Academy video version unverified)
entries.title: Independent input example
entries.text: A practice login may use a disposable username and a fake password. A payment workflow may need an already-created practice account. Decide which inputs are valid before running the application actions.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 2 (TDS2)
entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS (documentation baseline; Academy video version unverified)
entries.title: Two core challenges TDS solves

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 2 (TDS2)
entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS (documentation baseline; Academy video version unverified)
entries.title: Find suitable data
entries.text: Prepare or import suitable practice data, then select an item matching the intended preconditions. A create operation stores an item; it is not a guarantee of automatic production-data masking or valid account provisioning in the application.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 2 (TDS2)
entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS (documentation baseline; Academy video version unverified)
entries.title: Track explicit changes
entries.text: Verify the application result, then explicitly store any new identifier or state required by later tests. A property called Status is not automatically updated merely because an application action or TestCase completed.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 2 (TDS2)
entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS (documentation baseline; Academy video version unverified)
entries.title: Independent account example
entries.text: Suppose two tests both change a practice account. Separate accounts may permit parallel execution; if one shared account is required, coordinate access and verify its current state. Do not turn this example into a rule that all account tests must run sequentially.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 2 (TDS2)
entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS (documentation baseline; Academy video version unverified)
entries.title: Locking has a defined scope
entries.text: Find & provide item locks the selected item. Expert ReadOnly retrieves data without acquiring a lock; it does not unlock an existing one. Find releases its lock at execution completion, on failure or a new loop iteration. Locking test-data access does not automatically protect every application-side operation.

entries.title: Application state is separate
entries.text: An application action does not automatically synchronize a TDS property. Model the application action, verify its result, and explicitly write the needed test-data state. The web data view is not a test execution report.

entries.text: Suppose one test creates a practice user, another prepares a file, and a third uploads it. Record the actual identifiers needed by later steps. For a focused upload test, provide a suitable user and file during setup rather than assuming the whole journey must always run first.

entries.text: Restricts the search to records matching a specific condition — e.g. TDS attribute Status = 'New', to find only newly registered customers rather than any customer record.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS (documentation baseline; Academy video version unverified)
entries.title: Syntax
entries.text: Use {TDS[ResourceName.PropertyName]} in the Value field after finding or creating the item. ResourceName identifies the item by its alias, followed by the attribute name. Do not substitute the repository name or an arbitrary type name.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 2 (TDS2)

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS (documentation baseline; Academy video version unverified)
entries.title: Worked example
entries.text: Independent example: Find an item of type CustomerDetails with alias customer, then use {TDS[customer.Email]} to access its Email attribute. If Find instead omitted the alias, the default would be CustomerDetails, making {TDS[CustomerDetails.Email]} valid for that retrieved resource.

entries.text: Changes a known item's attributes through its alias. A usual workflow first finds the intended item, then supplies the alias to Update item; an item created earlier can also have an alias. Define changed attributes under Data structure with ActionMode Input.

entries.text: Existing alias name (item) must identify the item already available to the TestCase. For an explicit alias customer, pass customer; only an omitted Find alias defaults to the type name. A synthetic Status change from New to Active is an explicit test-data update.

entries.title: Explicit state maintenance
entries.text: This is an independent practice example, not a verified Academy payment walkthrough. Keep the application's state assertion separate from the repository update, and handle failures before marking test data consumed. A generic successful HTTP response does not prove a business operation completed.

entries.title: Why move data at all
entries.text: Once the full order process (including payment) has run, that customer's data is considered consumed. Moving it into a distinct TDS type keeps the repository stateful — it's immediately clear which records are still 'live' and which have already been used, which is especially valuable for a distributed team.

entries.text: Moves a known item identified by Existing alias name (item) into Existing or new TDS type. With alias customer, pass customer and destination CustomerDetails_Used. The alias need not equal the source type. One move targets one known item, not every item in the source type.

entries.title: What makes it different
entries.text: ReadOnly reads without acquiring an item lock. It is not the UnlockItem operation and should not be used to release a lock acquired earlier. Find reserves the retrieved item for exclusive use; documented automatic release occurs after execution or at a new loop iteration, including failure.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca - Test Design Specialist Level 2 (TDS2)
entries.moduleTitle: Lesson 4 - Introduction to the Standard TestData - Expert Module
entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS (documentation baseline; Academy video version unverified)
entries.title: When to reach for it
entries.text: Use non-locking reads for shared reference values when the test does not require exclusive consumption. For example, several tests may read the same synthetic product-category record. Reading without reservation does not guarantee the data remains unchanged by other tests.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 course unverified
entries.title: What this course is about

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 course unverified
entries.title: Beyond the browser
entries.text: A business process can span a web form, email, a document, a workbook, a Windows application and a mobile screen. These independent notes examine the Tosca technologies used for such steps.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 course unverified
entries.title: One tool, many engines
entries.text: TBox provides a shared model for Engines 3.0. Modules and TestSteps provide familiar building blocks; supported controls, ActionModes and prerequisites still depend on the selected technology.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 course unverified
entries.title: What you will be able to do

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 course unverified
entries.title: Workspace and subset
entries.text: Create an isolated workspace and inspect the imported Standard subset. Course-specific base files and their exact contents must be checked in the accessible course; no original AE1 subset was obtained in this review.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 course unverified
entries.title: How the course is structured

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 course unverified
entries.title: Learning workflow
entries.text: Read the matching documentation, attempt an isolated example and review the result against the specification. Do not infer Academy exam coverage or unlock requirements from these notes.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 course unverified
entries.title: TBox Theory - Engines and Frameworks
entries.text: TBox Theory Lesson - Engines and Frameworks

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 course unverified
entries.title: What an automation framework is

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 course unverified
entries.title: The problem a framework solves
entries.text: Each technology exposes different interfaces. A shared framework supplies common automation building blocks while engines implement technology-specific operations.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 course unverified
entries.title: TBox
entries.text: The Tosca TBox framework is the .NET-based foundation that all Engines 3.0 are built on, for both GUI and non-GUI tests. It provides one common interface across every supported technology, so the differences between technologies are absorbed by the Engine rather than pushed up into your TestCases. TBox and its Engines 3.0 are part of the standard Tricentis Tosca installation — nothing extra to install for the core engines.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 course unverified
entries.title: Engines 3.0

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 course unverified
entries.title: What an Engine does
entries.text: An Engine is the technology-specific layer that knows how to find and manipulate controls in one kind of application. It translates the generic instruction coming from the TestCase — 'set this value', 'verify this value', 'click this' — into whatever that particular technology actually requires.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 course unverified
entries.title: GUI vs non-GUI engines

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 course unverified
entries.title: GUI engines
entries.text: Steer something a human could see and click: a browser page, an Excel worksheet, a Windows dialog, a mobile screen. Identification is about locating a visible control.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 course unverified
entries.title: Non-GUI engines
entries.text: Steer backend systems with no visual component — the XML and JSON engines, API calls, protocol-level interactions. There is no screen to look at; the Engine works directly against the data or the service.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 course unverified
entries.title: Modules, XModules, and engine binding

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 course unverified
entries.title: XModules
entries.text: Engines 3.0 use XModules to steer test objects. An XModule is the Tosca object that represents a piece of the application under test, and it carries the information the Engine needs to find that object again at execution time. XModules can be structured hierarchically and referenced across many TestCases — the same reuse model you already know from web automation.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 course unverified
entries.title: How the Engine gets chosen
entries.text: A Module carries engine/interface information used by its TestSteps. Scanned and Standard Modules can represent different technologies; inspect the actual Module configuration.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 course unverified
entries.title: Why the workflow never changes
entries.text: Modules, TestSteps and TestStepValues remain familiar building blocks. Available ActionModes depend on InterfaceType and control support; they are not universally identical for every engine.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 course unverified
entries.title: Bonus: steering a specific table row

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 course unverified
entries.title: Header-relative positions, absolute positions and value constraints
entries.text: In table addressing, $ identifies positions relative to the configured header, while # identifies absolute positions. Both numeric forms are positional. To find a row by business values, configure cell constraints and resolve any multiple matches before acting on another cell.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 course unverified
entries.title: HeaderRow
entries.text: A steering parameter that tells Tosca which row of the scanned table holds the column headers. Once set, later TestStepValues can address a column by its header text instead of a raw column number — 'the Total column' rather than 'column 4' — which keeps the TestCase readable and keeps it working if columns are reordered but not renamed.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 course unverified
entries.title: Constraint ActionMode
entries.text: Constraint restricts the search using one or more cell values. Ensure that the resulting row is unique before verifying or buffering another cell; a constraint is not a guarantee of uniqueness.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 course unverified
entries.title: Bonus: operating Tosca outside Tosca Commander

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 course unverified
entries.title: TC Shell
entries.text: TC Shell is the command-line control of Tosca Commander itself — it lets you navigate a Workspace, read or modify a TestStepValue, and run an ExecutionList entirely from the command line, without the Tosca Commander UI ever opening. It has two modes: interactive, where you type commands one at a time and get the same range of functions the GUI offers; and script, where a batch of commands is read from a script data file with no opportunity to intervene — the mode built for running an extensive test portfolio unattended, for instance from a CI pipeline.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 course unverified
entries.title: Interactive mode: jumptonode and task
entries.text: Open TC Shell with the workspace path and authentication appropriate to its repository type. Parameters are case-sensitive. JumpToNode uses an object NodePath; task lists operations available for the current object. Inspect the applicable start/command documentation rather than assuming every repository uses -login.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 course unverified
entries.title: Script mode: .tcs and .bat
entries.text: Pass a plain-text .tcs command file to start script mode. Supply task inputs in that file; TC Shell processes commands, closes the workspace and exits. A wrapper is optional, not an intrinsic requirement of script mode.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 course unverified
entries.title: Printing reports through TC Shell
entries.text: The public 2026.1 reporting workflow requires a report definition with designer configuration and PrintOutputFormat set to NONE. Navigate to the data object, run its Print Report task, and supply the output location/name/type. This does not verify an older REST guide or guarantee a file solely from HTTP status.
