entries.title: Lesson 1 - Excel Engine
entries.text: Lesson 01 - Excel Engine · Excel Modules reference (Tricentis docs)

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: Two different ways to reach Excel

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: Excel Standard Modules (file-level, background)
entries.text: Excel Standard Modules work with a workbook in the background without steering its visible window. Prefer data-level operations when the test concerns workbook data; inspect current engine prerequisites, including the executing user’s valid Office license.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: Excel UI Engine 3.0 (application-level)
entries.text: The Excel UI Engine 3.0 scans and steers the Microsoft Excel user interface itself — the main application window, its dialogs, and the worksheets with embedded controls currently loaded by the application. Use it when the thing under test genuinely is the Excel UI: a dialog that must appear, a ribbon interaction, an embedded control a user would click.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: The mandatory open/close pattern

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: Open Excel Workbook
entries.text: The mandatory first step of any Excel Standard Module sequence. It opens the workbook in the background and can handle password-protected files and read-only access. Nothing else in the Excel Module family works until the workbook has been opened.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: Close/Save Excel Workbook
entries.text: Close/Save Excel Workbook supports Save, Save & Close, or Close. Save Path controls the destination; Save As Type only applies with Save Path, and its type must match the file extension. Choose an operation that saves changes when required and closes resources at the end.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: Working with data: Ranges

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: Define Excel Range
entries.text: Define a named range for manipulation. Choose Explicit start/end cells or Used Range; the selected range affects row/column counts and indexing.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: Manipulate Excel Range
entries.text: The workhorse Module. It reads and writes cell data, and it also reaches the technical properties of cells — formulas, formatting, colors, fonts, and comments. Because it supports verification as well as input, this is the Module that satisfies the course objective 'verify Microsoft Excel cell special properties': you are not just checking the displayed value, you are checking that the underlying formula, the fill colour, or the font is what it should be.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: Clear Excel Range
entries.text: Removes content from a range — and selectively, not just the values: formatting, notes, comments, hyperlinks, or outlines can each be cleared. Useful for resetting a sheet between test runs.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: Comparing workbooks and running macros

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: Excel 1:1 File Compare
entries.text: Excel 1:1 File Compare can check data, formatting and objects. Formatting and object comparisons are off by default; enable Include Formats and Include Objects when required. Select the relevant sheets and an Output Path for evidence.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: Run Excel Macro
entries.text: Executes an existing Microsoft Excel macro from a TestStep, with a configurable timeout. Note the word existing — this Module runs a macro that already lives in the workbook; it is not a way to write VBA from Tosca. The timeout matters because a long-running macro would otherwise hang the TestCase.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: Lesson 2 - PDF Engine
entries.text: Lesson 02 - PDF Engine · Scan PDF files (Tricentis docs) · Compare PDF files (Tricentis docs) · Configure PDF anchors (Tricentis docs)

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: Scanning a PDF

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: The PDF Scan
entries.text: The PDF Scan defines document regions for testing. Unlike HTML scanning, this workflow selects text, image or table areas in the document. Start Scan → PDF from a Module folder or use Ctrl+Shift+P, choose a file, then inspect the selected content before saving the Module.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: Anchor controls: the core concept of this lesson

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: Why anchors exist
entries.text: A target may move when document content changes. Absolute coordinates can still be used for fixed layouts. Use an anchor when the target retains a stable position relative to a distinctive element on the same page.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: How it works at runtime
entries.text: At runtime the engine finds the anchor, then calculates the target region from its recorded offset. Both may move together; if the distance between them changes, anchor identification alone does not guarantee the correct target.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: Anchor accuracy

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: Type-specific defaults
entries.text: The dedicated Tosca 2026.1 anchor configuration page specifies 100% matching accuracy for text anchors and 99% for image anchors. The scan overview describes exact matching more generally; use the type-specific guidance when configuring the Module.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: Lowering accuracy
entries.text: For a problematic anchor, select its ModuleAttribute and add the transition parameter Accuracy in the Properties pane. Use an integer from 0 to 100. This setting controls anchor matching; it is different from the comparison Module’s Accuracy [%] and from forcing OCR during scanning.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: Comparing PDF files

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: PDF 1:1 Compare
entries.text: PDF 1:1 Compare compares a reference PDF with one or more targets using a configured minimum similarity, Accuracy [%]. Page by Page Image is the default. Full Text Content ignores text position and does not support OCR text recognition; Page by Page Text compares corresponding pages. Choose the mode that matches the assertion.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: Combining compare with exclusions
entries.text: Scan the variable region, save the Module, and use Copy Dimensions on its ModuleAttribute. In the comparison TestStep, populate the excluded area’s Dimensions and Page(s). This explicitly connects the scanned region to the exclusion; verify that the chosen region does not hide meaningful defects.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; provider guidance checked 2026-10-06
entries.title: Lesson 3 - Mail Engine
entries.text: Lesson 03 - Mail Engine · Mail Engine 3.0 (Tricentis docs) · Connect to Cloud Mail Server (Tricentis docs)

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; provider guidance checked 2026-10-06
entries.title: Why mail automation matters

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; provider guidance checked 2026-10-06
entries.title: Mail as part of the business process
entries.text: Very few end-to-end processes finish inside the application. Register an account and a confirmation email arrives; place an order and an order confirmation follows; reset a password and the whole flow depends on a link that only exists in an inbox. If the test stops at the web page, the part the customer actually receives goes untested.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; provider guidance checked 2026-10-06
entries.title: Mail Engine 3.0
entries.text: Mail Engine 3.0 is part of the standard Tosca installation. Current Standard subset location: Standard modules → Engines → Mail.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; provider guidance checked 2026-10-06
entries.title: Connecting to the mail server

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; provider guidance checked 2026-10-06
entries.title: Connect to Mail Server
entries.text: Connect to Mail Server defines a named server configuration. Network use occurs during sending or receiving, so this configuration step alone does not prove delivery or retrieval.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; provider guidance checked 2026-10-06
entries.title: Connect to Exchange Server
entries.text: Connect to Exchange Server configures an EWS endpoint. Current Authentication Type values are Basic (legacy) and OAuth, selected with ActionMode Select. OAuth uses App Id and Tenant Id from a Microsoft identity registration; token-acquisition failure can fail this step, unlike the legacy configuration path.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; provider guidance checked 2026-10-06
entries.title: OAuth 2.0 for Exchange Online / Microsoft 365
entries.text: Connect to Cloud Mail Server has a separate Microsoft Office 365 integration with Tenant Id, Application Id, Client Secret and Mailbox. Its documented prerequisites include a registered Entra application and Graph mail permissions. Google Workspace uses a service-account JSON key and domain-wide delegation. These integrations are not interchangeable with a generic SMTP server or a personal Gmail login.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; provider guidance checked 2026-10-06
entries.title: Real-world setup notes: Gmail and corporate mailboxes

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; provider guidance checked 2026-10-06
entries.title: Provider server settings
entries.text: Google documents imap.gmail.com:993 with SSL and smtp.gmail.com:587 with TLS (or 465 with SSL). Configure receiving and sending separately with their corresponding protocols and security enabled; successful use still depends on account policy and supported authentication.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; provider guidance checked 2026-10-06
entries.title: Sending mail

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; provider guidance checked 2026-10-06
entries.title: Send Mail
entries.text: The Send Mail Module sends — or replies to — an email message via SMTP. Typical uses in a test are triggering an inbound process (a system that acts on incoming mail), or generating a message the test will later verify was received and correctly handled.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; provider guidance checked 2026-10-06
entries.title: Receiving mail: Simple vs Expert

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; provider guidance checked 2026-10-06
entries.title: Receive Mail Simple
entries.text: Checks whether you received one specific, single email. This is the right choice for the common case: 'after registering, did the confirmation email arrive?' One expected message, one check.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; provider guidance checked 2026-10-06
entries.title: Receive Mail Expert
entries.text: Receive Mail Expert searches a set of messages and exposes a ResultCount plus individual Mail nodes. Use it when the test needs to assert the number of matches or inspect multiple results.

entries.moduleTitle: Lesson 4 - WinX Engine and UIA Engine
entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: Lesson 4 - WinX Engine and UIA Engine
entries.text: Lesson 04 - WinX Engine and UIA Engine · Steering UIA 3.0 Controls (Tricentis docs) · WinX controls (Tricentis docs)

entries.moduleTitle: Lesson 4 - WinX Engine and UIA Engine
entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: Two engines for one platform

entries.moduleTitle: Lesson 4 - WinX Engine and UIA Engine
entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: Why Windows needs two options
entries.text: Windows applications use different control technologies. UIA and WinX are two available engines, alongside technology-specific engines such as DotNet. Evaluate supported controls and identification before selecting an engine for a large automation suite.

entries.moduleTitle: Lesson 4 - WinX Engine and UIA Engine
entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: UIA Engine 3.0
entries.text: UIA Engine 3.0 accesses controls through Microsoft UI Automation. Tricentis recommends it when the corresponding standard engine does not support the controls but their UI Automation interface permits steering; this is not a guarantee that every Windows element is supported.

entries.moduleTitle: Lesson 4 - WinX Engine and UIA Engine
entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: WinX Engine
entries.text: WinX steers supported PowerBuilder applications and applications using the Windows UI API. Evaluate its control support and setup requirements rather than treating it as a universal alternative for any UIA identification failure.

entries.moduleTitle: Lesson 4 - WinX Engine and UIA Engine
entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: Making the choice at scan time

entries.moduleTitle: Lesson 4 - WinX Engine and UIA Engine
entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: Where the decision happens
entries.text: Open XScan with Modules → Scan → Application, or Scan → Application from a Module folder. In Select Application, right-click the target application and choose UIA or WinX, then scan and save its controls. This creates technology-specific Modules.

entries.moduleTitle: Lesson 4 - WinX Engine and UIA Engine
entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: Consequences of the choice
entries.text: A scanned Module contains engine-specific identification and control information. Selecting a different engine for another scan does not automatically convert existing Modules or TestSteps. Evaluate new Modules and affected test references before migrating.

entries.moduleTitle: Lesson 4 - WinX Engine and UIA Engine
entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: Working with the scanned controls

entries.moduleTitle: Lesson 4 - WinX Engine and UIA Engine
entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: Nothing new above the Module
entries.text: The Module → TestStep → TestStepValue workflow remains familiar. ActionModes and properties still depend on the control and engine; do not assume every control supports Input, Verify, Buffer and Select identically. UIA table cell input uses embedded controls.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: Lesson 5 - Self Healing
entries.text: Lesson 05 - Self Healing · Self-healing TestCases (Tricentis docs)

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: The problem self-healing addresses

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: Controls change; tests break
entries.text: An application under active development changes its controls constantly — an id gets renamed, a class is restructured, a button moves into a different container. Nothing about the business behaviour changed, but the automation can no longer find the control and the TestCase fails. Investigating and repairing these false failures is one of the biggest ongoing maintenance costs in test automation.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: Self-healing Mode
entries.text: If ordinary identification fails, enabled self-healing attempts an alternative based on stored properties. A suitable match allows the current action to continue; no match, a wrong match or a failed later assertion can still make the test fail. Review healed actions before accepting their results.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: Turning it on: the SelfHealing TCP

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: A test configuration parameter, not a checkbox
entries.text: Self-healing is activated by creating a test configuration parameter named SelfHealing. Because it is a TCP, it inherits the usual scoping rules — set it high in the folder structure to apply broadly, or on a specific TestCase to limit it.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: SelfHealingWeightThreshold
entries.text: For Weighted mode, SelfHealingWeightThreshold defaults to 0.75. Candidate combinations below the accumulated-weight cutoff are ignored; this is not a calibrated probability that a match is correct. Use the decimal separator required by regional settings.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: Self-Healing Properties

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: Where the technical data lives
entries.text: Self-Healing Properties are the technical attributes of a control that give Tosca something to match against when the primary identification fails. They sit on the Self-Healing Properties tab of the ModuleAttribute — one level deeper than the identification you normally work with.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: They are created for you
entries.text: Tosca adds these properties automatically when a Module is created through XScan, Tosca Rescan, Salesforce Scan, or the Tricentis Automation Recording Assistant. You do not have to author them by hand — though you can edit, delete, or add properties manually after scanning if the automatic set is not right.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: Seeing and keeping the results

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: Spotting a self-healed run
entries.text: An icon on ExecutionEntries and the ExecutionLog Detail column identify healed objects. Inspect those details alongside assertions and the final result instead of interpreting every healed run as a clean pass.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: Apply Self-Healing properties
entries.text: Review the replacement control and its assertions first. If the change is correct, use Apply Self-Healing properties on the ExecutionLog to update the Module. This commits identification changes; it does not prove the chosen control or business behavior is correct.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: Which engines support it

entries.moduleTitle: Lesson 6 - Install and Use Custom Controls
entries.title: Lesson 6 - Install and Use Custom Controls
entries.text: Lesson 06 - Install and Use Custom Controls · Custom controls (Tricentis docs)

entries.moduleTitle: Lesson 6 - Install and Use Custom Controls
entries.title: The problem: widgets that aren't standard controls

entries.moduleTitle: Lesson 6 - Install and Use Custom Controls
entries.title: When an engine sees the wrong thing
entries.text: Standard identification works because the engine recognises a control as something it understands — a text box, a checkbox, a table. Complex or third-party UI widgets break that assumption. A custom date picker, a rich grid, or a bespoke component may be built from dozens of nested primitive elements, so the engine sees a pile of divs or panels rather than one meaningful control. You can sometimes still automate it, but the steering is fragile and the Module is unreadable.

entries.moduleTitle: Lesson 6 - Install and Use Custom Controls
entries.title: Custom controls
entries.text: The public Tosca Cloud documentation describes custom DLLs that adapt complex widgets to standard UI elements. An extension’s actual recognition and steering capabilities depend on its implementation and the supported product/version; this description does not verify on-prem installation steps.

entries.moduleTitle: Lesson 6 - Install and Use Custom Controls
entries.title: Where custom controls come from

entries.moduleTitle: Lesson 6 - Install and Use Custom Controls
entries.title: Not something you author in Tosca Commander
entries.text: The available Cloud guide directs users to their Tricentis contact for custom DLLs. It does not establish that every widget already has an adapter, or that extensions can never be developed for an on-prem installation.

entries.moduleTitle: Lesson 6 - Install and Use Custom Controls
entries.title: Making them available
entries.text: Cloud administrators upload through Configurations → Uploads → Custom controls; Launcher distributes those files. The guide explicitly says this does not affect on-prem customizations. The original AE1 on-prem package and installation instructions were unavailable during review, so no DLL path, restart requirement or activation procedure is verified here.

entries.moduleTitle: Lesson 6 - Install and Use Custom Controls
entries.title: Using them and where they fit

entries.moduleTitle: Lesson 6 - Install and Use Custom Controls
entries.title: After installation, nothing special
entries.text: With a compatible adapter, scan and check the recognized control and supported operations. Continue through the ordinary Module/TestStep workflow only after confirming that the adapter supports the required actions.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercise recipe unverified
entries.title: Lesson 7 - Standard Modules
entries.text: Lesson 07 - Standard Modules · File Operations (Tricentis docs) · Folder Operations (Tricentis docs)

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercise recipe unverified
entries.title: Why file automation belongs in a test

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercise recipe unverified
entries.title: Setup, teardown, and evidence
entries.text: Most non-trivial TestCases touch the file system somewhere. A test needs an input file placed in a watched folder before it starts; an export must be verified after it runs; yesterday's output has to be cleared so today's run is clean; a generated report needs archiving as evidence. Doing any of that by hand defeats the point of automation, and the Standard subset provides Modules for all of it — no scanning and no engine-specific work required.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercise recipe unverified
entries.title: Folder Operations

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercise recipe unverified
entries.title: File Operations: creating and reading

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercise recipe unverified
entries.title: TBox Read/Create File
entries.text: The dual-purpose workhorse: it creates files and writes text content, and it also verifies or buffers text content from an existing file. Encoding is configurable — UTF-8, UTF-16 and ISO-8859-1 are supported, with an optional byte order mark setting. Buffering content out of a file is how you feed data read from disk into later TestSteps.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercise recipe unverified
entries.title: TBox Append File
entries.text: Append File adds text and creates the file if absent. Optional encoding and newline settings apply; this does not guarantee that an invalid path, permissions or conflicting file lock can be ignored.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercise recipe unverified
entries.title: File Operations: moving, copying, deleting

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercise recipe unverified
entries.title: TBox Copy File
entries.text: Duplicates a file into another directory. The target directory must already exist at run time — this Module will not create it for you, which is why a TBox Create Folder step often precedes it. Tricentis also notes the Module might not work if a security and password management tool is in play.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercise recipe unverified
entries.title: TBox Move/Rename File
entries.text: Relocates a file, renames it, or both. As with Copy File, the target directory must pre-exist for a move to succeed.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercise recipe unverified
entries.title: TBox Delete File
entries.text: Delete File returns a positive result when no matching file is found. This permits missing-file cleanup but does not prove prior existence or guarantee success for permission, lock or path errors.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercise recipe unverified
entries.title: File Operations: verifying and comparing

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercise recipe unverified
entries.title: TBox File Existence
entries.text: Verifies whether a file exists in a directory. It supports negation with '!' (assert a file is absent), wildcards with '*' (match a pattern rather than an exact name), and the WaitOn ActionMode — which is what you use when a file is produced asynchronously and the test must wait for it to appear rather than checking once and failing.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercise recipe unverified
entries.title: TBox File Compare
entries.text: Compares the content of two files and can optionally generate a diff report. Where the second file has additional content, the Module highlights that in green in the report — useful when the question is not merely 'are these identical?' but 'what changed?'.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercise recipe unverified
entries.title: TBox Image Compare
entries.text: Verifies image files (BMP, JPG, GIF) with a pixel-accurate comparison — an exact pixel match, not a similarity threshold. Note the contrast with PDF 1:1 Compare from Lesson 2, which passes when similarity exceeds an accuracy you specify. Image Compare is the stricter of the two.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercise recipe unverified
entries.title: Matching actions to Engines: Excel, Database, Browser, and Expressions

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercise recipe unverified
entries.title: Excel UI Engine 3.0
entries.text: Steers the MS Excel application itself — driving it the way a user would, through its own interface. Use it when the TestCase needs to interact with Excel as an application, not just its data.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercise recipe unverified
entries.title: Excel Engine 3.0
entries.text: Excel Engine works with workbook content without driving the visible Excel UI. Choose it for content operations; installed prerequisites still apply and it is not universally faster or more stable than UI steering.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercise recipe unverified
entries.title: Database Engine 3.0
entries.text: Database Engine executes database operations through SQL statements. Use its compatible open/operate/close Modules or DB Expert; confirm the supported connection and driver.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercise recipe unverified
entries.title: HTML modules
entries.text: Cover browser and document-level actions that sit above individual HTML controls — such as Execute JavaScript, Open a URL, and Close Browser. These act on the browser session itself, not on a specific button or field inside the page.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercise recipe unverified
entries.title: TBox Evaluation Tool
entries.text: TBox Evaluation Tool verifies expressions that resolve to TRUE or FALSE. Use ActionMode Verify, quote values intended as strings, and account for supported dynamic expressions and NCalc special-character escaping. A string representation of a date is not automatically a chronological date comparison.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercise recipe unverified
entries.title: The XML Engine's Standard Modules

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercise recipe unverified
entries.title: Resource vs. file
entries.text: An XML Resource is Tosca's in-memory working copy — Create XML Resource makes one without any file on disk. Open/Create XML file can either make a brand-new file or load an existing one as a Resource. Save XML file is the step that commits an in-memory Resource's changes back to disk.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercise recipe unverified
entries.title: Bonus: the JSON Engine — reading a repeating array with one TestCase

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercise recipe unverified
entries.title: JSON structure and identification
entries.text: Current JSON Module guidance uses XScan. JSON object members are identified by name and treated as unordered pairs; array entries are positional and named item#<position>. Verify the generated structure and data types rather than assuming every export workflow is identical.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercise recipe unverified
entries.title: ExplicitName enables name editing
entries.text: The Configuration Param ExplicitName=True permits editing the referenced XTestStepValue name. It does not itself activate wildcard matching or prove that a chosen name selects every JSON array entry.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercise recipe unverified
entries.title: Counts and repetition are separate concerns
entries.text: ResultCount describes occurrences of the current node. TestStepFolder Repetition accepts a non-negative integer or dynamic expression, and {REPETITION} identifies the current pass. For variable-length JSON, validate counting and position selection against the actual Module; repetition alone does not guarantee coverage of each array element.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercise recipe unverified
entries.title: Windows, Buffer, and Process Operations — matching actions to Modules

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercise recipe unverified
entries.title: TBox Dialog
entries.text: TBox Dialog handles standard Microsoft Windows dialogs without scanning. Customized dialogs must be scanned first. Caption identifies the dialog window, optional Label further narrows it using message text, and Button supplies the text of the button to confirm. JavaScript dialogs have a separate HTML Module, Steer Dialog Box.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: Lesson 8 - Image Based Controls
entries.text: Lesson 08 - Image Based Controls · Identify controls by image: Image-Based Test Automation (Tricentis docs) · Identify controls by anchor (Tricentis docs)

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: Image-Based Test Automation (IBTA)

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: Identifying by what it looks like
entries.text: XScan can pair a selected control with one or more screenshot identifiers. Image matching provides appearance-based identification when that fits the target, but still requires a visible, sufficiently distinctive identifier.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: How to create one
entries.text: In XScan Advanced View, select the control and choose ADVANCED IDENTIFICATION → IMAGE. Add an identifier image, capture its region and inspect uniqueness. Set Accuracy and choose Method Fullscreen, Controlbased or Auto as appropriate.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: Making image identification as reliable as it can be

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: Use more than one screenshot
entries.text: Capture necessary variants when a control’s appearance changes. Tosca tries identifiers sequentially until it finds a match, so additional images increase execution time. Limit them to what is needed, and verify that each identifier selects the intended control.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: What still breaks it
entries.text: Keep scan and execution display settings consistent. Multiple identifiers can cover known variants; they do not guarantee tolerance of arbitrary redesigns, scaling or rendering changes. A non-unique identifier remains unreliable even if Module creation is permitted.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: The other Advanced Identification method: Anchor

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: Identify by anchor
entries.text: In XScan Advanced View, select the target and choose ADVANCED IDENTIFICATION → ANCHOR. Assign a reference control from the tree, screen or Auto Select. This establishes an anchor context for locating the target; it is not the PDF Scan’s text/image/same-page rule set.

entries.title: What TMA does for you
entries.text: Mobile automation traditionally means assembling a toolchain — Appium, Java components, environment variables, device drivers — before a single test can run. The Tricentis Mobile Agent (TMA) provides simplified setup and configuration of iOS and Android devices so that none of that is your problem: you do not need to install Appium, Java components, or configure environment variables yourself.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS / TMA 2025.4; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: Mobile Engine 3.0
entries.text: Mobile Engine 3.0 steers supported mobile applications through a configured connection. Modules use the familiar Tosca TestCase workflow, but application type, supported controls, capabilities and device preparation still affect execution.

entries.title: Local vs Remote connections

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS / TMA 2025.4; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: Local (TMA)
entries.text: Local (TMA) uses a locally connected supported device or Android emulator. Select a device explicitly when required by the topology; a single local Android device does not require DeviceName. Check the requirements for the installed Agent version.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS / TMA 2025.4; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: Remote (TMA)
entries.text: Remote (TMA) reaches an Agent on another machine and its supported device, emulator or simulator. Remote TMA is distinct from connecting directly to a cloud provider’s Appium endpoint.

entries.title: Preparing an Android device

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS / TMA 2025.4; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: Scanning and building the TestCase

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS / TMA 2025.4; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: Mobile Scan
entries.text: The Mobile Scan handles native, hybrid, and web applications on mobile. The sequence is: prepare the test environment, start the Mobile Scan and connect to your device, then add the mobile device, emulator, or simulator you want to scan against. From there, scanning produces Modules the same way it does for any other technology.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS / TMA 2025.4; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: Configuring the connection with TCPs
entries.text: The connection to a device, emulator, or simulator is established through test configuration parameters. This is the same TCP mechanism used elsewhere in Tosca — for the TestDataService endpoint, for SelfHealing — so the scoping rules you already know apply.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS / TMA 2025.4; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: Open the correct application type
entries.text: Use Open Mobile App for native/hybrid applications before steering them. The Standard Mobile Module reference documents an exception: Set Desired Capabilities may precede it. Mobile websites instead start with OpenUrl, Browser=ChromeAndroid or SafariiOS, and UseActiveTab left empty.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS / TMA 2025.4; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: Remote setup and diagnostic boundaries

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS / TMA 2025.4; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: Use the documented endpoint format
entries.text: The Tosca mobile configuration guide gives remote addresses as http://<ip_address>:<port_number>/. Keep the documented trailing slash. It does not establish that every missing-slash failure has one exact error or that the Scan wizard always tolerates it.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS / TMA 2025.4; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: REST binding is not the Appium port
entries.text: The TMA 2025.4 CLI binds services to localhost by default. Use --rest-address <IP>:<port> for a reachable web-server binding. --appium-port configures Appium separately; --grpc-address configures gRPC. Match the service endpoint required by Tosca rather than treating these switches as interchangeable.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS / TMA 2025.4; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: Diagnose one layer at a time
entries.text: Check Agent/device availability, the endpoint from the Tosca host, session logs, capabilities and application identifiers. A connected or idle device status alone cannot rule out firewall, routing, permissions or session-creation problems. No undocumented REST response schema is required for this lesson.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS / TMA 2025.4; original AE1 exercises unverified
entries.title: Choose supported host hardware
entries.text: TMA 2025.4 documents bare-metal hosts and requires the Android emulator to run on the same machine as the Agent. It supports Android Studio for Android virtual devices and Xcode for iOS virtual devices. Confirm host architecture, OS and emulator support for your installed versions before setup.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exam blueprint unverified
entries.title: Where this module sits

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exam blueprint unverified
entries.title: What Vision AI is

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exam blueprint unverified
entries.title: Seeing the UI the way a person does
entries.text: Conventional scanning reads an application's technical structure — element ids, class names, the control tree. Vision AI instead analyses the application's visual components, using two neural networks: one for finding controls and one for optical character recognition (OCR). It identifies what is on screen much as a human tester would: this looks like a text field, that is a button labelled 'Submit'.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exam blueprint unverified
entries.title: Recognising control types, not just pixels
entries.text: The crucial detail is that Vision AI detects control types and adjusts its steering mechanism to the classification it has made. Having decided a region is a dropdown, it steers it as a dropdown. This is what separates it from raw appearance matching.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exam blueprint unverified
entries.title: Vision AI vs the two methods you already know

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exam blueprint unverified
entries.title: Versus property-based scanning
entries.text: Vision AI uses visual recognition rather than relying on the target’s DOM identifiers. Changes to technical attributes may therefore leave a visual locator usable, but labels, layout, detection quality and steering support still require validation.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exam blueprint unverified
entries.title: Versus image-based controls (Lesson 8)
entries.text: Image identifiers match a captured appearance. Vision AI detects control types and uses type-specific steering. Classification can require adjustment; neither method guarantees reliable execution after arbitrary visual changes.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exam blueprint unverified
entries.title: When automatic recognition is not enough

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exam blueprint unverified
entries.title: User Identified Controls (UIDCs)
entries.text: When detection is unsuitable, XScan can adjust the ControlType among detected choices, refine labels or create a User Identified Control (UIDC). In Advanced View, define the target region, control type and application category, select anchor controls, save and rescan. UIDC definitions are shared within the company.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exam blueprint unverified
entries.title: Anchors, again
entries.text: UIDCs use reference controls inside or outside the target region. A single anchor preserves a fixed relative size/position and may fail when sizes vary. Prefer unique text labels and multiple appropriate anchors for variable dimensions; use UidcCategory for the defined application group.

entries.version: Tosca 2026.1 LTS public documentation; original AE1 exam blueprint unverified
entries.title: When to reach for it
Grand Scenario - Demo Web Shop
entries.text: Grand Scenario - Demo Web Shop · Reusable TestStepLibraries · Capture and reuse dynamic values

entries.title: What the Grand Scenario is for
From isolated lessons to one business process
entries.text: This local worked scenario combines login, book ordering, invoice download and logout to illustrate cross-technology test design. The original Academy base subset and exact exercise sequence have not been inspected, so the labels and steps below are an independent teaching example, not a certified reproduction.

entries.title: Why the scenario is split into three
entries.text: In this local example, Precondition establishes the starting session, Process exercises ordering and Post condition verifies logout and closes the browser. These names are a design choice, not a Tosca-required folder structure. Session cleanup does not delete orders or restore all business data.

entries.title: The 'Login to web shop' reusable block
entries.text: Logging in is needed by the Precondition and would be needed by any other scenario against the same shop. Rather than duplicating those steps, the scenario keeps a TestStepLibrary containing a reusable TestStep block named 'Login to web shop', made up of three steps: Open demo web shop, Click on log in link, and Provide log in details.

entries.title: Why this matters beyond tidiness
entries.text: References to a Reusable TestStepBlock share centrally maintained steps; changes affect all linked references. A resolved reference becomes an independent copy, so it no longer receives those changes. Updating shared steps still requires validating callers and their assertions.

entries.title: The Process TestCase, step by step
Three TestStep folders
entries.text: This independent flow groups ordering into three folders for readability. A folder label helps locate a phase but does not prove the root cause of a failure or verify the original Academy sequence.

entries.title: The two techniques that make it work
Buffering the order number
entries.text: Capture the current order identifier with ActionMode Buffer, or use XBuffer within a verified message to extract its dynamic part. Later steps read {B[OrderID]}. Do not assume the identifier differs on every run; use the value actually produced by the application.

entries.title: Crossing into the PDF Engine
entries.text: Downloading the invoice is a browser/file operation, not automatic PDF verification. Verify the file is available, then use PDF Modules for the chosen checks. Content extraction and reference comparison are distinct operations. Configure explicit page/area exclusions only for allowed differences; verify the captured order identifier separately rather than hiding an important mismatch.

The current guide distinguishes Mobile Engine 3.0 and Mobile Web Engine 3.0 scanning/steering paths.

entries.title: A separate installer from Tosca Commander
entries.text: TMA is installed separately from Tosca Commander using the package for its host operating system. Local/remote deployment changes topology and configuration, not the authoring model. Windows, macOS and Linux installation steps are different; use the matching official guide.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca Mobile - Getting Started with Mobile Test Automation
entries.title: Default startup binds locally
entries.text: The TMA 2025.4 CLI guide states that services bind to localhost by default. A default local start is suitable only when the caller can reach those local bindings; check actual configuration rather than assuming every customized GUI start has the same bindings.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca Mobile - Getting Started with Mobile Test Automation
entries.title: Command-line launch with --rest-address — required for remote use
entries.text: For the documented cross-machine connection, start with tricentis-mobile-agent start --rest-address <IP>:<port>. This binds the web server to the chosen address. Appium and gRPC have separate --appium-port and --grpc-address settings; use the endpoint required by each consumer.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca Mobile - Getting Started with Mobile Test Automation
entries.title: Ports and firewalls

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca Mobile - Getting Started with Mobile Test Automation
entries.title: Distinguish service ports
entries.text: The Tosca configuration guide documents 8585 as the default Appium port; the TMA preparation guide also uses http://localhost:8585/ for its interface. Remote examples use a configured REST binding. Inspect the actual endpoints and permit the necessary traffic; do not infer one universal REST port from an Appium example.

entries.title: Device Management
entries.text: Device management lists detected devices and their information. Inspect availability before session creation, but a device entry or ready status is only one diagnostic signal. Authorization, capabilities, target app and network paths still need validation.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca Mobile - Getting Started with Mobile Test Automation
entries.title: Version alignment with Tosca
entries.text: Check the release notes and documented compatibility for the installed Agent and Tosca versions. The TMA upgrade guide installs the matching OS package to replace the previous Agent and retain configuration/devices. Version numbers do not imply a required one-to-one matching release.

entries.text: Add capabilities set creates a named group; Add capability adds an entry to the selected group. Select Capability Set applies that group to the scan. It is not a separate one-off versus reusable mechanism.

entries.text: A hybrid app wraps one or more web views inside a native shell. From the outside it looks and behaves like a native app, but part or all of its content is actually rendered as HTML/CSS/JS inside an embedded browser engine.

entries.title: Application opening and capability ordering
entries.text: Use Open Mobile App to begin native/hybrid application steering. Desired Capabilities setup is the documented exception: Set Desired Capabilities, and any additions, precede application opening. Mobile websites use OpenUrl.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca Mobile - Getting Started with Mobile Test Automation
entries.moduleTitle: Lesson 7 - Building Your First Mobile TestCase
entries.title: What Open Mobile App actually does
entries.text: It's more than a click-through step: Open Mobile App creates the mobile device session (via TMA) for the TestCase, and it can install the app on the device at the start of that session if an install source (a local .apk path, or the equivalent iOS install path) is configured — or, for an app already on the device, open it directly by its identifier: BundleID for iOS, or AppPackage/AppActivity for Android.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca Mobile - Getting Started with Mobile Test Automation
entries.moduleTitle: Lesson 7 - Building Your First Mobile TestCase
entries.title: Switch Mobile App
entries.text: For TestCases that move between apps mid-flow (e.g. testing a deep link handoff, or a share-sheet interaction that opens a different app), Switch Mobile App changes the active app context without needing a second Open Mobile App step.

entries.title: What stays the same across all three
entries.text: Native, hybrid and mobile web tests share Tosca’s Module/TestStepValue and supported ActionMode concepts. Opening differs: native/hybrid apps use Open Mobile App after any required capability setup; websites use OpenUrl. Buffer stores data; Verify performs assertions.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca Mobile - Getting Started with Mobile Test Automation
entries.moduleTitle: Automating Mobile Apps on TMA — Part 2: Testing Native, Hybrid & Web Apps
entries.title: What actually changes
entries.text: Native controls use exposed platform properties. Hybrid flows combine native and web content with the appropriate context. Mobile web scanning/execution defaults to Mobile Web Engine 3.0, with version-specific legacy alternatives; it is not one identical engine path for every app type.

entries.text: Tosca documents a DeviceName value that requests Appium dynamic selection of a connected Android or iOS device. This independent local guide explains that setting and operational checks; it does not reproduce an unavailable Academy exercise or certify a scheduling policy.

entries.title: DeviceName selection value
entries.text: Set DeviceName to TOSCA_DYNAMIC_DEVICE_SELECTION to request that Appium dynamically select a connected iOS or Android device. This is a documented literal value, not arbitrary wildcard syntax or a criterion expression. The guide does not establish a Ready/non-Busy scheduler, fairness, queue timing or reservation guarantee.

entries.title: Why go past the console
entries.text: Agent and driver logs can provide information about failed sessions beyond a status summary. Tosca’s Log Viewer adds execution evidence and supports text/regex search. Logging detail and retained history vary; preserve the relevant run before logs expire.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca Mobile - Getting Started with Mobile Test Automation

entries.title: Session correlation
entries.text: Use a session ID where present together with timestamps, target information and the failing command to correlate a run. Do not assume every log line contains that ID or that a session-creation failure produced an ID. Correlation helps locate evidence; it does not edit controls or TestCase data.

entries.title: The gap it fills
entries.text: Image matching can help when stable usable control properties are unavailable, including some custom-rendered surfaces. Inspect the actual hierarchy and identifiers first: a canvas, map or chart does not universally imply that no accessible target exists.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca Mobile - Getting Started with Mobile Test Automation
entries.moduleTitle: Advanced Use Cases - Image-Based Test Automation (IBTA)
entries.title: What IBTA matches on
entries.text: A captured target image and optional additional reference images help locate an on-screen control. Accuracy controls how closely the image must match. Successful identification locates a target; separate assertions are still needed to verify business behavior.

entries.trackName: Tricentis Tosca Mobile - Getting Started with Mobile Test Automation

entries.title: Matching tolerance
entries.text: Higher Accuracy requires a closer match; lowering it allows more differences and may admit unintended regions. Additional reference images and supported resolution search methods can help. Validate both intended matches and competing similar regions; do not blindly lower accuracy until a run passes.

entries.title: Connection TCPs versus tuning TCPs
entries.text: Documented mobile TCPs configure connection, target and execution behavior. TMAServer and DeviceName are connection/target examples; LiveView, ScreenFlow, ScrollToVisible and TapByCoordinates control other documented behavior. Type is a Mobile Scan selection, not a generic execution TCP listed in the mobile TCP table. Invalid values in either group can produce errors; failure timing is not a guaranteed classification.

entries.title: Reset application and test independence
entries.text: Establish the application, account and relevant backend state required by each test. A driver-specific application reset may be useful, but a scan checkbox does not certify execution reset, complete backend cleanup or independence of every subsequent test.

entries.title: The same TestCase, several environments
entries.text: TCPs are supported on multiple Tosca objects, including the project root, relevant folders, TestCases, ExecutionLists and ExecutionEntries. Child objects inherit values and lower-level values can override them. Bundled configurations support reuse; inspect effective values for each environment rather than inventing a fixed Project → Configuration → environment hierarchy.

entries.title: Fix it once, not in every TestCase
entries.text: A reusable Module stores control identification and supported steering configuration. Changes can affect tests that reference it, so validate the affected usages. Not every wait, focus, keyboard or transition behavior is a configurable Module property; some require TCPs, Modules or scenario-specific TestStepValues.

entries.title: Why realistic matters on mobile
entries.text: Use the supported interaction path and verify the required business outcome. If a scenario explicitly depends on focus, confirmation or another action, establish that it occurred; a final stored value alone may not demonstrate the required path. This is a local testing principle, not a claim that every native value-setting operation bypasses user behavior.

entries.title: Session-level configuration, not TestCase logic
entries.text: Appium capabilities are supplied when a session starts and cannot be changed during that session’s lifecycle. Driver-supported Settings APIs can change some runtime behavior without changing the session capabilities; distinguish those mechanisms. Tosca scan capability sets and execution Set/Add Desired Capabilities Modules are separate configuration paths.

entries.text: For a workflow that needs granted permissions, a supported automatic grant may be appropriate. For permission or alert behavior coverage, use controlled initial state and explicitly verify the required dialogs and outcomes. Suppression is not a universal recommended default for the whole suite.

entries.text: Mobile tests can run in parallel on multiple devices, and can use DEX or CI orchestration. entries.moduleTitle: Creating your first codeless test in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Creating your first codeless test in Tricentis Testim
entries.text: Web Testing Getting Started (Codeless Test) (Tricentis docs) · Recording a Web Test (Tricentis docs) · Editing target element properties (Tricentis docs) · Running tests overview (Tricentis docs)

entries.moduleTitle: Creating your first codeless test in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Creating a basic test by recording

entries.moduleTitle: Creating your first codeless test in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: The AUT browser
entries.text: Creating a test starts by navigating to the relevant website inside the Application Under Test (AUT) browser window and recording the series of actions you want tested — clicks, text entry, scrolling, navigation. Testim captures each action as a step.

entries.moduleTitle: Creating your first codeless test in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Steps
entries.text: Recorded actions appear as individual steps with action-type icons. Execution follows the configured sequence; edit the test as needed rather than assuming the original recording order is permanent.

entries.moduleTitle: Creating your first codeless test in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Smart Locators and identification resilience

entries.moduleTitle: Creating your first codeless test in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Smart Locators
entries.text: Testim identifies targets using many weighted attributes and can improve identification across runs. Other useful attributes may preserve a match after a change, but resilience does not guarantee success or the correct target in every changed UI.

entries.moduleTitle: Creating your first codeless test in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Saving a test and viewing results

entries.moduleTitle: Creating your first codeless test in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Saving
entries.text: Save the named test in the project library. Editor, CLI and scheduling provide different execution paths; available configuration and permissions still govern a run.

entries.moduleTitle: Creating your first codeless test in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Viewing results
entries.text: Inspect executed-step statuses and available error details, including expected and actual validation values. Failure evidence supports diagnosis but is not a guarantee that the root cause is already identified.
