entries.text: Testim overview (Tricentis docs) · Running Tests Overview (Tricentis docs) · Validation (Tricentis docs) · Index (Tricentis docs) · Editing target element properties (Tricentis docs) · Run multiple tests locally (Tricentis docs) · Running tests on multiple browsers (Tricentis docs) · Validate element visible (Tricentis docs) · Validate element not visible (Tricentis docs) · Validate element text (Tricentis docs)

entries.moduleTitle: Tricentis Testim Fundamentals − Creating Automated Tests
entries.title: The Testim visual editor

entries.moduleTitle: Tricentis Testim Fundamentals − Creating Automated Tests
entries.title: Visual, codeless-first editing
entries.text: Testim's visual test editor has features built directly into the UI so that customizing a test — reordering steps, editing properties, adding validations — does not require writing code, while still allowing custom JavaScript steps for advanced cases (covered later in this learning path).

entries.moduleTitle: Tricentis Testim Fundamentals − Creating Automated Tests
entries.title: Base URL
entries.text: The project default base URL initializes new tests; an individual test can use another URL. It is the starting AUT address, not the editor address. For target editing, open the AUT and reach the relevant test state; opening only the initial page may not expose a later target.

entries.moduleTitle: Tricentis Testim Fundamentals − Creating Automated Tests
entries.title: Running tests: editor vs. Test List

entries.moduleTitle: Tricentis Testim Fundamentals − Creating Automated Tests
entries.title: Running from the editor
entries.text: The editor runs the open test locally or on a configured remote grid. Use the Play dropdown for Run on grid and choose the applicable configuration. Local editor playback uses Chrome; a single grid run is distinct from a cross-browser matrix.

entries.moduleTitle: Tricentis Testim Fundamentals − Creating Automated Tests
entries.title: Running from the Test List
entries.text: One or more tests can be selected in the Test List (Ctrl/Cmd-click for multiple) and run together with the Play button. Tests run this way execute locally, which is useful for quickly re-checking a batch of related tests without leaving the Test List view.

entries.moduleTitle: Tricentis Testim Fundamentals − Creating Automated Tests
entries.title: From actions to assertions: basic validations

entries.moduleTitle: Tricentis Testim Fundamentals − Creating Automated Tests
entries.title: Why validations matter
entries.text: Successful action replay establishes that those steps executed, not every business outcome or overall application health. Add assertions at meaningful outcomes; a click-through recording alone does not establish correctness.

entries.moduleTitle: Tricentis Testim Fundamentals − Creating Automated Tests
entries.title: Core validation types
entries.text: Visible checks element existence and visibility, not its specific content. Text checks the chosen element’s expected content and supports Regex in Expected Value. The documented not-visible step is web-only: it asserts absence from view, not necessarily removal from the DOM.

entries.moduleTitle: How to edit tests in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: How to edit tests in Tricentis Testim
entries.text: Editing Target Element Properties (Tricentis docs) · Shared Steps (Tricentis docs) · Steps (Tricentis docs) · Editing a steps properties (primary documentation) · Index (primary documentation) · Auto complete (primary documentation) · Index (primary documentation) · Labels (primary documentation) · Revisions (primary documentation) · Generating a random value (primary documentation) · Generating a date (primary documentation) · Extract text (primary documentation) · Checkbox and radio button validation (primary documentation) · Parameters for groups (primary documentation) · Validate element text (primary documentation) · Variables (primary documentation) · JavaScript identifier rules (MDN)

entries.moduleTitle: How to edit tests in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: The target element and its Properties panel

entries.moduleTitle: How to edit tests in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Target element
entries.text: A step’s target is the selected AUT element, represented by a thumbnail in Properties. Open Show Properties to edit supported settings; available fields depend on the step type.

entries.moduleTitle: How to edit tests in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Opening the Properties panel
entries.text: Hovering over any step in the test and clicking Show Properties opens the Properties panel on the right-hand side. From there, hovering over the target element thumbnail reveals four options: Highlight, Reassign, Improve, and View locators.

entries.moduleTitle: How to edit tests in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: The four Target Element options

entries.moduleTitle: How to edit tests in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Highlight
entries.text: Highlight temporarily emphasizes the selected target in the AUT for inspection; it does not replace locators or highlight every element matching a class.

entries.moduleTitle: How to edit tests in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Reassign
entries.text: Reassign chooses a different target and replaces its locators. Use it when the intended target has genuinely changed.

entries.moduleTitle: How to edit tests in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Improve
entries.text: Improve updates identification for the existing target after a DOM change, comparing captured and current attributes. Reach the relevant AUT state and verify the resulting target.

entries.moduleTitle: How to edit tests in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: View locators
entries.text: View locators displays weighted target and parent attributes. Resilience is not guaranteed; manual locator edits disable future Auto Improve for those locators, and the documentation recommends consulting support.

entries.moduleTitle: How to edit tests in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Specialized step properties

entries.moduleTitle: How to edit tests in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Expected value
entries.text: The value Testim checks for when the step runs (used by Validate element text, Validate CSS property, Validate HTML attribute, Wait for element text). It's editable after the step is created, and — importantly — it isn't limited to a literal string: Parameters, regular expressions, and JavaScript expressions can all be used in the Expected value field.

entries.moduleTitle: How to edit tests in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Expected status (checkboxes / radio buttons)
entries.text: Used by Validate checkbox and Validate radio button to set whether the step expects Checked (the default) or Unchecked. These validations only work on native checkbox/radio input elements — a custom checkbox implementation that doesn't use an underlying native input isn't supported.

entries.moduleTitle: How to edit tests in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Add Prefix / Add Suffix / String type / Length
entries.text: Generate random value sets character type and random length. Optional prefixes and suffixes can contain quoted strings or existing variables/expressions; they are not restricted to fixed strings.

entries.moduleTitle: How to edit tests in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Date format / Time difference / Use UTC
entries.text: Generate date uses configurable format tokens (default YYYY-MM-DD), a signed time offset and browser time or UTC. Check the required input format; do not confuse format tokens with an arbitrary JavaScript Date object.

entries.moduleTitle: How to edit tests in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Extract Mode
entries.text: Extract Mode selects the whole text or number/date/Regex matches. Individual extracted matches remain strings; All matches modes return arrays. Convert deliberately before numeric calculations.

entries.moduleTitle: How to edit tests in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Variable name and Variable scope
entries.text: Choose a valid JavaScript identifier; dollar signs and underscores are allowed. Generated values default to Test scope; Local limits scope and Suite shares it across suite tests. Consult the individual step’s documentation: the Extract Value page describes Local availability differently from the general Properties table.

entries.moduleTitle: How to edit tests in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Native events (Click step)
entries.text: Click can use native browser events or synthetic events. The Native events setting is a possible troubleshooting change, not proof that event type caused every click-without-effect failure; inspect target, readiness and outcome.

entries.moduleTitle: How to edit tests in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Pre-step delay (ms)
entries.text: Pre-step delay postpones the not-visible check. It does not continuously monitor absence or prove the element cannot appear after the check.

entries.moduleTitle: How to edit tests in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Sleep duration
entries.text: The property of a Sleep step — how long (in ms) the test pauses before the next step. The default is 1 second (1,000 ms), and it's directly editable.

entries.moduleTitle: How to edit tests in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: +PARAMS
entries.text: Supported custom, API and network steps expose PARAMS for HTML and JavaScript inputs. Parameters let callers supply different data to the same logic.

entries.moduleTitle: How to edit tests in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Auto complete
entries.text: While recording a test, Testim watches for a match against your existing Shared Groups and suggests them as the next steps — a pop-up labeled 'Auto record your steps' appears above the steps counter listing the matching suggestions. Clicking a suggestion has Testim automatically perform and save those steps in the test being recorded, instead of you re-recording a sequence you've already built elsewhere. If the matched group has parameters, you're prompted to name them and supply values before the steps are added. This feature is available on the professional plan.

entries.moduleTitle: How to edit tests in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Replace with a clone / See old revisions
entries.text: Replace with a clone creates a separately editable copy of a shared step/group. Cloning a group does not automatically detach nested shared steps: they remain shared. Saved changes create revisions; reverting shared content can affect other instances.

entries.moduleTitle: How to edit tests in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Reusable editing: groups and Shared Steps

entries.moduleTitle: How to edit tests in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Groups
entries.text: Steps can be grouped together, and groups can be nested inside other groups. A group is identified in the test by a folder icon in its upper-left corner.

entries.moduleTitle: How to edit tests in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Shared Steps / Shared Group
entries.text: Shared groups enable cross-test reuse within a project. Edits to shared definitions affect their references; review affected tests and distinguish instance-specific properties from shared ones.

entries.moduleTitle: How to edit tests in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Shared Steps Library
entries.text: A dedicated library view listing every shared step, group, and folder in the project, with four columns: Name, Date Modified, Kind (shared step / group / folder, plus the underlying step type), and Used by (a clickable count of how many tests reference that item — clicking it navigates to the Test Library filtered to just those tests). The library can be filtered by category: Groups, Actions, Validations, and Wait for.

entries.moduleTitle: How to edit tests in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Labels
entries.text: A lightweight organizational tool applied to tests in the Test Library, letting you categorize and quickly find tests without moving them between folders. A test can carry multiple labels at once (e.g. 'smoke', 'checkout'), and the library can be filtered or searched by label — useful once a project's test count grows past what folders alone can keep navigable. (Covered in more depth, alongside folders and dependencies, in the 'Advanced test management' module.)

entries.moduleTitle: Advanced test customization in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Advanced test customization in Tricentis Testim
entries.text: Conditions (Tricentis docs) · Advanced Conditions Settings (Tricentis docs) · Parameters (Tricentis docs) · Wait for (Tricentis docs) · Search Within a Test (Tricentis docs) · Recovering a test that was not saved (Tricentis docs) · Parameters for groups (Tricentis docs) · Generating a random value (Tricentis docs) · Generating a date (Tricentis docs)

entries.moduleTitle: Advanced test customization in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Conditions: running steps only when it makes sense

entries.moduleTitle: Advanced test customization in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Conditions
entries.text: Conditions can be applied to a step (run it or not) or to a loop (repeat it or not). If a condition is false, the default behavior is to skip the step immediately or end the loop immediately; if true, the step executes or the loop repeats immediately.

entries.moduleTitle: Advanced test customization in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Condition types
entries.text: Element conditions use visibility; Element text checks the selected target’s text; Custom permits JavaScript logic. Always Run and Never (skip) are additional execution choices. A condition gates execution, not an assertion that a business outcome occurred.

entries.moduleTitle: Advanced test customization in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Advanced condition settings — retry
entries.text: By default, a false condition immediately skips the step (or ends the loop). The 'retry' setting changes this: you specify a period in milliseconds during which Testim keeps re-checking the condition before giving up and moving on — useful for conditions tied to asynchronous UI states that need a moment to resolve.

entries.moduleTitle: Advanced test customization in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Setting a Custom condition on a step
entries.text: To attach a Custom (JavaScript) condition to a step or shared step: open the step, click the gear icon to open its Properties, find 'When to run step' (or 'When to run this step'), and select Custom — this opens the field where the JavaScript condition expression is written.

entries.moduleTitle: Advanced test customization in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Parameters: variable data instead of hardcoded values

entries.moduleTitle: Advanced test customization in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Parameters
entries.text: A parameter is a variable that can be used to pass information into a test step, letting the same step or group work with different data without needing separate, near-duplicate steps for each scenario.

entries.moduleTitle: Advanced test customization in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Parameters on groups
entries.text: Groups can define their own parameters. If a group is shared across multiple tests, those parameters remain available to every calling test — each test just sets its own values for the parameters rather than duplicating the group's underlying steps.

entries.moduleTitle: Advanced test customization in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Generating dynamic test data: random values and dates

entries.moduleTitle: Advanced test customization in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Generate random value
entries.text: Add Generate random value through predefined Actions. Configure character type, random length and optional prefix/suffix, then reference the stored variable in a later input. Randomness does not guarantee uniqueness; verify collision handling when uniqueness is required.

entries.moduleTitle: Advanced test customization in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Generate date
entries.text: Add Generate date through predefined Actions. Configure the date format (default YYYY-MM-DD), signed offset and browser time or UTC. Match the application’s actual clock, timezone and required calendar semantics.

entries.moduleTitle: Advanced test customization in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Finding your way around: search and draft recovery

entries.moduleTitle: Advanced test customization in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Search within a test
entries.text: Within-test search is case-insensitive and requires at least three characters. It searches descriptions, code, parameters, supported URLs, data and conditions, but not every property. Documented exclusions include Sleep duration, Extract variable name and generated-value settings other than descriptions.

entries.moduleTitle: Advanced test customization in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Recovering an unsaved test
entries.text: Testim stores a local recovery draft every 30 seconds. Recover restores the last available cached draft, so edits after that snapshot may be missing; cleared/unavailable cache cannot be treated as durable backup. Dismiss opens the last saved test. Save deliberately after recovery.

entries.moduleTitle: Advanced test customization in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Wait For: condition-based waiting instead of fixed delays

entries.moduleTitle: Advanced test customization in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Wait For step
entries.text: Condition-based waits retry until the required state is detected or the step timeout is reached. A condition that never becomes true must not hang indefinitely. Select a timeout and failure handling for the scenario.

entries.moduleTitle: Mastering advanced editing techniques in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Mastering advanced editing techniques in Tricentis Testim
entries.text: Keyboard Shortcut Step (Tricentis docs) · Parameter override rules (Tricentis docs) · Extract Value Step (Tricentis docs) · Wait for (Tricentis docs) · Editing target element properties (Tricentis docs) · Editing a steps properties (Tricentis docs)

entries.moduleTitle: Mastering advanced editing techniques in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Keyboard Shortcut steps

entries.moduleTitle: Mastering advanced editing techniques in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Add Keyboard Shortcut step
entries.text: Add Keyboard Shortcut sends a supported combination to the AUT. Windows/Mac fields synchronize equivalent shortcuts by default; Unsync Fields permits separate combinations. Inspect the effective test configuration OS rather than assuming the host OS always wins.

entries.moduleTitle: Mastering advanced editing techniques in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Setting the shortcut in Properties
entries.text: In Properties, press the combination in the applicable Windows or Mac field. The opposite field receives the default translation; use Unsync Fields when the intended combinations differ. A conflicting test-configuration OS governs which command is sent.

entries.moduleTitle: Mastering advanced editing techniques in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Unsupported combinations
entries.text: Unsupported combinations produce an unsupported keyboard shortcut error. Inspect failure handling rather than inferring that the entire test must always stop or always continue.

entries.moduleTitle: Mastering advanced editing techniques in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Parameters: flexible test step customization

entries.moduleTitle: Mastering advanced editing techniques in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Why parameterize
entries.text: Parameters let a step or group be customized per use — passing in different information without knowing every value in advance — so the same underlying steps serve multiple scenarios instead of being copy-pasted with small edits each time.

entries.moduleTitle: Mastering advanced editing techniques in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Parameter override rules
entries.text: Before execution, config-file values override params-file values, which override default test/run data; beforeTest overrides beforeSuite within the config file. During execution, scope and later assignments matter: a more local same-name parameter can shadow a broader one. This is not a universal parameters-always-win rule.

entries.moduleTitle: Mastering advanced editing techniques in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Extract Value: capturing data for later steps

entries.moduleTitle: Mastering advanced editing techniques in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Extract Value step
entries.text: Extract Value captures selected AUT element text. Extract Mode chooses the whole text or number/date/Regex matches; individual matches remain strings and all-matches modes can return arrays. Selecting a mode does not guarantee a JavaScript number/date type.

entries.moduleTitle: Mastering advanced editing techniques in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Wait for Events: synchronizing tests with the application

entries.moduleTitle: Mastering advanced editing techniques in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Waiting for an event, not a fixed time
entries.text: Use the supported wait for readiness such as element visibility, text or a completed download, with a bounded step timeout. Wait for Download uses the documented scripted completion check; adding the step alone does not configure every possible file condition.

entries.moduleTitle: Mastering advanced editing techniques in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Wait for element visible / not visible
entries.text: Visible waiting is available for web and mobile; documented not-visible waiting is web-only. Prepare the relevant AUT state before targeting. Visibility is not merely DOM presence, and absence from view does not necessarily mean removal.

entries.moduleTitle: Mastering advanced editing techniques in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Changing the element after the fact
entries.text: Use Reassign when the required target is different. If the same element still exists with changed identification, consider Improve. Validate the wait condition and timeout; extending time alone does not fix a wrong target.

entries.moduleTitle: Optimizing Test Execution in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Running multiple tests locally and on a schedule

entries.moduleTitle: Optimizing Test Execution in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Run multiple tests locally
entries.text: From Test List > Tests, selecting several tests and running them takes control of your mouse and runs the selected tests sequentially in your local Chrome browser (local runs are Chrome-only). Because Testim is actively driving the browser, you should not use your mouse or computer while the tests run. Locally-run tests are tracked and viewable afterward under Runs > Executions, tagged 'local-suite'.

entries.moduleTitle: Optimizing Test Execution in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Scheduler
entries.text: Scheduler runs selected labels, suites or test plans on a schedule, with applicable grid, branch and configuration. It can coexist with CI. Test plans supply their own grid/base URL/configuration, so those overrides are not available in the scheduler. Clone a schedule and review the copied settings.

entries.moduleTitle: Optimizing Test Execution in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Incognito mode and the Configuration File

entries.moduleTitle: Optimizing Test Execution in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Incognito mode (Testim IO)
entries.text: Incognito isolates browser cookies, login state and autocomplete from ordinary sessions. Enable the Testim extension in Incognito before local use. It does not reset backend data or guarantee an entirely fresh application/account state.

entries.moduleTitle: Optimizing Test Execution in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Configuration File with the CLI
entries.text: A CLI configuration file supplies execution options, parameters and hooks; it is not automatic encryption. Use supported Secrets Manager references instead of literal credentials. Static JSON params files need the documented JavaScript/module.exports conversion for secret references. Screenshot masking applies only to password-type fields, so review artifacts separately.

entries.moduleTitle: Optimizing Test Execution in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Timeouts and retries

entries.moduleTitle: Optimizing Test Execution in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Test timeout
entries.text: CLI --timeout uses milliseconds; Scheduler Test timeout uses seconds. Both document a 10-minute default and three-hour maximum. Do not confuse this test limit with the execution-list status that can temporarily become Timeout after 90 minutes while grid work continues.

entries.moduleTitle: Optimizing Test Execution in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Timeout retry
entries.text: CLI documentation describes timeout-specific retries up to three times and --disable-timeout-retry. Scheduler documentation describes one extra timeout run and its disable toggle. Check the actual execution path/version rather than promising one universal retry count.

entries.moduleTitle: Optimizing Test Execution in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Failed-test retries
entries.text: General failed-test retries use their configured maximum and stop on success. They are separate from timeout retries; passing after retry is evidence to investigate, not proof the original defect or instability is fixed.

entries.moduleTitle: Optimizing Test Execution in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Diagnosing a failure and reading the Execution Runs view

entries.moduleTitle: Optimizing Test Execution in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Diagnosing why a test failed
entries.text: For visual symptoms, compare available baseline and result screenshots alongside the failed step, error and environment. Screenshots do not establish every network, credential or backend cause; gather relevant evidence before changing configuration.

entries.moduleTitle: Optimizing Test Execution in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Execution Runs view
entries.text: The execution list shows duration, parallel test concurrency and results. Its graph plots execution count over time, not duration. Execution details include source/version/grid/data evidence; the details’ concurrent-executions count is distinct from the list’s parallel-test count.

entries.moduleTitle: Optimizing Test Execution in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: The Test Runs view: statistics across past runs

entries.moduleTitle: Optimizing Test Execution in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Test Runs / Test statistics
entries.text: The Test Runs screen shows statistics on past runs — aggregated across all selected tests, and per-test (e.g. how many times a specific test passed/failed and its average test duration) — under the Test statistics section. Filters (status, time, execution/label) narrow what's shown, and clicking a specific run opens it in the Test Editor to drill into per-step screenshots and durations.

entries.moduleTitle: Optimizing Test Execution in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Counted runs vs. Local Editor Runs
entries.text: Test Runs separates Counted Runs from Local Editor Runs. Under the documented test-runs subscription model, local editor runs are exempt; local library/CLI executions and remote grid runs are counted. A remote grid run launched from the editor must not be treated as quota-free solely because the editor triggered it.

entries.moduleTitle: Advanced test management in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Test Library: folders, labels, and test status

entries.moduleTitle: Advanced test management in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Folders and labels
entries.text: Folders (create via + → New Folder) give tests a single-location home in the Test Library. Labels are applied/removed via Edit Labels (or right-click → Edit Labels) and, unlike folders, a test can carry several at once — better suited to cross-cutting groupings like 'smoke' or 'checkout'. Search the library with label:<name> to filter by a label.

entries.moduleTitle: Advanced test management in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Test status
entries.text: The documented lifecycle statuses are Draft, Active, Evaluating and Quarantine; Failed is a run result. The status feature is professional-plan functionality and documents CLI 3.135.0 or later. At feature enablement, tests run within the preceding 30 days are identified as Active; this does not promise perpetual rolling automatic promotion. Evaluating failures do not fail CI/Scheduler; quarantined tests normally do not run, with an explicit CLI bypass available.

entries.moduleTitle: Advanced test management in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Shared Steps Library and Revisions

entries.moduleTitle: Advanced test management in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Filtering the Shared Steps Library
entries.text: Clicking Advanced filters opens the Filter Shared Steps pane, letting you filter by step category (Groups, Actions, Validations, Wait for) — the same filtering pattern used elsewhere in Testim's library views, including surfacing steps that are otherwise hidden from the default view so they can be selected and unhidden.

entries.moduleTitle: Advanced test management in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Revisions
entries.text: Saving a changed test stores the previous version as a revision with author/date and an optional message. Reverting shared content can affect other instances; inspect the shared references before restoring. A save with no change is not a promise of a new revision.

entries.moduleTitle: Advanced test management in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Test Plans and Test Suites

entries.moduleTitle: Advanced test management in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Test Plans - Web
entries.text: A web plan selects labels/suites, optional Before All/After All tests and run configuration. Before/after phases use parallel level 1; a failing Before All stops the main list. After All is documented to run when main-list tests fail, but that does not certify successful cleanup after every abort/infrastructure failure. CI invokes the plan through the supported CLI workflow.

entries.moduleTitle: Advanced test management in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Test Suites
entries.text: Suites collect tests and set an intended order. Parallel execution does not guarantee that order. CLI/Scheduler can run suites; suite creation alone does not provision a CI pipeline or delete unused tests.

entries.moduleTitle: Advanced test management in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Locators: Auto Improve and Smart Locator confidence

entries.moduleTitle: Advanced test management in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Locators: Auto Improve
entries.text: The documentation describes an Auto Improve attempt below 70% locator score, with replacement and a revision after successful improvement. It applies automatically to writable master, can be enabled on read-only master, and does not run on other branches. Manual locator editing disables future Auto Improve for that locator. An attempt is not guaranteed repair or outcome correctness.

entries.moduleTitle: Advanced test management in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Smart Locator confidence and changed attributes
entries.text: Changed attributes may reduce confidence while other weighted attributes still permit matching. A documented page-change warning is associated with a variation greater than 20% from the recorded confidence. Verify the actual target and asserted result; confidence alone does not establish correctness.

entries.moduleTitle: Advanced test management in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Bug Reporting with the Testim Extension

entries.moduleTitle: Advanced test management in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Capture Video & Bug Scenario
entries.text: The Chrome extension offers Capture Video & Bug Scenario with screen recording and per-step screenshots. Publishing requires a connected tracker. Bug Reporting also supports reporting a tagged test failure; not all reporting requires a new video capture.

entries.title: Validating Test Steps in Testim
entries.text: Validate CSS property (Tricentis docs) · Validating using custom code (Tricentis docs) · Extract Value Step (Tricentis docs) · Custom code (Tricentis docs) · Add cli validations and actions (Tricentis docs) · Index (Tricentis docs) · Index (Tricentis docs)

entries.title: Validate CSS property
entries.text: Checks any CSS property of an element. Property name takes a valid CSS property for the selected element (e.g. color, display, font-weight); Expected value is what that property should equal. The expected value can be a hardcoded literal (wrapped in quotes, e.g. 'red') or a parameter (entered by name, without quotes) — the same pattern used across other validation types.

entries.title: Editing after creation
entries.text: The property name and/or expected value can be changed later without re-selecting the element. If the element itself needs to change, hover the target element thumbnail and click Reassign, then click the new element in the AUT window — the same Reassign mechanism used on any other step.

entries.title: Data-driven validation in a real flow
entries.text: Independent signup example: assert the required heading and resulting registered account using supported text/visibility/custom checks. Add intermediate assertions where they establish meaningful requirements or help diagnosis; asserting every typed value is not a universal Testim requirement. Generating a string does not create a working email inbox or prove a password was accepted.

entries.title: Custom validations for actions beyond the predefined menu
Custom validations and custom actions
entries.text: Browser custom steps can inspect DOM/HTML parameters. Node.js CLI steps are a separate execution path with their own runtime and supported package setup; local execution requires the connected Testim CLI and documented entitlement.

entries.title: Pass/fail contract for custom validations
entries.text: For a synchronous browser custom validation, return an explicit boolean. False or a thrown error can fail the check; timeout and failure handling also matter. Supported asynchronous examples return a Promise that resolves/rejects. The final synchronous true/false value is not the entire contract for every custom or CLI step.

entries.title: Extracting a user-defined value for custom checks
entries.text: Extract selected AUT text into a variable and reference it in a supported later validation or custom-code scope. Numeric/date matches can remain strings and require deliberate conversion; not every field accepts parameter references.

entries.title: Reading the step's status
entries.text: After a run, a passed validation step shows its icon (upper-left corner of the step) in green, with a confirming message in the Properties panel. A failed validation step shows that same icon in red, with a failure message in the Properties panel — the same visual pattern applies to custom validation steps as to any predefined validation.

entries.title: Performing Data-driven Testing using Excel Files
entries.text: Data-driven testing (Tricentis docs) · Configuring a data driven test from the visual editor (Tricentis docs) · Passing parameters from excel file (Tricentis docs) · Configuring data driven tests using data from an external source (Tricentis docs) · Json parameters file parameters (Tricentis docs) · Reusable test data (Tricentis docs)

entries.moduleTitle: Performing Data-driven Testing using Excel Files
entries.title: Uploading and structuring test data

entries.moduleTitle: Performing Data-driven Testing using Excel Files
entries.title: Supported formats and limits
entries.text: The Setup-step Excel/CSV workflow uses the first row for parameter names, then subsequent data rows for individual data sets, with a documented 1200-row limit. Test data must fit the documented 2 MB limit. The separate reusable Test Data library supports CSV, JSON and Excel; do not conflate that resource workflow with embedded Setup data.

entries.moduleTitle: Performing Data-driven Testing using Excel Files
entries.title: Multiple ordered data sets
entries.text: A single file can define multiple ordered data sets, letting one test run repeatedly against a whole matrix of input combinations instead of a single hardcoded scenario.

entries.moduleTitle: Performing Data-driven Testing using Excel Files
entries.title: Config File vs. Params File for data-driven CLI runs

entries.moduleTitle: Performing Data-driven Testing using Excel Files
entries.title: Config File overrides
entries.text: A Config File can override the Visual Editor's test data at either the execution level or a specific test level (via overrideTestData) — and it's also how an external data source (like a linked CSV file, or a database) is supplied instead of an uploaded file.

entries.moduleTitle: Performing Data-driven Testing using Excel Files
entries.title: Params File
entries.text: A params file supplies execution-wide parameter values. JSON is supported; current documentation also supports JavaScript/module.exports. Config hooks with overrideTestData can target named tests. Verify precedence, including the separate reusable-file Prioritize test data option, instead of assuming every source always overrides every other.

entries.moduleTitle: Performing Data-driven Testing using Excel Files
entries.title: Where the multiple data sets actually run

entries.moduleTitle: Performing Data-driven Testing using Excel Files
entries.title: Editor run vs. CLI/Scheduler run
entries.text: For the documented embedded Setup data workflow, ordinary editor playback runs the first data set. CLI, Scheduler or local suite execution can run the ordered data sets; inspect each data-set result. This is scoped to that workflow, not certification that every newer reusable-file option has identical playback behavior.

entries.moduleTitle: Using loops for multiple validations in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Using loops for multiple validations in Tricentis Testim
entries.text: Repeat Group Loops (Tricentis docs) · Advanced conditions settings (Tricentis docs) · Index (Tricentis docs)

entries.moduleTitle: Using loops for multiple validations in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Loops in Testim: six repeat-group types

entries.moduleTitle: Using loops for multiple validations in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Where a loop lives
entries.text: Repeat group configures a group’s repetition; Don’t repeat is the default. Execution conditions and failures can still skip or stop work. The documented maximum is 99 iterations for any loop type, not only fixed-count loops.

entries.moduleTitle: Using loops for multiple validations in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: For each item, in depth

entries.moduleTitle: Using loops for multiple validations in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: 'For each item' loop
entries.text: For each item applies grouped actions to similar matched elements, within the configured item count (maximum 99). Verify actual matched items, iteration results and any paging/virtualization; a loop does not guarantee every record in an arbitrarily large table was visited.

entries.moduleTitle: Using loops for multiple validations in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: TESTIM_ITERATOR
entries.text: TESTIM_ITERATOR is available within group loops and increments with iterations. It is not a general test-wide parameter outside that scope; use it only where loop parameters are supported.

entries.moduleTitle: Using loops for multiple validations in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Condition-based and fixed-count loops

entries.moduleTitle: Using loops for multiple validations in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: While element / While element text is
entries.text: While element tests Visible/Not visible; While element text is tests the target’s expected text. Visibility and DOM existence are not interchangeable. Condition timing can be configured; neither loop is unlimited.

entries.moduleTitle: Using loops for multiple validations in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Loop for
entries.text: Runs the group a fixed number of times — either a literal number typed in directly, or a parameter holding a number, capped at a maximum of 99. Unlike For each item, this doesn't depend on matching elements on the page at all; it's a pure iteration count.

entries.moduleTitle: Using loops for multiple validations in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Custom
entries.text: For loop conditions that don't fit any of the built-in types, Custom lets you define the condition as a JavaScript function — with optional JS/HTML parameters passed in, and its own timeout override separate from the test's general settings.

entries.title: Extracting SMS messages using email service in Tricentis Testim
entries.text: Validate email (Tricentis docs) · Extract Value Step (Tricentis docs) · Extract sms message (Tricentis docs) · Add cli validations and actions (Tricentis docs)

entries.moduleTitle: Extracting SMS messages using email service in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: What Testim's email service is

entries.moduleTitle: Extracting SMS messages using email service in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Testim's own email service
entries.text: Testim’s managed email feature creates permanent inbox addresses in Settings > Email Service or temporary addresses through Generate email address. Third-party providers are not used to generate these managed addresses; that is not a ban on all external-service integrations.

entries.moduleTitle: Extracting SMS messages using email service in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Email validation and exports
entries.text: Validate email reads managed-inbox messages for coded checks or codeless filters. The codeless mode can extract text/links and exposes emailData, emailExtractedText and emailExtractedLinks. Generic DOM Extract Value is not required to read that inbox.

entries.moduleTitle: Extracting SMS messages using email service in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Email and SMS are separate retrieval paths

entries.moduleTitle: Extracting SMS messages using email service in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Direct email flows
entries.text: Use the managed inbox for supported email flows. Match the intended message and required outcome rather than assuming any message proves the current request succeeded.

entries.moduleTitle: Extracting SMS messages using email service in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Direct SMS retrieval
entries.text: The official Extract SMS message example uses a CLI action with Twilio, sender/recipient filters, recent-message checks and a returned Promise. It exports the code from the selected message. This is an SMS-provider path, not the managed email inbox.

entries.moduleTitle: Extracting SMS messages using email service in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Selecting and reusing the required message value

entries.moduleTitle: Extracting SMS messages using email service in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: The extraction pattern
entries.text: Filter for the intended message, verify required content and export the code/link with supported scope. Extracting one value does not replace message assertions or prove phone delivery. Avoid assuming the first old mailbox message belongs to the current test.

entries.moduleTitle: Extracting SMS messages using email service in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Choosing permanent vs. temporary for this scenario
entries.text: Use a reusable permanent inbox or per-run temporary inbox according to the email scenario. A fresh inbox does not create a fresh phone number or guarantee a newly registered backend account.

entries.title: CLI actions vs. custom (browser) actions

entries.moduleTitle: Generating coded test steps with CLI actions in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: CLI actions and validations
entries.text: CLI actions/validations execute Node.js in the connected CLI environment; browser custom actions execute in the browser. Node.js can use configured packages and authorized resources, but network access, credentials and dependencies still need setup.

entries.title: Copilot assistance for supported coded steps

entries.title: Generate a draft, then insert and test it
entries.text: The Coding Assistant documentation explicitly lists Add CLI Validation among supported steps. Open Write code with AI, acknowledge the notice and request code. Use Paste code at cursor or Copy code to insert it; appearing in chat does not automatically install the implementation.

entries.title: Generating custom steps with generative AI

entries.title: Testim Copilot
entries.text: Copilot proposes JavaScript for supported coded steps from prompts. The response is a draft, not a guarantee of a working or correct test; review the intended action or assertion and runtime.

entries.moduleTitle: Creating custom action steps with Copilot in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Using the Coding Assistant
entries.text: Open Write code with AI on a supported step and acknowledge the notice. Slash commands include Generate, Explain, Fix and Help. Generated or fixed code appears in chat; Paste code at cursor or Copy code inserts it deliberately.

entries.title: Duplication levels: scoring how much repetition exists

entries.moduleTitle: How to Auto group Test Steps in Testim
entries.title: The duplication score
entries.text: The duplication score is a 0–100 estimate of ungrouped repeated sequences on master, refreshed by weekly offline processing rather than every edit. Auto grouping is documented for professional-plan web/mobile-web projects, not native mobile projects.

entries.title: Performing API testing in Tricentis Testim
entries.text: API testing (Tricentis docs)

entries.moduleTitle: Performing API testing in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Two types of API steps: Add API Action vs. Validate API

entries.moduleTitle: Performing API testing in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Add API Action
entries.text: Used to get data returned from an API call — the data it retrieves can simply be used to check that something was returned (or extracted and used later), rather than asserting a specific value on the spot.

entries.moduleTitle: Performing API testing in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Validate API
entries.text: Used to validate data returned from an API call — usually validating data directly against the backend, asserting the response matches an expected value rather than just retrieving it.

entries.moduleTitle: Performing API testing in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Configuring an API step

entries.moduleTitle: Performing API testing in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Adding an API validation step
entries.text: Hover over the arrow where the step should go, click the predefined-steps icon ('M'), then choose Validations to add an API validation step to a test.

entries.moduleTitle: Performing API testing in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: URL and request method
entries.text: Choose HTTP method and endpoint, then configure headers, authorization, body and assertions. Named Basic/Bearer authorization overrides manually entered authorization headers. A configured assertion runs before additional response code; failed assertions prevent that code from running.

entries.moduleTitle: Performing API testing in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Validating API responses against the UI
entries.text: Use supported assertions or additional code to compare response data and UI values. A quick Send preview does not execute assertions/additional code; only static local parameters are supplied and dynamic values become empty strings. Request retries apply to failed request status, separately from assertion behavior.

entries.moduleTitle: Performing API testing in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Send via web page

entries.moduleTitle: Performing API testing in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Send via web page (checked = default)
entries.text: Browser-context sending includes browser session information such as cookies where applicable. Verify effective authentication, cookie policy and page readiness; selecting this setting does not guarantee every request is authenticated.

entries.moduleTitle: Performing API testing in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Send via web page (unchecked)
entries.text: Outside-browser sending avoids browser CORS restrictions. It does not bypass server authorization, network access or all failure causes; configure the required authentication separately.

entries.text: Hooks (Tricentis docs) · Configuration File - Hooks (Tricentis docs)

entries.moduleTitle: How to use Hooks in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Hooks: running a shared step/group before or after something

entries.moduleTitle: How to use Hooks in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Hook
entries.text: Test Configuration hooks call an existing shared step/group at configured step/test boundaries. Create or edit the configuration and apply it to the relevant tests; creating a configuration alone does not attach it to every test.

entries.moduleTitle: How to use Hooks in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Before each step / After each step
entries.text: Per-step handlers attach before/after steps. After handlers have Run on choices (Always, Success, Failure), so they are not unconditional in every configuration. Hooks can still run around a step skipped by its own condition; distinguish that condition from the hook’s Run on selection.

entries.moduleTitle: How to use Hooks in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Configuration File run hooks
entries.text: A separate, CLI/config-level mechanism: the Configuration File can define run hooks used to set up the application backend and define parameters before/after a single test or before/after all tests in a run — useful for environment-level setup/teardown that isn't tied to any one specific step.

entries.title: When to recognize a hook is the right tool

entries.moduleTitle: Managing and analyzing test results in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Debugging tests during runtime

entries.moduleTitle: Managing and analyzing test results in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Stop, Pause, Step
entries.text: Local debug mode supports Pause/Continue, stepping and breakpoints. Pause stops at the nearest step boundary, not an arbitrary instant inside any action. Local playback without debugging does not pause at breakpoints; remote grid execution is not this local debug mode.

entries.moduleTitle: Managing and analyzing test results in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Resuming from a breakpoint
entries.text: Continue/Play resumes a paused run from the current location, unlike Rerun, which restarts. Distinguish manual breakpoints from temporary virtual debug locations rather than promising every breakpoint marker remains unchanged.

entries.moduleTitle: Managing and analyzing test results in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Running from a specific step
entries.text: Play from here starts after the selected arrow. Establish earlier required state, such as authentication and variables; skipping setup can cause failure. This is partial debugging, not full-flow coverage.

entries.moduleTitle: Managing and analyzing test results in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Organizing and filtering with Result labels

entries.moduleTitle: Managing and analyzing test results in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Result labels
entries.text: Free-text labels attached to a run — distinct from the Labels applied to tests in the Test Library. Result labels are commonly used to record things like which application environment was tested, which application version was tested, or which user/system executed the run (examples: 'nightly-scheduler', 'v1.42.34', 'Jenkins', 'Staging').

entries.moduleTitle: Managing and analyzing test results in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Adding and filtering by result labels
entries.text: Add remote-run result labels with CLI --result-label or Scheduler Advanced Options. Each label has a 250-character maximum. Run pages support filtering; test-definition Labels are a separate selection/organization mechanism.

entries.moduleTitle: Managing and analyzing test results in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Tagging failed runs with failure types

entries.moduleTitle: Managing and analyzing test results in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Tagging a failure
entries.text: Tag remote-run failures using the documented categories: Bug in app, Environment issue, Invalid test data, Test design or Other. These human-selected cause categories are distinct from engine errors such as Element not found or JavaScript Error.

entries.moduleTitle: Managing and analyzing test results in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Why tag failures
entries.text: Once failures are tagged, the failure-type filter can show only the runs tagged with a specific reason, and the Reports view's donut chart shows the percentage distribution of failure types (each tag's share of total runs, alongside its change vs. the previous period) — turning individual failures into a trend you can act on. Clicking a failure tag jumps straight to the Test Runs screen, pre-filtered to every run tagged with that type.

entries.text: Use a supported Node.js LTS/runtime and install the npm CLI package. The documented global workflow is npm install -g @testim/testim-cli followed by testim connect; a local package install needs the applicable local launcher rather than assuming a global testim command appears.

entries.title: Why use the CLI at all
entries.text: CLI supports configured test selection, grids, parallelism, data sets and CI invocation. It is not the sole mechanism for all non-local execution: the editor can run a single grid test and Scheduler can trigger configured matrices.

entries.moduleTitle: Leveraging the Command Line Interface (CLI) in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Configuration file
entries.text: A config file (e.g. testimConfig.js) is created and passed to the CLI runner as a parameter, pointing to its path if needed. It can define the project ID, token, labels selecting which tests to run, the Selenium grid to use, and base URL overrides.

entries.title: Running on multiple browsers
entries.text: Use CLI/Scheduler with supported browser/OS configurations for a cross-browser matrix. The editor also supports a single grid test. Supported combinations depend on the grid; selecting desktop browser configurations is not evidence of physical-device or native-mobile coverage.

entries.title: Grid configuration via CLI
entries.text: --grid selects the configured grid by name. --test-config selects browser/OS/resolution or other test configuration overrides; these flags have different roles. Verify both target infrastructure and the supported browser configuration.

entries.moduleTitle: Exporting test lists and results in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Exporting to CSV
entries.text: CSV exports apply the chosen view/filter scope. Execution Runs exports executions; Test Runs exports individual runs (CSV is documented only for Counted Runs); Test Library exports test metadata, not the same result table. For Test Runs, the visible 200-result default does not truncate the matching CSV results. The export guide documents professional-plan entitlement.

entries.title: Exporting to PDF
entries.text: The result editor’s three-dot menu offers Generate PDF run report. Share it as a report of the selected run, not proof of complete requirement/code coverage or all project tests. The export does not execute or edit tests.

entries.text: CI can invoke the npm-based Testim CLI when its runner has a supported Node.js environment, configured credentials/project/grid and required network access. Shell capability alone does not guarantee a working integration.

entries.text: Settings > CLI > CI provides a platform-specific starting command. Adapt it to the runner and actual selection/configuration; configure safe credential handling and a JUnit report path that the CI collector also reads.

entries.moduleTitle: Integrating Tricentis Testim with Continuous Integration (CI) Tools
entries.title: Monitoring CI runs from Testim
entries.text: Inspect the applicable test/execution result and time-filtered history. Correlate them with the actual CI build; a chart or copied command does not by itself prove the pipeline completed or identify every failure cause.

entries.text: Map a Testim test from Setup properties to one or multiple TTM test cases. Bulk create-and-map skips tests already mapped and reports failures for retry. Only one TMS connection is supported at a time; disconnecting removes mappings.

entries.moduleTitle: Recording new steps to resolve bugs in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Adding steps to an existing test

entries.moduleTitle: Recording new steps to resolve bugs in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: When a test is missing steps
entries.text: After running a test with debugging, you may find it's lacking some steps, or that some steps are outdated and need re-recording. Rather than re-recording the whole test from scratch, you can add steps manually or record just the missing portion through the AUT.

entries.moduleTitle: Recording new steps to resolve bugs in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Inserting recorded steps at a position
entries.text: Hover over the arrow between two existing steps where the new steps should go, click Start recording at this position, then record the additional actions on the AUT window — the new steps are inserted exactly where the arrow was, not appended to the end.

entries.moduleTitle: Recording new steps to resolve bugs in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Start Recording vs. Start recording at this position
entries.text: Testim actually offers two distinct entry points: the plain 'Start Recording'/Record button (available while execution is stopped) appends new steps to the END of the test, while 'Start recording at this position' — triggered from the arrow between two steps — inserts steps at that exact mid-test point instead.

entries.moduleTitle: Recording new steps to resolve bugs in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Setting up the AUT state before recording mid-test
entries.text: Run to the insertion point with the required AUT state, then record the missing sequence and Stop recording. Review inserted actions and assertions, save and replay the full relevant flow; an insertion alone does not certify the defect is fixed.

entries.moduleTitle: Recording new steps to resolve bugs in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Combining recording with debugging

entries.moduleTitle: Recording new steps to resolve bugs in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Investigate before changing coverage
entries.text: Local breakpoints and stepping expose application state and failed-step evidence. They do not guarantee exact root-cause identification or consistent reproduction of every intermittent failure. Establish whether the missing behavior is in the test, application or environment before adding recorded actions.

entries.moduleTitle: Identifying CLI prerequisites in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: What the CLI needs to run

entries.moduleTitle: Identifying CLI prerequisites in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Node.js requirement
entries.text: Running Testim via the CLI requires Node.js to be installed on the machine — the CLI is itself an npm package and runs in the Node.js runtime.

entries.moduleTitle: Identifying CLI prerequisites in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Supported versions
entries.text: Testim supports all LTS (Long-Term Support) / supported versions of Node.js — not just one specific pinned version — giving teams flexibility in which supported Node.js release they standardize on.

entries.moduleTitle: Identifying CLI prerequisites in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Local vs. remote runs
entries.text: The CLI requires its installed package and supported Node.js on the initiating machine. Local/grid execution additionally needs its own browser/device infrastructure, credentials and connectivity; runtime prerequisites alone do not establish readiness.

entries.moduleTitle: Identifying CLI prerequisites in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: The Testim CLI package itself also has a version-support policy
entries.text: The CLI prerequisites table specifies latest CLI with backward compatibility for the previous two versions. It also lists a Node.js supported-runtime requirement with a previous-two compatibility comment. The table does not define those as previous major releases or guarantee end-of-life Node.js security/support.

entries.title: Debugging Helper Panels and JS Code Debugging

entries.moduleTitle: Debugging test cases in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Debug Helper panels
entries.text: Console Log filters messages and can preserve them between runs; Breakpoint Manager locates/removes breakpoints; Scope shows incoming parameters and test/global exports. Future, unexecuted steps have no runtime values to inspect.

entries.moduleTitle: Debugging test cases in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: JS Code Debugging
entries.text: For supported browser steps, pause before the step in a local debug run, use Step Into, switch to the AUT, open Chrome DevTools and follow the confirmation prompt. Inspect the code, resume its execution and return to the editor. Supported types include custom action/validation/wait, email/network validation and API action/validation; CLI actions are not listed for this browser workflow.

entries.moduleTitle: Debugging test cases in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Debugging Controls: pausing and stepping through a test

entries.moduleTitle: Debugging test cases in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Pause
entries.text: Pause stops at the nearest step boundary in local debug mode. Continue proceeds from the current location; another breakpoint can pause it again.

entries.moduleTitle: Debugging test cases in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Step-by-step execution
entries.text: Start a local run with debugging. Pause or insert a breakpoint, then use the available stepping controls. Step Over executes a step/group; Step Into opens a group before its first step; Step Out executes its remaining steps before leaving.

entries.moduleTitle: Debugging test cases in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Breakpoints: manual vs. virtual
entries.text: Breakpoints pause execution at various stages. Manual breakpoints are explicitly set by the user at a chosen step. Virtual breakpoints are created automatically by the system when debugging controls are used — such as step into, step out, step over, and pause — without the user having to set them by hand.

entries.title: The TestOps Dashboard: reading project health

entries.moduleTitle: Streamlining Testing and Debugging in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: TestOps Dashboard
entries.text: The Dashboard summarizes project activity with plan-dependent panes and selected branch context. It helps prioritize investigation; activity alone does not prove coverage.

entries.moduleTitle: Streamlining Testing and Debugging in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Duplication Level pane
entries.text: Duplication Level estimates redundant sequences that may benefit from shared groups. A lower duplication estimate does not certify overall project health.

entries.moduleTitle: Streamlining Testing and Debugging in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Recent Activity pane
entries.text: Recent Activity links project events. Assigned to me concerns owned tests; the remote pane changes from execution counts to owned-test runs, rather than filtering only actions performed by you.

entries.moduleTitle: Streamlining Testing and Debugging in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Turbo Mode: faster feedback

entries.moduleTitle: Streamlining Testing and Debugging in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: What Turbo Mode does
entries.text: Turbo Mode is a professional-plan feature. It ignores step delays and omits successful-run artifacts to reduce overhead. The vendor reports an average speed improvement, not a promised result for every test; browser crashes can prevent failed-run artifacts too.

entries.moduleTitle: Streamlining Testing and Debugging in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Enabling Turbo Mode
entries.text: Enable --turbo-mode for CLI runs or the Scheduler toggle. Execution is extension-based on Chrome or Edge Chromium; this is not a general mode for every browser or mobile device.

entries.moduleTitle: Streamlining Testing and Debugging in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Capturing a video for a bug scenario

entries.moduleTitle: Streamlining Testing and Debugging in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Prerequisite: the Testim Chrome Extension
entries.text: The Testim browser extension can capture webpage bugs independently of automated tests. Bug reports may include a screenshot, reproduction video, interaction screenshots and generated reproduction text.

entries.moduleTitle: Streamlining Testing and Debugging in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Publishing the capture
entries.text: Connect the relevant bug tracker before submitting a report. The accessible capture page is incomplete and does not establish that every extension video is stored in an associated test-run result: a standalone webpage capture may have no such run.

entries.moduleTitle: Streamlining Testing and Debugging in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Quarantine and CI/CD: what actually happens to a quarantined test

entries.moduleTitle: Streamlining Testing and Debugging in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Quarantined tests are skipped in CI/CD, not run
entries.text: A test marked Quarantine (unstable/flaky, generating errors) does NOT run as part of a normal CI/CD execution — it still appears in the suite run with a quarantine indication, and is recorded in the run's result XML with a 'Skipped' flag, rather than being executed.

entries.moduleTitle: Streamlining Testing and Debugging in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Why quarantine this way
entries.text: This lets a team quarantine a flaky/failing test without removing it from the CI/suite entirely — the test stays visible (so it's not forgotten), doesn't fail the overall build, and can be gradually re-added to real execution once fixed. A CLI override, --run-quarantined-tests, exists for the rare case where you deliberately want quarantined tests to run anyway.

entries.moduleTitle: Configuring and managing projects in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Generating base test code with the CLI

entries.moduleTitle: Configuring and managing projects in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Settings > CLI: CI vs. Local
entries.text: On the Settings > CLI page, clicking CI generates base code (containing your token and project ID) for running tests remotely on a CI platform; clicking Local generates the equivalent base code for running tests on your own machine (web only — this opens a local browser). Under CI, you can also pick a CI Platform and a Grid to further tailor the generated command.

entries.moduleTitle: Configuring and managing projects in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Using the generated code
entries.text: Whichever mode you pick, Testim generates a ready-to-run CLI command pre-filled with your token and project ID — click Copy to grab it for your shell or CI pipeline, rather than typing the whole command (and looking up the token/project ID) by hand every time.

entries.moduleTitle: Configuring and managing projects in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Managing project users and roles

entries.moduleTitle: Configuring and managing projects in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Project teammates
entries.text: The Project teammates screen (via the Users icon in the main navigation) lists everyone currently assigned to the project. Inviting is done by entering each teammate's work email (followed by space or Enter), then clicking Invite.

entries.moduleTitle: Configuring and managing projects in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Roles: member vs. owner
entries.text: Any team member can invite new project teammates. A project owner has broader authority: they can remove teammates and add/remove other project owners — a distinction worth knowing since 'can invite' and 'can remove/promote' are not the same permission level.

entries.moduleTitle: Configuring and managing projects in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Overseeing projects and users at the company level

entries.moduleTitle: Configuring and managing projects in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Tracking who worked on a project
entries.text: The Users section displays which user is associated with which particular project — that's the built-in, membership-level view. For tracking what other users have actually DONE on a project (their actions, not just their membership), the course expects you to integrate a separate project-management tool into Testim, via Testim's existing integrations such as TTM for Jira or Azure DevOps.

entries.moduleTitle: Configuring and managing projects in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Protecting branches: pull request settings

entries.moduleTitle: Configuring and managing projects in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Protect branches from changes
entries.text: A toggle in the project's pull request settings that prevents writing directly to the Master branch and/or other selected branches (making them read-only) — changes must go through a pull request instead of a direct commit.

entries.moduleTitle: Configuring and managing projects in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Related settings
entries.text: If Master is protected, 'Allow Auto-improve on master' can still be enabled so the Auto-improve locator feature keeps working even on a protected branch. 'Require approving reviewer' can be turned on per-branch to mandate a review before a pull request merges. Only the project owner or company owner can change these settings, and they're a professional-plan-only feature.

entries.moduleTitle: Using the REST API in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Enabling and authenticating API access

entries.moduleTitle: Using the REST API in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Plan restriction
entries.text: API access is a professional feature, available only to projects on the professional plan — it isn't something every project tier has access to by default.

entries.moduleTitle: Using the REST API in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Generating an API key
entries.text: Go to Settings → API, click Generate API Key, and name it. The key's value is shown once; you must copy it immediately and click Done, since that display is the only time the raw value is visible.

entries.moduleTitle: Using the REST API in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Authenticating requests
entries.text: The API key is used in the Authorization header as a Bearer token: Authorization: Bearer PAK-[your-api-key]. For calls involving encrypted credentials (e.g. POST /tests/run/{testId}), the user-access-key value is instead added to the X-User-Access-Key field.

entries.moduleTitle: Best practices for automating logins in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Best practices for automating logins in Tricentis Testim
entries.text: Best practices for handling logins (Tricentis docs)

entries.moduleTitle: Best practices for automating logins in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Reusable, parameterized login groups

entries.moduleTitle: Best practices for automating logins in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Grouping login steps
entries.text: Grouping login steps allows reuse of those steps across other tests — give the group a meaningful name so its purpose is clear to anyone browsing the project's groups later.

entries.moduleTitle: Best practices for automating logins in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Parameterizing credentials
entries.text: To make the group generic across different accounts, add JavaScript parameters for username and password in the group's properties panel. Every time the group is used, different credentials can be supplied without duplicating the underlying steps.

entries.moduleTitle: Best practices for automating logins in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Cleaning up recorded noise
entries.text: Steps recorded as a manual user — like pressing Tab to move between fields — often aren't relevant to the automated test and can simply be deleted, keeping the login group lean and focused on what actually matters.

entries.moduleTitle: Best practices for automating logins in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Handling browser/session state around login

entries.moduleTitle: Best practices for automating logins in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Incognito mode
entries.text: Running in incognito mode is useful specifically while building the login process: each run starts with a clean browser — no cookies, no local storage, nothing remembered — so the test reliably exercises the actual login flow instead of skipping it because a previous session is still active.

entries.moduleTitle: Best practices for automating logins in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Conditional login execution
entries.text: Adding a condition that checks, at runtime, whether login is actually needed (e.g. an element condition on whether a login button is visible) lets the same test work whether the session starts logged in or logged out — rather than assuming one state and breaking under the other.

entries.moduleTitle: Automating mobile tests in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Testim Mobile overview

entries.moduleTitle: Automating mobile tests in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Testim Mobile
entries.text: Extends Testim's AI-powered test automation — Smart Locators, visual validation, codeless authoring — specifically to mobile app testing, covering native apps, hybrid apps, and cross-platform frameworks.

entries.moduleTitle: Automating mobile tests in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Native app language support
entries.text: For Android devices, Testim supports Java or Kotlin native apps; for iOS devices, Objective-C or Swift. Recording works the same way as web — click through the app and Testim captures elements — building toward more stable tests as more application elements are found during recording.

entries.moduleTitle: Automating mobile tests in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Enhanced mode vs. Appium mode

entries.moduleTitle: Automating mobile tests in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Enhanced mode
entries.text: Testim's newer recording/execution mode, designed to be more stable, faster, and more versatile than Appium-based testing. It uses a zero-knowledge approach with a unified API supporting native, hybrid, or cross-platform apps alike. The trade-off: tests recorded in Enhanced mode can only be executed on VMG (Testim's own mobile grid).

entries.moduleTitle: Automating mobile tests in Tricentis Testim
entries.title: Appium mode
entries.text: Guarantees compatibility with other Appium-based grids and supports local execution on your own local devices. The trade-off runs the other way: it's restricted to Appium's own capabilities, meaning some flows — especially hybrid apps or webviews — may not be fully recordable.
